title: How to Play the Armenians
summary: Armenians get Long Swordsmen in the Feudal Age, cheap Mule Carts instead of camps and a free Relic in their first Fortified Church. This guide covers the Feudal infantry rush, the Warrior Priest fast castle and a late game built on Champions, Halberdiers and Composite Bowmen.
body:
## What the Armenians are good at

Armenians are a Barracks civilization first. The Long Swordsman upgrade and everything above it arrive one age early, and so do the Spearman line upgrades. You can train Spearmen in the Dark Age, research Long Swordsman and Pikeman in the Feudal Age, and have Two-Handed Swordsmen, Champions and Halberdiers in the Castle Age. Most opponents meet these units while their own Blacksmith and unit upgrades are still one age behind.

The economy runs on the Mule Cart, a moving drop site that replaces both the Lumber Camp and the Mining Camp. Armenian Mule Carts cost 25% less, so one costs 15 food and 60 wood, and the wood and mining upgrades are 40% more effective than usual. Double-Bit Axe and Bow Saw each give about 28% more wood instead of 20%. When a woodline thins out you drive the cart closer instead of building a new camp, and a cart parked between wood and gold lets you shift villagers between the two without long walks.

The Fortified Church replaces the Monastery. It fires arrows when villagers or Relics are inside, and the first one you build gets a free Relic, which means gold income from the moment it stands. It also trains the Warrior Priest, an infantry unit that fights in melee, heals nearby units, carries Relics and can only be converted with Atonement. The Castle trains the Composite Bowman, a foot archer whose arrows ignore armor, so it does full damage to targets that laugh at normal arrows.

The weak side is the Stable and the Siege Workshop. Armenians have no Paladin, no Hussar, no Plate Barding Armor, no Siege Onager, no Hand Cannoneer and no Bombard Cannon, and their archers miss Thumb Ring. Plan your games around infantry, Skirmishers, Composite Bowmen and the Fortified Church, and use Trebuchets to take down buildings late.

On water the Galley line and Dromons fire one extra projectile, and the Castle Age tech Cilician Fleet adds range to both, so Armenians are a strong pick on hybrid and water maps.

## Openings that suit them

The signature land opening is the Feudal Long Swordsman rush (see the build Armenian Feudal Long Swordsmen). You reach Feudal at about 21 population, research Man-at-Arms and then Long Swordsman, and arrive with units that beat Spearmen, Scouts and towers hand to hand. ColinAoC's version adds towers next to the opponent's resources, and St4rk shows follow-ups into Skirmishers or Archers when the rush alone will not end the game.

The second opening is a fast castle into Warrior Priests from a Fortified Church (see the build Fast Castle into Warrior Priests). It takes Relics early, heals your army and holds off early Castle Age Monks, since Warrior Priests cannot be converted before Atonement.

Against a scout rush you can make Spearmen before you click Feudal, which few civilizations can do. On Arena and closed maps a plain fast castle into Fortified Church, Relics and two extra Town Centers works well because the free Relic pays for itself.

## Castle Age plan

After a Feudal infantry opening, go up with your Barracks still working. Two-Handed Swordsman is available as soon as you land in Castle Age, so the Long Swordsmen that survived the Feudal fight upgrade straight away. Add Skirmishers against archers and Halberdiers against Knights, since both cost no or little gold and Armenian infantry already has the upgrades other civilizations wait for.

Build the Fortified Church early in the age to claim the free Relic, then use Warrior Priests or Monks to collect more. Warrior Priests are slow and cost 50 gold each, so keep them behind your army as healers and Relic carriers and let other units do most of the killing.

Make Composite Bowmen when the opponent goes for units with high pierce armor, such as Eagle Warriors or upgraded infantry. They also mix well with Champions against Knights, because the infantry holds the line while the archers shoot over it.

## Imperial Age plan

Research Fereters at the Castle. It gives infantry (except the Spearman line) 30 extra hit points and doubles Warrior Priest healing speed, which turns Champions into one of the sturdiest infantry units in the game. A typical late army is Champions and Halberdiers in front, Elite Skirmishers and Composite Bowmen behind, a few Warrior Priests healing and Trebuchets for Castles. Get Treadmill Crane and keep Mule Carts close to new gold and stone as the map runs out.

## Matchups

According to AoE2Insights, Armenians win just under half of their 1v1 random map games and do worst against Shu, Malians, Chinese, Ethiopians, Huns and Mongols. Two patterns stand out.

Fast cavalry and cavalry archer civilizations such as Huns and Mongols run around slow infantry and raid wherever the army is not. Wall early, keep Pikemen at home in the Feudal Age and lean on Skirmishers and Composite Bowmen, since your Stable stops at Cavalier without Plate Barding.

Strong archer play from Ethiopians or Chinese shreds Long Swordsmen in the open. Pair your infantry with Skirmishers or Mangonels, get armor at the Blacksmith and avoid walking into massed Crossbowmen with infantry alone. Malians are awkward because their Barracks units shrug off arrows, so swap to infantry against infantry and use your earlier upgrades to win those fights.

The civilization does best against slower infantry and Eagle civilizations such as Goths, Mapuche, Gurjaras and Slavs, where Long Swordsmen and Champions arrive first and with more upgrades.

## Common mistakes

- Massing Long Swordsmen into a crowd of archers. Infantry needs Skirmishers or siege next to it against ranged armies.
- Leaving Mule Carts at a depleted woodline. Move them every few minutes so villagers keep short walks.
- Building the Fortified Church late. The free Relic is gold you only collect once the church is up, so place it early in Castle Age.
- Treating Warrior Priests as a main army. They are expensive, slow and best used as healers and Relic carriers.
- Going for Knights in the late game. Without Paladin or Plate Barding Armor, your gold is better spent on Champions and Composite Bowmen.

title: How to Play the Aztecs
summary: Aztecs turn fast military production, a strong early economy and the toughest Monks in the game into constant pressure. This guide covers the Men-at-Arms and Militia openings, Eagle Warriors and Monks in the Castle Age, the Imperial Age army and the matchups to watch.
body:
The Aztecs are an infantry and Monk civilization with no Stable, so every plan runs through the Barracks, the Archery Range and the Monastery. Their bonuses point toward early aggression. They get 50 extra gold once the first Town Center stands, all military units train 15% faster, and villagers carry 3 more resources per trip, which speeds up farming and woodcutting for the whole game. A good Aztec player attacks early, keeps attacking, and uses the economy to stay ahead in production.

## What the Aztecs do well

- Early pressure. The extra gold pays for most of a Militia opening, and faster training gets your first units to the enemy sooner.
- Eagle Warriors. They cost 20 food and 50 gold, move fast, take little damage from arrows and come out quickly from several Barracks. They raid, kill archers, siege and Monks, and they are the core of most Aztec armies.
- Monks. Each Monastery technology adds 5 hit points to Aztec Monks, so a fully researched Monk has 100 hit points. Their team bonus also makes relics produce a third more gold.
- Infantry. Garland Wars gives all infantry +4 attack in the Imperial Age, so Champions and Elite Eagle Warriors hit very hard late.

The weak spots are just as clear. Without a Stable there are no Knights, Light Cavalry or Camels, and the Barracks stops at Pikeman, so heavy cavalry has to be handled with Pikemen, Monks and numbers. Archers miss Thumb Ring and Ring Archer Armor. Defenses are poor with no Keep and no Masonry, and the navy has no Galleon.

## Openings

The standard Arabia opening is Aztecs Men-at-Arms into Archers, written up as a build on this site. Three Militia come out at the end of the Dark Age, become Men-at-Arms the moment Feudal Age lands, and go after the enemy wood line while an Archery Range starts at home. Because of the starting gold you only need two gold miners in the Dark Age, which keeps more villagers on food and wood.

The other common opening is a Militia drush into a fast Castle Age. Three to five Militia hit the opponent, the villagers never stop, and you click up to Castle Age while the opponent repairs and rebuilds. TheViper made this version popular; it suits players who want to reach Eagles, Monks or a quick second Town Center early.

Your starting Eagle Scout is a little slower than Scout Cavalry, so plan your sheep search and boar lures with that in mind and do not take risky deer pushes.

## Castle Age plan

Most Aztec games turn into Eagle Warriors in the Castle Age. Build two to four Barracks, get Forging and Scale Mail Armor early, and keep the Eagles moving: hit villagers, kill Mangonels and Scorpions, chase Crossbowmen. Eagles are cheap in food and heavy in gold, so a Market is part of the plan. Sell extra food or wood, buy food when you have spare gold, and keep every Barracks working.

If you opened archers, Crossbowmen can stay in the mix while you add Eagles. Against heavy archer play, Skirmishers with Atlatl (+1 attack and +1 range) are a cheap answer that needs no gold.

A Monastery belongs in every Aztec Castle Age. Collect relics early, since each one is worth more for you than for other civilizations, and use Monks to convert Knights that your Pikemen cannot reach. The Jaguar Warrior from the Castle is the answer to enemy infantry such as Long Swordsmen, Huskarls or other Eagles; it gains attack with every kill, up to four.

For pushing, Aztecs have Capped Ram and later Siege Ram, plus Mangonels that become Siege Onagers. A few Rams behind Eagles break walls and Town Centers quickly.

## Imperial Age

In the Imperial Age, research Garland Wars and Elite Eagle Warrior, finish the infantry armor at the Blacksmith and add Trebuchets for sieges. Elite Eagles with Champions or Jaguar Warriors form a fast melee army, Siege Onagers deal with massed archers, and Monks with Redemption and Theocracy handle what the infantry cannot. When gold runs low, Elite Skirmishers and Pikemen keep you in the game while relics keep paying.

## Matchups

- Knight and Paladin civilizations such as Franks, Lithuanians and Burgundians are the hardest test. Eagles lose to heavy cavalry, so mass Pikemen in front, keep Monks behind them and use the Eagles to raid instead of taking the main fight.
- Strong infantry and anti infantry units punish Eagles. Hand Cannoneers, Champions with full upgrades and Cataphracts all trade well against them. Switch to Jaguar Warriors against infantry, Skirmishers and Monks against Cataphracts, and avoid fighting Hand Cannoneers without Rams or Onagers.
- Archer civilizations like Britons and Mayans are good matchups once Eagles are out. In the Feudal Age, Men-at-Arms and Skirmishers hold them off.
- On water maps the lack of Galleons hurts. Win early with Fire Galleys and Galleys or play a land heavy game where possible.

## Common mistakes

- Making too few Barracks. One Barracks of Eagles cannot keep up with the gold you collect; three or four is normal.
- Letting resources pile up. Aztecs depend on the Market to turn spare food or wood into the gold their army needs.
- Fighting Paladins or Cataphracts head on with Eagles. Use Pikemen and Monks for those fights and send the Eagles somewhere else.
- Skipping relics. Each relic gives Aztecs extra gold, and that income carries the late game.
- Forgetting the economy during a rush. The faster training is wasted if the Town Center sits idle while you control the Militia.

title: How to Play the Bengalis
summary: The Bengalis get two free Villagers per Town Center every time they reach a new age, and their elephants shrug off much of the damage from their usual counters. This guide covers openings, Castle and Imperial Age plans, Rathas and the matchups to watch.
body:
The Bengalis are an elephant and Monk civilization with an economy that pays out every time you reach a new age. All of their Town Centers spawn two Villagers the moment the next age arrives. With one Town Center that is two free Villagers in the Feudal Age and two more in the Castle Age. With three Town Centers it is six free Villagers when the Imperial Age lands. The civilization rewards players who add Town Centers early in the Castle Age and click Imperial on time.

## What the Bengalis are good at

Bengali elephants take 25% less bonus damage and are harder to convert. Pikemen, Camel Riders and Monks, the usual answers to elephants, all do less work against a Bengali Battle Elephant or Elephant Archer. Paiks, the Castle Age unique technology, makes elephants and Rathas attack 20% faster. Mahayana in the Imperial Age makes Villagers and Monks take 10% less population space, which leaves more room for elephants.

The rest of the bonuses support that plan. Bengali Monks have +3/+3 armor, so Scout Cavalry and archers have a hard time picking them off. Cavalry units deal +2 damage to Skirmishers, which means your Scout Cavalry and Light Cavalry keep raiding when the opponent answers with Skirmishers. Ships regenerate 15 HP per minute.

The gaps are just as clear. There are no Knights, no Cavalry Archers, no Hussar, no Hand Cannoneer and no Bombard Cannon. Foot archers lack Thumb Ring, infantry lacks Plate Mail Armor, and the ram line is replaced by the Armored Elephant and Siege Elephant. The Viking Sagas patch also removed Treadmill Crane. The win condition is a strong Castle Age economy that turns into elephants, Rathas and Monks, with a large Imperial Age army behind it.

## Openings that suit them

The free Villagers do nothing in the Dark Age, so the Bengalis open like any civilization and get their bonus when the age lands. Plan where those two Villagers go before you click up.

- Bengalis Scouts (civ-bengalis-scouts) is the common Arabia opening. On the ladder, Scout Cavalry is the most produced Bengali unit by a wide margin, and the bonus against Skirmishers keeps your scouts useful longer than usual.
- Bengalis Arena Fast Castle Boom (civ-bengalis-fast-castle-boom) is the plan on closed maps. You reach the Castle Age with extra Villagers and add two Town Centers right away.
- A Monk rush is a real option on closed maps thanks to the Monk armor. TheViper has shown one on Rage Forest.

## Castle Age plans

The Ratha is the Bengali unique unit, trained at the Castle for 60 wood and 60 gold. It switches between a bow and a sword. In ranged mode it shoots like a Crossbowman, and in melee mode it hits like a Knight. Use the bow against infantry and Spearmen, and the sword against archers and Skirmishers. Rathas keep the archer and cavalry archer armor classes in both modes, so Skirmishers and Huskarls still hurt them. Since The Viking Sagas the non-Elite Ratha takes 24 seconds to train, so one Castle cannot produce many. Add a second Castle if you commit to them.

Battle Elephants are the other core unit. They beat infantry-light armies and buildings, and the reduced bonus damage lets them trade with small groups of Pikemen. Elephant Archers were made more expensive in the October 2026 patch (70 food and 80 gold, 220 HP), so treat them as a mid-game unit for when you already have a gold lead.

Good Castle Age priorities are a second and third Town Center, Bloodlines and Husbandry for elephants, Paiks once you have a Castle, and a Monastery. Light Cavalry is your raiding and anti-Monk unit since you have no Hussar.

## Imperial Age

The late-game army is Elite Battle Elephants or Elite Rathas in front, Monks behind, and Siege Elephants for buildings. Halberdiers and Elite Skirmishers fill out the trash units, and Light Cavalry handles raids and siege. Arbalesters without Thumb Ring fall behind other archer civilizations, so do not build your late game around foot archers. Get Mahayana once your economy is stable.

## Matchups

Mobile ranged armies are the main problem. Cavalry archers and massed Crossbowmen can kite elephants, and you have neither Hussar nor Hand Cannoneer to catch them. Answer them with Rathas in melee mode, Light Cavalry and Elite Skirmishers, and fight close to your Castles.

Large numbers of Halberdiers plus Monks still beat elephants; the bonus only softens them. Switch Rathas to ranged mode against infantry and add Onagers or Armored Elephants.

Early aggression is dangerous because the Bengalis have nothing in the Dark Age. Against Men-at-Arms or a fast archer opening, wall your wood and gold and keep a few Spearmen or Skirmishers ready.

On the current ladder (AoE2Insights) the Bengalis do best against Muisca, Saracens and Gurjaras and worst against Wu, Shu and Inca.

## Common mistakes

- Clicking up late. The two Villagers per Town Center come when the age arrives, so every minute of delay costs economy.
- Staying on one Town Center. The Imperial Age payout is two Villagers per Town Center, which makes a third Town Center worth more than usual.
- Massing elephants alone. They are slow, so mix in Monks, Rathas or Light Cavalry.
- Fighting with Rathas as if they were Knights. Watch their mode and switch it when the target changes.
- Forgetting Paiks. The 20% attack speed applies to every elephant and every Ratha.

title: How to Play the Berbers
summary: The Berbers turn faster villagers and cheap Castle Age cavalry into a strong Knight timing, then win long games with Hussars, Camel Riders and Genitours that need little gold.
body:
## What the Berbers are good at

Berber villagers walk 5% faster in the Dark Age and 10% faster from the Feudal Age on. Every trip to a drop site, every walk to a new woodline and every lap around a farm gets a little shorter, so the economy runs slightly ahead of a normal civilization for the whole game. Their ships also move 10% faster, which helps Fishing Ships, Trade Cogs and hit-and-run fights on water.

The bonus that decides most games is the Stable discount: cavalry costs 15% less in the Castle Age and 20% less in the Imperial Age. A Berber Knight costs about 51 food and 64 gold instead of 60 and 75, so two Stables turn out more Knights than the same economy would give another civilization. Late in the game the discount makes Hussars and Heavy Camel Riders very cheap, and the Genitour, a mounted Skirmisher from the Archery Range that costs only food and wood, gives the Berbers a gold-free answer to archers.

The win condition has two halves. Hit the Castle Age with Knights and use the cheaper cavalry to stay ahead in units and villagers, or drag the game into the Imperial Age where Hussars, Genitours and Heavy Camel Riders make one of the best trash armies in the game.

The tech tree has clear holes: no Halberdier, no Arbalester, no Paladin, no Siege Ram or Siege Onager, no Parthian Tactics, and no Keep or Architecture. Berber defenses are below average, and their foot archers and infantry fall off in the Imperial Age.

## Openings that suit them

Fast Castle into Knights is the standard Berber plan on open maps, and the Berbers Fast Castle Knights build on this site walks through it with the Berber changes. Scouts into Knights works too, though the Berbers get no military bonus in the Feudal Age, so their Scout Cavalry are ordinary scouts with a slightly better economy behind them. Go scouts when you want map control against a greedy opponent, and go for the fast Castle Age when you want to cash in the discount as early as possible.

On water and hybrid maps, the faster ships make a Galley or Fire Galley opening comfortable, since you can always choose when to fight. On closed maps you can boom behind walls into Knights or straight into Camel Archers.

## Castle Age plan

Make Knights from two Stables the moment the Castle Age lands and research Bloodlines and Husbandry early, because Berber cavalry wins through speed and numbers. Raid with the whole group, keep the Town Center producing villagers and add a second and third Town Center behind the first push. The discount means you can afford a third Stable sooner than most Knight civilizations.

When the opponent answers with Pikemen, you have two good switches. Crossbowmen are fine in the Castle Age even though the Arbalester upgrade never comes. Camel Archers (built at the Castle for 50 wood and 60 gold) beat Cavalry Archers, and Camel Riders and Mamelukes deal little bonus damage to them, so they are the default answer to Mongols, Huns, Tatars, Magyars and other horse archer civilizations. Kasbah, the Castle Age unique technology, makes Castles work 25% faster for you and your allies, which mostly speeds up Camel Archer production and Trebuchets.

Against other Knight civilizations, Camel Riders get the same discount. In the Imperial Age, Maghrebi Camels lets every camel heal 15 HP per minute, so a Berber camel army that pulls back for a minute comes back healthier than the enemy expects.

## Imperial Age

The Knight line stops at Cavalier, so do not plan a Paladin finish. A typical Berber Imperial army has Camel Archers or Heavy Cavalry Archers for damage, Hussars and Heavy Camel Riders in front, Genitours in large numbers once the gold runs low, and Bombard Cannons or Trebuchets for buildings. With the 20% discount a Hussar costs 64 food. Hand Cannoneers are the best Berber answer to massed infantry.

Siege is a weak spot. Capped Ram and Onager are the top of those lines, so Bombard Cannons and Heavy Scorpions do most of the heavy work against buildings and armies.

## Matchups

- Halberdiers backed by Siege Rams are the classic way to beat the Berbers in a long game. Do not run cavalry into the pikes. Kite them with Camel Archers, add Hand Cannoneers, and kill the rams with Hussars or Camel Riders when the pikes are out of position.
- A strong Feudal rush before your Knights arrive is the main danger of the fast Castle plan. Wall early, use your faster villagers to fight towers and forward buildings, and make a few Spearmen or Skirmishers if you have to.
- Archer civilizations such as the Britons or Ethiopians win the straight archer war in the Imperial Age because you have no Arbalester. Fight them with Genitours, Hussars and Bombard Cannons instead.
- Infantry civilizations like the Goths or Japanese should face Camel Archers and Hand Cannoneers that stay out of melee range.
- Monk-heavy opponents struggle against cheap Light Cavalry and Hussars.

## Common mistakes

- Massing regular Cavalry Archers in the Imperial Age. Without Parthian Tactics they fall behind, and Camel Archers do the job better if you have the wood.
- Expecting the cavalry discount in the Feudal Age. It starts in the Castle Age, so a Feudal scout war against Franks or Lithuanians is an even fight at best.
- Ramming Knights into Halberdiers instead of switching to ranged units.
- Waiting too long to switch to Genitours. Start them before your last gold mine runs dry and get the Elite upgrade early in the Imperial Age.
- Leaving the base open. Without Keeps or Architecture, a late wall costs you more than an early one.

title: How to Play the Bohemians
summary: The Bohemians get free mining upgrades, cheap Blacksmiths and Hand Cannoneers in the Castle Age. This guide covers the fast Castle opening, the gunpowder and Monk army, the matchups that hurt and the habits that lose games.
body:
The Bohemians are a gunpowder and Monk civilization. They do their best work on closed maps and in long games, and they have one of the clearest power spikes in the game: Hand Cannoneers in the Castle Age, a full age before everyone else.

## What the Bohemians are good at

Most of the Bohemian economy sits in the Mining Camp. Every Mining Camp technology is free, so your gold and stone miners speed up the moment you reach the Feudal Age and again in the Castle Age, and you never spend food or wood on them. Blacksmiths and Universities also cost 100 wood less. A Blacksmith costs you only 50 wood, which makes the two Feudal buildings for a fast Castle Age cheap, and a University costs 100 wood when you want Chemistry.

Chemistry and the Hand Cannoneer are available in the Castle Age. A group of Hand Cannoneers behind Pikemen shreds Castle Age infantry and cavalry, and the Bohemian Spearman line deals 25 percent more bonus damage, so your Pikemen hit Knights much harder than usual. Fervor and Sanctity also affect villagers. With both researched your villagers walk faster and have more hit points, which helps farming, woodcutting and surviving raids.

The win condition: get through the Feudal Age without losing villagers, reach Castle Age with a good gold income, then push with gunpowder, spears and Monks. In the Imperial Age the Houfnice (the Bohemian Bombard Cannon upgrade) breaks Castles and packed armies, and Hussite Reforms turns the gold cost of Monks and Monastery technologies into food, which keeps your Monks going after the gold runs out.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

Bohemian cavalry is poor. There is no Bloodlines, no Plate Barding Armor, no Hussar and no Paladin, and the civilization has no Cavalry Archer. The Archer line lacks Thumb Ring, and the navy lacks Shipwright, Dry Dock and the Fast Fire Ship. You will rarely win a long raiding war, and water maps are a poor pick.

The free mining upgrades start in the Feudal Age, so your Dark Age is completely generic. A Militia or archer rush meets no special defense from you.

## Openings that suit them

- Fast Castle into Hand Cannoneers, written up as the build "Bohemians Fast Castle into Hand Cannoneers". This is the signature plan on Arena, Black Forest and other closed maps, and on Arabia when you can wall. The cheap Blacksmith pays for part of the second Feudal building, and free Gold Mining helps you collect the 200 gold for Castle Age.
- Archers, or Men-at-Arms into Archers, on open maps. Free Gold Mining helps a gold hungry Feudal Age, and the 50 wood Blacksmith lets you get Fletching early.
- A Feudal tower rush is possible because Stone Mining is free, though it is a niche choice.
- On Arena some players drop a forward Castle very early and make Hussite Wagons. It wins games at lower ratings, but Mangonels and an alert scout who spots the villagers walking over punish it.

## Castle Age plan

When you land in Castle Age, build a University and research Chemistry. Hand Cannoneers train at the Archery Range, so a second range comes next. Keep Pikemen in front of them. Hand Cannoneers fire slowly and miss part of their shots, so they melt if Knights reach them, and your spears with the extra bonus damage make that hard for the enemy.

Add a Monastery early. Fervor and Sanctity are economy upgrades for you, and Monks answer Knights and elephants well. The Bohemians have every Monastery technology.

Massed Crossbowmen and Skirmishers are the main threat to Hand Cannoneers. Bring Mangonels against archer armies, and use Hand Cannoneers mainly against melee units. A Castle unlocks Wagenburg Tactics (gunpowder units move 10 percent faster) and the Hussite Wagon, a sturdy gunpowder siege unit that blocks arrows aimed at the units behind it. A few wagons in front of your army help a lot against archers and towers.

If the opponent is passive, take a third and fourth Town Center behind the first push. Your gold income is better than most civilizations here thanks to free Gold Shaft Mining.

## Imperial Age plan

The late army is Hand Cannoneers or Arbalesters with Halberdiers in front and Houfnices behind. The Houfnice upgrade is expensive, but it hits harder and over a wider area than a normal Bombard Cannon, and it deals with enemy siege, Castles and packed infantry. Research Hussite Reforms once gold gets short. Food Monks heal and convert in trash wars, and Halberdiers with the spear bonus protect them from Hussars.

## Matchups

- Cavalry archer civilizations such as the Mongols, Magyars and Tatars are hard. Hand Cannoneers cannot catch them and your cavalry cannot chase them. Use Skirmishers, Hussite Wagons as a shield, Castles and siege, and push into their base so they have to fight.
- Strong Feudal rushers such as the Britons, Ethiopians or Aztecs can deny a fast Castle Age. Wall early, add Skirmishers or Spearmen as needed, and delay the Castle click by a minute before you lose villagers to save it.
- Knight civilizations are comfortable matchups. Spears with bonus damage, Monks and Hand Cannoneers all trade well against cavalry.
- Civilizations with strong Mangonels and Onagers punish clumped gunpowder. Spread your Hand Cannoneers and kill siege with a few Knights or with Bombard Cannons.

## Common mistakes

- Making Knights or Light Cavalry your main army. Without Bloodlines and the late armor upgrades they lose to almost everything.
- Skipping the Monastery. Fervor and Sanctity are part of your economy, and the Monk line is one of your best units.
- Massing Hand Cannoneers without a front line. They need Pikemen or Halberdiers in front, and Mangonels or Skirmishers when the enemy has archers.
- Clicking up to Castle Age on an open map without walls. The fast Castle only works if your wood and gold lines survive the Feudal Age.
- Forgetting Hussite Reforms in long games. Food Monks are what lets the Bohemians keep fighting after the gold mines are gone.

title: How to Play the Britons
summary: Britons win by massing foot archers that outrange everything built to counter them. This guide covers the archer opening, the Castle Age boom with half price Town Centers, the Imperial Age army and the matchups that give Britons trouble.
body:
The Britons are the classic archer civilization, and their plan is easy to understand: build a big group of foot archers, keep them alive, and let their extra range do the work. That makes them a good first civilization to learn, and they stay strong at every level on open maps such as Arabia.

## What the Britons are good at

Four bonuses shape the civilization.

- Foot archers (all of them except Skirmishers) get +1 range in the Castle Age and +2 in the Imperial Age. Yeomen adds one more, so a fully upgraded Briton Arbalester shoots from much further away than most units built to fight it.
- Archery Ranges work 10% faster. This is the team bonus, and it helps your own production too.
- Shepherds work 25% faster, so your Dark Age food comes in quicker and you can reach the Feudal Age with a villager or two fewer than other civilizations.
- Town Centers cost 50% less wood from the Castle Age on, which makes a Castle Age boom cheap.

Your win condition is a large, upgraded archer army that kills Skirmishers, Mangonels and infantry before they can close the gap, while Pikemen or Halberdiers stand in front to stop cavalry. The extra range lets you shoot Mangonels and Skirmishers from outside their own range, so the units your opponent makes to counter archers trade much worse than usual.

The weak side is cavalry and siege. Britons have no Bloodlines, no Thumb Ring, no Hussar and no Paladin. Since The Viking Sagas they train the Mounted Crossbowman in place of the Cavalry Archer, but without Thumb Ring or Bloodlines it is a support unit at best. Their Siege Workshop stops at Capped Ram and Onager, and they have no Bombard Cannon or Hand Cannoneer.

## Openings that suit the Britons

The standard opening on open maps is archers from one Archery Range, clicking up a little earlier than a generic civilization thanks to the shepherd bonus. The build is written out as Britons One Range Archers on this site. Add a second range once your gold income allows it.

On closed maps such as Arena, go for a Fast Castle and use the cheaper Town Centers to boom into Crossbowmen and Trebuchets. A Men-at-Arms opening into archers is also fine against civilizations that like to sit at home, since your infantry is fully upgraded.

## Castle Age plan

Click up when you have around 15 to 20 archers and your farms are running. On arrival get Crossbowman and Bodkin Arrow first, then Ballistics so your army hits moving targets. Build one or two extra Town Centers right away; each costs only half the usual wood, so a boom costs you less army than it would for anyone else.

Add a few Pikemen against Knights, and a Siege Workshop if the opponent hides behind walls or towers. Yeomen is worth buying once you have a real archer army, since it adds range again and gives your towers more attack.

Longbowmen come from the Castle and are slower to produce than Crossbowmen from several ranges. In the Castle Age most players stay on Crossbowmen. Elite Longbowmen become the better unit later, when you have Castles running and want the longest range in the game.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age you want Arbalesters or Elite Longbowmen with Bracer, a front line of Halberdiers, and Warwolf Trebuchets. Warwolf gives your Trebuchets blast damage and full accuracy against units, which turns them into a weapon against tightly packed armies as well as buildings. Champions with full Blacksmith armor are your answer to Siege Rams and to Skirmisher masses that walk under your arrows.

Keep a few Elite Skirmishers if the opponent adds Cavalry Archers or mounted crossbows of their own; your Mounted Crossbowmen lose to most units of the same role from fully upgraded civilizations.

## Matchups and what gives Britons trouble

Archer armies have three natural enemies, and Britons have answers to each of them as long as you respect the counter.

- Skirmishers with armor upgrades. Use your range: stop, let them walk into your volleys, then retreat a step. Add Men-at-Arms or Long Swordsmen if they keep coming.
- Heavy cavalry, especially Knight civilizations such as the Franks, Lithuanians and Persians (whose Knights also deal +2 damage to archers). Keep Pikemen in front, wall early, and do not let your archers stray from the group.
- Siege. Civilizations with Siege Onagers or Bombard Cannons outrange your archers or kill them in one shot. Split your army, use Trebuchets and Champions to answer siege, and attack the Onagers before they fire.

Against other archer civilizations your range wins most straight fights. Against infantry civilizations such as the Goths or Japanese, your archers are strong, but watch for Huskarls and rams later in the game.

## Common mistakes with the Britons

- Stopping villager production while you mass archers. The archer plan needs a lot of wood and gold, so keep the Town Center busy and add farms steadily.
- Using attack orders on single units. Patrol or attack move so every archer fires, and pull back wounded ones.
- Forgetting a meat shield. A group of 30 Crossbowmen with nothing in front loses to 10 Knights.
- Making Mounted Crossbowmen or Cavaliers as your main army. Without Bloodlines and Thumb Ring they lose to almost every other civilization's version.
- Fighting under enemy Castles or Town Centers. Your range only helps when the fight happens on your terms.

title: How to Play the Bulgarians
summary: Bulgarians fight early with free Militia line upgrades and cheap Blacksmith techs, then push with Konniks from a half price Krepost. This guide covers the openings, the Castle and Imperial plans and how to handle archer civilizations.
body:
The Bulgarians are a melee civilization with two strong branches: infantry from the Barracks and cavalry from the Stable. Their bonuses save resources on upgrades, so they can afford to fight earlier than most civilizations and keep fighting at every stage of the game. Their weak point is the Archery Range, which makes the matchup plan very clear.

## What the Bulgarians are good at

- Man-at-Arms, Long Swordsman and Two-Handed Swordsman upgrades are free. You get Men-at-Arms the moment the Feudal Age arrives and Long Swordsmen the moment you reach the Castle Age.
- Blacksmith and Siege Workshop technologies cost half the food. Forging, the barding armors and the mail armors all come cheaper, which matters when you upgrade both infantry and cavalry.
- Town Centers cost half the stone (the starting one excluded), so a three or four Town Center boom needs very little stone mining.
- The Krepost is a small Castle for 350 stone. It shoots arrows, trains Konniks and supports 20 population, and you can place it close to the opponent. It cannot research technologies apart from the Elite Konnik upgrade, so Stirrups and Bagains still need a Castle.
- Stirrups makes all cavalry attack 33% faster. Bulgarian Hussars and Cavaliers hit very hard for their cost.
- Bagains gives the Militia line +5 melee armor in the Imperial Age, so Two-Handed Swordsmen win most melee fights even without the Champion upgrade.
- The team bonus makes Blacksmiths work 80% faster for everyone on the team.

The win condition is simple: use the cheap upgrades to hit early, then keep the pressure going with Konniks and Krepost pushes while your Town Centers boom at home.

## Openings that suit them

Two openings are worth learning first. The Bulgarians Men-at-Arms into Scouts build on this site clicks up at 20 population and has Men-at-Arms in the opponent's base about a minute earlier than a generic build, because you skip the 100 food and 40 gold upgrade. It is the most common Bulgarian opening on Arabia and it pairs well with a Stable once the first three Men-at-Arms are out.

The Bulgarians Fast Castle Krepost build skips Feudal fighting and goes straight for a forward Krepost and Konniks, with a second Town Center paid for by the cheap stone cost. Hera has shown this plan in several recent videos. It is stronger on closed maps and against players who boom.

Scouts are also fine. Bulgarians have no Feudal cavalry bonus, but Bloodlines and the barding armors are cheap, so a Scout opening moves smoothly into Knights. Avoid Feudal archer play: Bulgarians have no Crossbowman, so archers have nowhere to go.

## Castle Age plan

Most games go into one of two compositions. Knights with Stirrups are the main raiding force; Konniks join them once a Krepost or Castle is up. Konniks cost 60 food and 70 gold and train in 16 seconds. When a Konnik dies it leaves a Dismounted Konnik, an infantry unit that keeps fighting, so a Konnik army trades very well in drawn out fights. Upgrade the mail armors as well as the barding armors, since the dismounted form uses infantry upgrades.

The second option is Long Swordsmen with Pikemen and Skirmishers. Long Swordsmen are free and the armor upgrades cost little food, so a Barracks army is affordable even on a small gold income. Siege Rams and Mangonels from a cheap Siege Workshop back up either army.

Build a second and third Town Center early in the Castle Age. Each one needs only 50 stone, so two or three stone miners in Feudal are enough to pay for the Town Centers and a Krepost.

Research Stirrups at a Castle once you have a sizable cavalry army. Research Bloodlines and Husbandry early, because Bulgarian cavalry depends on hit-and-run raids.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age, Bulgarians have Cavalier, Hussar, Heavy Cavalry Archer, Two-Handed Swordsman, Halberdier, Siege Onager, Siege Ram and Heavy Scorpion. A common late game army is Two-Handed Swordsmen with Bagains plus Elite Konniks, supported by Siege Onagers. Against archers, Hussars with Stirrups clean up Arbalesters and Hand Cannoneers quickly. The missing parts are Paladin, Champion, Bombard Cannon and Fortified Wall. Plan for a melee army and use Trebuchets and Siege Onagers as your siege.

## Matchups

Bulgarians win most of their games against civilizations with slow starts or heavy infantry. They struggle against civilizations that keep them at range. Ladder statistics show their weakest matchups are Mongols, Saracens, Ethiopians, Khitans, Shu and Huns.

- Against mounted archers (Mongols, Huns), you cannot fight back with Crossbowmen. Make Elite Skirmishers with full Blacksmith upgrades, and use Hussars and Konniks to force fights in narrow places. Cavalry Archers of your own are an option in the Imperial Age.
- Against massed foot archers (Ethiopians, Saracens), get Siege Rams and Mangonels early. Infantry alone walks into arrows; with rams in front, Long Swordsmen reach the archers.
- Against Camel Rider civilizations, switch from Knights to Long Swordsmen and Two-Handed Swordsmen, which beat Camel Riders for much less gold.
- Against booming civilizations, the Krepost rush is the best answer. A forward Krepost kills villagers on its own and keeps the opponent busy while you add Town Centers.

## Common mistakes

- Playing a Feudal archer game. Without Crossbowman there is no follow up, and you waste the money on Fletching and archers.
- Forgetting that Militia line upgrades are free. You can go straight to Long Swordsmen in the Castle Age without paying the upgrade, so do not wait for a separate Barracks timing.
- Paying full price in your head. Blacksmith upgrades cost half the food, so get Forging and Scale Barding early instead of saving the food for later.
- Using Konniks without a plan for pikes. Halberdiers and Camel Riders still beat both Konnik forms, so keep a few Long Swordsmen or Skirmishers with the army.
- Ignoring the cheap Town Centers. A Bulgarian player who stays on one Town Center gives up their only economic bonus.

title: How to Play the Burgundians
summary: The Burgundians get their economy upgrades one age early and Cavaliers in the Castle Age. How to get through the first fifteen minutes, when to buy each upgrade and how to turn the lead into a Cavalier push.
body:
The Burgundians are a cavalry civilization whose economy pulls ahead by itself. Every economic technology except Coinage and Banking is available one age earlier than usual and costs 40 percent less food. That puts Double-Bit Axe, Horse Collar, Wheelbarrow and Gold Mining in the Dark Age, Bow Saw, Heavy Plow and Hand Cart in the Feudal Age, and Two-Man Saw, Crop Rotation and Guilds in the Castle Age.

## What the Burgundians are good at

The second big bonus sits at the Stable. Stable technologies cost half, and the Cavalier upgrade is available in the Castle Age. A Burgundian Knight rush turns into a Cavalier rush a couple of minutes after Castle Age lands, before any other civilization can field Cavaliers. In the Imperial Age, gunpowder units deal 25 percent more damage, so Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons hit unusually hard.

The win condition follows from this. Survive the Dark and Feudal Ages without losing villagers, arrive in the Castle Age with more upgrades than your opponent, and hit with Cavaliers while the other side still has Knights, Crossbowmen or a half finished wall. The Burgundians have no military bonus before the Castle Age, and that is where they lose most games. TheViper's 2025 video on them is titled after exactly that problem, and Hera's from the same year blames their falling win rate on nerfs to the early upgrades and a meta full of Feudal infantry pressure.

The tech tree has gaps you need to know about. The Burgundians lack Bloodlines, so their Knights, Paladins and Hussars have fewer hit points than the same units of other cavalry civilizations. The Archery Range is weak, with no Arbalester, no Thumb Ring and no useful Cavalry Archer. The Siege Workshop lacks Siege Ram, Siege Onager and Heavy Scorpion, and the Monastery lacks Heresy, so enemy Monks can convert your expensive cavalry.

## When to buy the early upgrades

Food spent in the Dark Age pushes your age up back, so buy the upgrades that pay back fast.

- Double-Bit Axe comes first. It costs 60 food and 50 wood, it is researched at the Lumber Camp so the Town Center keeps making villagers, and the extra wood means Farms and buildings on time. Most builds get it somewhere around villager 10 to 14.
- Horse Collar goes in just before the first Farms are placed.
- Gold Mining is worth it once three or more villagers mine gold, usually while you advance to the Feudal Age.
- Wheelbarrow is researched at the Town Center and stops villager production for over a minute. Leave it out of fast builds and buy it once you have 25 or more villagers.
- In the Feudal Age, take Bow Saw first and Heavy Plow when you have about eight Farms. Hand Cart pays off only with a big economy, so it usually waits until the Castle Age.

## Openings

Two builds on this site are written for the Burgundians. Burgundians Fast Castle into Cavaliers is the default on closed maps and against opponents who play slowly. It gets Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar in the Dark Age and clicks up to the Castle Age with two Feudal buildings, one of them a Stable. Burgundians Scouts into Cavaliers is the open map choice. It uses Double-Bit Axe at around villager 10, takes map control with Scout Cavalry and then goes up to the Castle Age with the upgrades already bought.

The general Fast Castle into 3 Town Center boom also suits them, since their Castle Age farming and wood upgrades come early. On Arena, a Castle Age boom into a fast Imperial Age with Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons is a strong plan, and several 2026 Arena builds use exactly that.

In the current patch the Flemish Militia can be trained at the Barracks from the Feudal Age without any research. It costs 35 food and 25 gold and carries bonus damage against cavalry, so a few of them are your cheapest answer to an early Scout Cavalry rush.

## Castle Age plan

Arrive with two Stables. Make Knights from both and research the Cavalier upgrade as soon as you can afford it. At half price it costs 150 food and 150 gold, which is less than two Knights, and every Knight you own gets stronger at once. Husbandry is also half price and worth getting early for raids. Keep the Town Center working and add a second and third Town Center behind your first attack, since a raid that covers a boom is how the Burgundians usually win.

The Coustillier is the Castle unique unit. It is a lighter Knight with a charge attack that deals heavy damage on the first strike and refills while the unit stays out of combat. Coustilliers are best at hit and run: pick off a Monk or a wounded archer with the charge, ride away and come back once it refills. They do worse than Cavaliers in a long melee fight, so make them when you already have a Castle and plan to raid.

Burgundian Vineyards makes your farmers earn a slow trickle of gold. It costs 400 food and 300 gold, so research it once you have 30 or more farmers. Around 28 farmers produce about as much gold as one Relic.

Against massed Pikemen, keep the cavalry alive for raids and push to the Imperial Age, where Hand Cannoneers with their attack bonus handle infantry.

## Imperial Age

The Paladin upgrade costs half here too. A typical late army is Paladins with Hand Cannoneers behind them and Bombard Cannons for buildings and enemy siege. When gold runs low, Hussars and Flemish Militia are your trash units, and Vineyards keeps some gold coming in after the mines are gone.

Flemish Revolution turns every villager into a Flemish Militia. Its price grows with the number of villagers you own, and your economy disappears the moment it finishes. Keep it for a finishing move when one big attack will end the game, or for a last defense when the base is falling anyway.

## Matchups

- Early aggression is the main danger. Drush, Men-at-Arms, archer rushes and civilizations like the Aztecs, Malians, Mongols or Vikings can wreck the slow Burgundian start. Wall early, keep Loom ready, and use Flemish Militia or towers instead of panicking.
- Civilizations with Camel Riders and good Halberdiers, such as the Saracens, Hindustanis or Berbers, blunt the Cavalier timing. Scout them, and plan a boom with Crossbowmen and Monks instead of an all in cavalry push.
- Strong Monk civilizations convert your cavalry easily because you lack Heresy. Hunt them with Coustilliers or Light Cavalry.

## Common mistakes

- Buying every early upgrade at once. Wheelbarrow at villager 15 or Hand Cart at five Farms costs more than it returns.
- Skipping walls on open maps.
- Making Knights without the Cavalier upgrade. At half price, the upgrade is the whole point of the Castle Age plan.
- Sending Cavaliers into a wall of pikes. Raid elsewhere, and switch units when the counter shows up.
- Researching Flemish Revolution while still trading evenly, which throws away your economy for an army that may not finish the game.

title: How to Play the Burmese
summary: Burmese hit hard with infantry from the Feudal Age, get every Lumber Camp upgrade for free and field very sturdy Battle Elephants. This guide covers the Men-at-Arms opening, the fast castle into Arambai and how to deal with the archer civilizations that trouble them.
body:
## What the Burmese are good at

The Burmese have one of the simplest economies to play. Every Lumber Camp technology is free: Double-Bit Axe arrives with the Feudal Age, Bow Saw with the Castle Age and Two-Man Saw with the Imperial Age, without any research time. That saves 100 food and 50 wood in Feudal alone and keeps your woodcutters ahead of the opponent's all game.

Their infantry gets +1 attack in the Feudal Age, +2 in the Castle Age and +3 in the Imperial Age on top of Blacksmith upgrades. Men-at-Arms kill villagers and Spearmen faster than anyone else's, and late-game Champions and Halberdiers trade very well. Battle Elephants have +1/+1 armor as a civilization bonus and get another +1/+1 from the Imperial Age tech Howdah, which makes Burmese elephants very hard to kill. Monastery technologies cost half, so Redemption, Sanctity and Fervor are cheap, and the team bonus shows every Relic on the map from the start.

The unique unit is the Arambai, a mounted ranged unit from the Castle with a huge but inaccurate attack. It deletes clumps of infantry, Monks and villagers, and it is fast enough to raid. The Castle Age tech Manipur Cavalry gives all cavalry +4 attack against archers, which matters because the Archery Range is where the Burmese are weakest.

The tech tree has holes. There is no Thumb Ring and no Arbalester, so your foot archers fall off after the Castle Age. The Stable stops at Cavalier, and the Siege Workshop has no Siege Ram or Siege Onager. Plan for Hussars, Cavaliers, Battle Elephants, Arambai and Barracks units, with Monks and Bombard Cannons for support.

## Openings that suit them

The infantry attack bonus points straight at a Feudal Men-at-Arms rush (see the build Burmese Men-at-Arms). Three Men-at-Arms with the extra point of damage reach the opponent before they have Spearmen or archers out, and the free Double-Bit Axe means your wood economy does not suffer while you fight.

The second plan is a fast castle into Arambai (see the build Fast Castle into Arambai). TheViper and DauT both show it: a Castle goes down as soon as you land, and Arambai start raiding or defending before the opponent has Crossbowmen in numbers. On Arena the double castle version from the Build Order Reference keeps two Castles training Arambai at once.

Scout Cavalry is the unit Burmese players train most according to AoE2Insights, and jimmyjames59 shows a scout rush that grabs an early Blacksmith armor upgrade. Scouts work well on open maps when you expect a fast castle opponent.

## Castle Age plan

Coming out of a Feudal infantry start, most Burmese players go up and pick one of two paths. Against archers and siege, make Knights with Manipur Cavalry and Arambai behind them. Against cavalry and infantry, go Battle Elephants with Halberdiers or Pikemen next to them, and use Monks with cheap Redemption to steal enemy elephants or Knights.

Arambai are best in a group of eight or more. Their shots miss a lot, so they do the most damage against tight groups that stand still, like archers behind a wall of infantry or villagers on a gold mine. Get Bloodlines early so they survive a few more hits.

Use your cheap Monastery. Fervor and Sanctity cost half, and three or four Relics pay for a lot of Arambai.

## Imperial Age plan

Elite Battle Elephants with Howdah are the late-game hammer: +2/+2 armor over the standard elephant makes them hard to kill with anything except Halberdiers, Monks and camels. Mix them with Champions or Halberdiers, Elite Arambai and Hussars to clean up archers and siege. Bombard Cannons and Trebuchets take down Castles. Because Two-Man Saw is free, you can afford wood-heavy Elite Arambai and still keep up with Farms.

## Matchups

AoE2Insights puts the Burmese just under a 50% win rate in 1v1 random map, with their worst results against Huns, Vikings, Mongols, Ethiopians, Maya and Shu.

The common thread is massed archers and cavalry archers. Burmese cannot match them with their own archers, so use Skirmishers in the Feudal Age, then Knights or Hussars with Manipur Cavalry, Arambai against foot archers and Mangonels against clumps. Battle Elephants are too slow to catch Mangudai or Cavalry Archers, so do not commit to them against Mongols or Huns.

Vikings have cheap, durable infantry and good archers, and both handle Burmese Men-at-Arms and Champions well; go Knights with Manipur Cavalry and Arambai there. Against Maya, Plumed Archers and Eagle Warriors are both fast and cheap, so elephants struggle to catch anything. Champions with the attack bonus handle the Eagles, and Skirmishers with Hussars handle the archers.

The Burmese do well against slower civilizations that rely on infantry or elephants without strong archers, such as Burgundians, Jurchens, Sicilians and the Three Kingdoms civilizations Wu and Wei.

## Common mistakes

- Massing Arbalester-less archers into the Imperial Age. Burmese archers stop upgrading early; switch to Skirmishers, Arambai and cavalry.
- Spreading Arambai out. They need to fire together to make up for their poor accuracy.
- Sending Battle Elephants into Halberdiers or Monks without support. Even with the armor bonus they lose those fights.
- Forgetting that Lumber Camp upgrades are already done. Do not wait for them; spend the saved resources on units or a faster age up.
- Ignoring the Monastery. Half-price techs and visible Relics make Monks a cheap source of gold and conversions.

title: How to Play the Byzantines
summary: Byzantines have no economic bonus but the widest tech tree in the game, cheap counter units and a discounted Imperial Age. This guide explains how to open with Skirmishers and Spearmen or archers, how to adapt in the Castle Age and what the late game army looks like.
body:
The Byzantines are the counter unit civilization. They have no bonus that speeds up gathering, but almost every unit and technology is available to them, and the units that counter other units are cheaper. Skirmishers, Spearmen and Camel Riders, with all their upgrades, cost 25% less. Buildings, walls and Farms have extra hit points that grow every age, Town Watch and Town Patrol are free, and the Imperial Age costs a third less. Their game plan is to scout, build the right answer more cheaply than the opponent can build the threat, and reach the Imperial Age with Arbalesters, Bombard Cannons and Cataphracts.

## What the Byzantines do well

- Cheap counters. A discounted Skirmisher or Pikeman means the opponent's archers and cavalry trade badly for the whole game. Heavy Camel Riders cost so little that even without Bloodlines they beat most cavalry in numbers.
- Defense. Walls and buildings last longer, so a Feudal Age wall holds and a Castle Age Town Center is hard to take down.
- The Cataphract. This Castle unit deals heavy bonus damage to infantry and takes reduced bonus damage from Pikemen and Camels. With Logistica it gains trample damage. It is one of the best answers in the game to infantry armies.
- Water. Fire Ships and Dromons fire 25% faster, and Greek Fire adds range and splash.
- Monks. Every important Monastery technology is there, and the team bonus makes Monks heal twice as fast.

The gaps are small but real. No Bloodlines and no Blast Furnace make Knights and Cavalry Archers average. The Siege Workshop lacks Siege Onager, Heavy Scorpion and Siege Engineers, so Bombard Cannons and Trebuchets do the long range work. Without an economy bonus you must avoid falling behind in villagers.

## Openings

The Byzantines Skirmisher and Spear rush, written up as a build on this site, uses the discount from the first minute of Feudal. Click up at around 20 population, put a Barracks at home and an Archery Range near the enemy, and send a steady stream of Skirmishers and Spearmen at their berries and gold. Skirmishers beat archer openings, Spearmen beat scout openings, and together they force the opponent off food. The free Town Watch helps you see what is coming.

The other standard plan is archers behind walls: an archer opening, solid palisades with the extra hit points, and a move to Crossbowmen in Castle Age. If you expect Knights later, an opening with a Stable gives you a building ready for Camels.

A third option, popular at lower ratings, is to wall early, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar quickly and make cheap Skirmishers behind the walls only when needed. This plays to the cheap counters and sturdy walls without requiring a precise rush.

## Castle Age plan

Scout and react. Against archers, mass Elite Skirmishers and add Crossbowmen for damage. Against Knights, make Camel Riders and Pikemen; the discount lets you outnumber the enemy. Against infantry and Eagles, build a Castle and make Cataphracts. Crossbowmen with a few Pikemen in front is a fine default when you are not sure.

Because there is no economic bonus, add Town Centers when the map is quiet and get the economy technologies on time. A Monastery for relics helps the gold situation in long games.

## Imperial Age

Use the discount to arrive early. Survivalist's advice for archer play is to research Bracer and Chemistry first, start Bombard Cannons, and click the Arbalester upgrade later so it lands with Chemistry. Arbalesters in front of Bombard Cannons beat most late game armies, and Cataphracts with Logistica clean up infantry. Halberdiers, Elite Skirmishers and Heavy Camel Riders form a cheap trash army when gold runs out, and the Halberdiers and Elite Skirmishers get every upgrade. Hussars and the Varangian Guard line round out the options.

## Matchups

- Strong economy civilizations that boom, such as Burgundians, outgrow you if you sit back with walls and counter units. Apply pressure with the Skirmisher and Spear rush or an early Crossbow push.
- A Men-at-Arms opening kills a Skirmisher and Spear rush. If your scout sees a Barracks going up early, keep the Skirmishers at home and add a few archers.
- Siege heavy armies with Siege Onagers punish your massed Arbalesters, and you cannot answer with Siege Onagers yourself. Use Bombard Cannons, Hussars and Cataphracts to reach the enemy siege.
- Cavalry archer civilizations like Mongols and Huns struggle against discounted Elite Skirmishers and Camels.

## Common mistakes

- Making a bit of everything. The tech tree is wide, but upgrades are expensive. Pick one or two unit lines and upgrade them fully.
- Falling behind in villagers while turtling. Walls buy time; use it to boom.
- Building Paladins or Cavalry Archers as the main army. Without Bloodlines they lose to the same units on the other side.
- Forgetting the cheap Imperial Age. A Byzantine who is slightly behind can still be the first to reach Imperial Age if the army holds.

title: How to Play the Celts
summary: The Celts chop wood faster, move their infantry faster in every age and have the strongest siege in the game. How to open with them, how to build a Castle Age infantry and siege push, and how to deal with archers and cavalry archers.
body:
The Celts are an infantry and siege civilization with one of the best wood economies in the game. Their lumberjacks work 15% faster, their infantry moves faster in every age, and their siege weapons fire 25% faster. A Celt army that reaches the Imperial Age with Siege Onagers, Halberdiers and Woad Raiders is very hard to fight head on. The price is a thin tech tree outside those two branches.

## What the Celts are good at

The infantry speed bonus grows with the ages: 5% in the Dark Age, 10% in the Feudal Age, 15% in the Castle Age and 20% in the Imperial Age. That is more than Squires, which the Celts do not have, and it lets your infantry catch villagers, run from archers and reach the opponent's base sooner. The Woad Raider, the Celt unique unit, is the fastest of them. It costs 70 food and 25 gold, trains in 10 seconds and does bonus damage to buildings, so it raids very well.

The Siege Workshop is the best in the game. Siege fires 25% faster, the team bonus makes Siege Workshops work 20% faster (team bonuses apply to you as well), and Furor Celtica gives siege +40% HP. Celt Mangonels and Siege Onagers are what opponents fear most. Stronghold makes Castles and towers fire 33% faster and lets Castles heal nearby infantry.

The lumberjack bonus pays off from the first minute. Archery Ranges, Siege Workshops, Farms and extra Town Centers all cost wood, and the Celts get it faster than anyone. Celts can also steal sheep that the opponent's scout is standing next to, which is worth a few hundred food on maps with spread herdables.

The weak spots are archers, cavalry and Monks. There is no Thumb Ring, no Bracer and no Arbalester. Cavalry lacks Bloodlines and Plate Barding Armor. Monks miss most Monastery technologies including Redemption. Since The Viking Sagas the Celts train Mounted Crossbowmen instead of Cavalry Archers and lost Treadmill Crane.

## Openings that suit them

- Celts Men-at-Arms into Archers (civ-celts-men-at-arms-archers) is the standard aggressive start. Faster Men-at-Arms reach the enemy base sooner and catch fleeing villagers, and the extra wood pays for two Archery Ranges behind them.
- Celts Fast Castle Siege Push (civ-celts-fast-castle-siege) skips Feudal fighting and hits with rams, Mangonels and infantry early in the Castle Age. It is strongest on closed maps or against an opponent who walls.
- A straight archer opening also works because of the wood bonus, but Celt archers fall behind from the Castle Age, so plan the switch to infantry and siege before then.

## Castle Age plans

Your Castle Age army is infantry plus siege. Long Swordsmen and Pikemen in front, Mangonels or Scorpions behind, and a pair of Battering Rams or Capped Rams for buildings and Castles. Mangonels deal with massed archers, which are the usual answer to infantry. Scorpions are a safer choice when your own infantry stands in the line of fire.

Woad Raiders come from the Castle and are best as a raiding force. Send a group into the opponent's wood lines and gold while the main army pushes. Do not expect them to beat Knights or massed archers in a straight fight.

Get Bow Saw early since wood is your strength, then infantry armor at the Blacksmith. You never need Squires because the speed bonus already covers it. Add a second and third Town Center if the opponent is passive.

## Imperial Age

Celt Imperial armies are built around Siege Onagers with Furor Celtica. Halberdiers protect them against cavalry and keep up thanks to the speed bonus. Champions or Elite Woad Raiders take care of enemy infantry and buildings. Heavy Scorpions are useful when you have a lot of infantry in front. Trebuchets also fire 25% faster and win most trebuchet duels.

Your trash units are weak: Skirmishers lack Bracer and the Imperial Skirmisher, and Hussars lack Bloodlines. In a long game with no gold left, Halberdiers are your best trash unit.

## Matchups

Cavalry archer civilizations are a hard matchup. Mangonels miss moving horse archers, your Skirmishers are weak and your cavalry has no Bloodlines. Keep Skirmishers and Halberdiers in your army, push buildings so the opponent has to fight, and use Woad Raiders to punish their economy.

Gunpowder and strong melee civilizations are the other problem. On AoE2Insights the Celts' worst ladder matchups are Malians, Bulgarians, Romans, Mongols, Teutons and Japanese. Hand Cannoneers and heavy infantry trade well with Celt infantry, so lean on siege, and use Onagers against masses of gunpowder.

The Celts do well against civilizations that rely on slow infantry or that cannot handle siege, and their best matchups include Mapuche, Gurjaras, Inca, Muisca and Goths.

## Common mistakes

- Making Knights in the Castle Age. Without Bloodlines they lose to the same Knights from most civilizations.
- Leaving siege without infantry next to it. Celt siege is strong, but a few Light Cavalry or Knights destroy it if nothing protects it.
- Keeping archers into the Imperial Age. Without Thumb Ring and Bracer they fall behind; change to Siege Onagers and infantry.
- Forgetting the sheep. Use your Scout Cavalry to look for the opponent's sheep early; you can take them even if their scout is next to them.
- Spending the extra wood slowly. A Celt player with 800 wood in the bank is wasting the bonus; add Farms, Archery Ranges or Siege Workshops.

title: How to Play the Chinese
summary: The Chinese start with three extra villagers but no food, which makes the first minutes hard. Get through them and cheaper technologies, a flexible tech tree and the Chu Ko Nu carry you into a strong late game.
body:
## What the Chinese are good at

The Chinese start with 6 villagers instead of 3, but with 200 less food and 50 less wood. That leaves you with no food at all, so the Town Center cannot train a villager in the first seconds. Their Town Centers support 15 population instead of 5 and see 7 tiles further, so the first House can wait until about 13 population. Technologies cost 5% less in the Feudal Age, 10% less in the Castle Age and 15% less in the Imperial Age, which adds up to a lot of free resources over a long game. Fire Galleys, Fire Ships and Fire Lancers move faster from the Castle Age, and the team bonus gives Farms 10% more food.

The tech tree is wide. Foot archers are fully upgraded, the Knight line goes to Cavalier, and the Barracks gets the Fire Lancer, an anti-cavalry gunpowder infantry that costs only wood and gold. The Rocket Cart replaces the Mangonel line, the Chu Ko Nu fires several bolts at once, and the Lou Chuan and the Dragon Ship (the Chinese upgrade of the Fire Ship) make the navy strong. Great Wall gives walls and towers 30% more hit points, and Rocketry adds 25% attack to Scorpions, Rocket Carts and Lou Chuans.

The gaps matter too. The Chinese have no Hussar, no Camel Rider, no Paladin, no Bombard Cannon, no Hand Cannoneer, no Redemption and no Heresy, and since the Viking Sagas patch they lose the Heavy Cavalry Archer as well. Their answers to enemy siege are cavalry and their own Rocket Carts.

The win condition: survive the awkward Dark Age and early Feudal Age, then use the tech discount to stay one upgrade ahead in the Castle Age and grow into a late game where Chu Ko Nu or Arbalesters with Rocket Carts and Halberdiers are very hard to break.

## The Chinese start

Research Loom the moment the game starts, since the Town Center has nothing else to do. Send all six villagers to the sheep your scout brings in, and as soon as you can afford 50 food, queue villagers. Force a food drop off (select the sheep villagers and right-click the Town Center) only when the Town Center is about to go idle; dropping too early or too often wastes walking time. Send the seventh villager to food as well before you start wood, because six shepherds cannot keep up with nonstop villager production. You start short on wood, so do not delay the Lumber Camp after that.

## Openings that suit them

This site has two Chinese builds that handle the start: Chinese Scouts at 23 population and Chinese Archers at 24 population. Men-at-Arms into Archers is a third common choice. On closed maps like Arena or Black Forest a fast Castle Age boom is often the best use of the tech discount, and Great Wall makes your walls and towers much harder to break.

## Castle Age plan

The Castle Age is where the discount starts to show. Crossbowmen and Knights are both strong because Bodkin Arrow, Fletching, Bloodlines and the armor upgrades all cost less. Pick the one the opponent is weak to and keep the other in mind as a switch. Fire Lancers open each fight with a short-range shot that ignores armor and then fight in melee, so they hold off Knights and infantry, but they need careful use; a careless Fire Lancer push can lose a lot of resources. A Monk push is also possible thanks to cheaper Monastery technologies.

Add Town Centers behind your army. The extra population space from each Town Center means you build fewer Houses during the boom.

## Imperial Age

Massed Elite Chu Ko Nu shred infantry, Skirmishers and even rams, because each extra bolt deals a small fixed amount of damage. Fully upgraded Arbalesters are cheaper to get going and nearly as good. Behind them, Rocket Carts and Heavy Scorpions with Rocketry punish clumped armies. Halberdiers are the cheapest front line against cavalry; Cavaliers and Light Cavalry deal with siege and raid. Elite Skirmishers are your trash archer once the gold runs out.

## Matchups

- Early aggression from civilizations like the Huns, Mongols, Aztecs or Goths is the biggest threat, because your bonuses arrive late. Wall early, and use the extra Town Center vision to see attacks coming.
- Siege Onagers and Bombard Cannons are the natural counter to massed Chu Ko Nu and Scorpions. Split your ranged units, keep Cavaliers or Light Cavalry ready to dive on the siege, and use your own Rocket Carts against the units protecting it.
- Cavalry Archer civilizations used to be handled with your own Heavy Cavalry Archers. Now the answer is Elite Skirmishers with Chu Ko Nu or Arbalesters behind a Halberdier screen.
- Monk-heavy opponents are annoying without Heresy. Light Cavalry and Chu Ko Nu kill Monks quickly.

## Common mistakes

- Leaving the Town Center idle at the start, or forgetting to queue Loom first.
- Forcing food drop offs every few seconds, which costs more than it gains.
- Building Houses too early. The Town Center gives 15 population, so the first House is due around 13 population.
- Playing too few lumberjacks after the start. You begin with 150 wood and need a Lumber Camp, a Mill and Houses soon.
- Skipping the Castle Age upgrades. The discount is the reason to play the Chinese, so research Blacksmith and unit upgrades early and often.
- Building no answer to siege. Without Bombard Cannons or Redemption, plan your cavalry before the enemy Onagers arrive.

title: How to Play the Cumans
summary: The Cumans can build a second Town Center and Battering Rams in the Feudal Age and have the fastest cavalry in the game. Learn when to boom, when to ram, and how to finish before their weak late game catches up with you.
body:
The Cumans are a cavalry civilization with the strangest Feudal Age in the game. They can build a second Town Center before Castle Age, they can make Battering Rams in the Feudal Age, and their Stables and Archery Ranges cost 75 wood less. Those tools give you a lot of early choices. The price is a thin late game, so the Cumans want to turn an early lead into a win before the Imperial Age.

## What the Cumans are good at

The headline bonus is the Feudal Age Town Center. It costs the usual 275 wood and 100 stone, and it takes 4 minutes 30 seconds for one villager to build, longer than a normal Town Center. Once it stands you produce villagers from two buildings while your opponent has one, and you can research Wheelbarrow or click Castle Age in one Town Center while the other keeps making villagers. A clean two Town Center boom reaches Castle Age around 19 to 20 minutes with 50 or more villagers, and from there you can add even more Town Centers or flood the map with cavalry.

Feudal Battering Rams are the second trick. The Siege Workshop and the Battering Ram are available in the Feudal Age, and the Capped Ram upgrade comes in Castle Age. Rams shrug off arrows and tear through palisades, gates and Town Centers, so they punish a player who walls up and goes for a fast Castle Age.

The cavalry itself is good. Mounted units move 5, 10 and 15 percent faster in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age, and the Stable has Paladin, Hussar, Steppe Lancer and every cavalry technology except Husbandry, which the speed bonus replaces. The only Stable unit upgrade they miss is the Heavy Camel Rider. Steppe Husbandry at the Castle trains the Scout Cavalry line, Steppe Lancers and Cavalry Archers twice as fast. The unique unit, the Kipchak, is a cheap mounted archer that fires several arrows per shot.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

The Cumans have no Arbalester, Hand Cannoneer or Bombard Cannon, and no Bracer for their archers. They cannot build Stone Walls, Guard Towers or Keeps. Their Monks miss Redemption, Illumination, Block Printing and Theocracy, and the navy is weak. Without Siege Engineers, the late siege is average. This is why the civilization falls off: in a long game against a strong Imperial Age civilization you run out of good answers. In early 2026 Hera even made a video arguing that the Cumans were the weakest civilization on the ladder at the time.

## Openings that suit them

- The Feudal second Town Center boom, written up as "Cumans Feudal Second Town Center Boom". It is the signature Cuman build, strong against players who fast Castle or boom, and weak against an early all in.
- Scouts into Feudal rams, written up as "Cumans Scouts into Feudal Rams". Cheap Stables let you open Scout Cavalry, then rams break walls and threaten the Town Center.
- Archers with two cheap ranges. The 75 wood discount lets you reach two Archery Ranges a little faster than most civilizations.
- Scouts or archers first and a second Town Center behind them, once the opponent is pinned at home.

## Castle Age plan

After a boom, the classic follow up is Knights from two or three Stables, or Steppe Lancers. Steppe Lancers hit from a short reach, cut through buildings quickly and train twice as fast with Steppe Husbandry. Light Cavalry and Hussars with Steppe Husbandry make cheap raiders that can be replaced faster than the enemy kills them.

Cavalry Archers and Kipchaks are the ranged option. Kipchaks are cheap, trained at the Castle, and do well against slow infantry and Pikemen. They need Fletching, Bodkin Arrow and Bloodlines to work. Capped Rams stay useful all game, both to break buildings and to absorb Castle arrows while your cavalry fights.

## Imperial Age plan

Your fully upgraded units are Paladins, Hussars and Halberdiers, plus Heavy Cavalry Archers and Elite Kipchaks without Bracer. Siege Rams and Siege Onagers support them. Keep raiding in several places with fast Hussars and Paladins, because a straight fight against a fully upgraded army with gunpowder is where the Cumans lose. Cuman Mercenaries lets your teammates train five free Elite Kipchaks per Castle, which is mostly a team game technology.

## Matchups

- Early aggressive civilizations such as the Aztecs, Britons, Mongols or Huns hurt the two Town Center boom, because the second Town Center takes a long time to build and the money spent on it is not an army. Scout your opponent before you commit, and switch to a scout or archer opening when you see an early Barracks or Archery Range.
- Fast Castle and boom civilizations are the targets. Feudal rams or a second Town Center both punish a slow, greedy Feudal Age.
- Strong late game civilizations such as the Spanish, Portuguese, Bohemians or Teutons beat the Cumans in long games. Close the game in Castle Age or keep them under constant raids.
- Camel and Pikemen heavy civilizations blunt your cavalry. Mix in Kipchaks or Cavalry Archers and some infantry.

## Common mistakes

- Booming blind. Build the second Town Center only after you know your opponent is not rushing, and wall around it.
- Building the second Town Center with one villager. Put four or five builders on it so it is done in about two minutes.
- Letting a Town Center sit idle. The whole boom depends on both buildings working all the time.
- Sending rams without an escort. Villagers with Loom and any melee unit kill rams quickly, so bring cavalry or infantry along.
- Playing a slow Imperial Age game. Your tech tree gets worse the longer the game goes, so attack while your economy lead is fresh.
