title: How to Play the Danes
summary: The Danes from The Viking Sagas are an infantry and siege civilization that profits from every building it destroys. Here is how to open with Men-at-Arms, turn raids into resources and build a Castle and Imperial Age army around siege, Mounted Crossbowmen and Halberdiers.
body:
The Danes arrived with The Viking Sagas in September 2026. They are listed as an infantry and siege civilization, and in practice they reward the player who keeps attacking: every enemy building they knock down pays them back part of its cost.

## What the Danes are good at

- Villagers and Fishing Ships drop off 5% more food. It works much like the Roman gathering bonus, but only for food, and it makes the early game smoother and farming cheaper later on.
- Units and buildings loot 25% of the cost of every enemy building they destroy. A Farm gives you 15 wood, a Lumber Camp about 25, and a Watch Tower pays out stone. Foundations count too, at 25% of what the owner would not get back by deleting them, and since Update 188329 walls and gates count as well.
- Barracks and Siege Workshop technologies cost 66% less gold. The Man-at-Arms upgrade costs about 14 gold, and late upgrades such as Siege Onager and Siege Ram become very affordable.
- Varangian Guards and Longships move 10% faster, and the team bonus gives land siege +2 line of sight.

The unique unit is the Jomsviking, a cheap Castle infantry unit (65 food, 15 gold) with large bonus damage against cavalry and buildings. Against buildings and ships it throws a torch from 3 range, which lets a group of them burn down a Town Center in seconds. Hamask, the Castle Age unique technology, gives infantry +1 attack for every 10% of hit points they have lost. Northmen's Fury in the Imperial Age gives the Mangonel line +1 range and all siege 40% more attack against buildings, but it costs 950 wood and 900 gold, so it is a late game purchase.

The Danes also get the northern regional units: the Varangian Guard at the Barracks, the Mounted Crossbowman at the Archery Range (fully upgradeable, with Cranequins), the Longship at the Dock and the Catapult Galleon. Missing pieces are the Arbalester, Cavalier, Hussar, Hand Cannoneer and Bombard Cannon, plus Two-Man Saw, Crop Rotation, Architecture and Fortified Wall. Their Monks lack Atonement, Heresy and Faith, so expensive siege can be converted.

The win condition follows from all this. Pressure early, hit buildings whenever villagers run away, and push with siege in the Castle Age so that every Farm and camp you destroy funds your next unit.

## Openings that suit the Danes

Men-at-Arms is the opening most players use, because it combines three bonuses at once: the extra food gets you up quickly, the upgrade is cheap in gold, and the Men-at-Arms can burn down a Lumber Camp or a Stable when the villagers hide. The full build is Danes Men-at-Arms into Skirmishers on this site. Follow it with Skirmishers against archers, or archers against cavalry openings. Both Hera and DragonstarAoE prefer Skirmishers as the default because they cost food and wood, which the food bonus covers well.

## Castle Age plan

Build a Siege Workshop as soon as you arrive. A single Battering Ram or two Mangonels next to the enemy farms gets far more value for the Danes than for anyone else, because each Farm destroyed costs the opponent 60 wood and gives you 15.

For the army, Mounted Crossbowmen are a strong choice. They hit hard but reload slowly, so move between shots. They are good at sniping Farms and Knights, and the Danes can give them Bloodlines, Husbandry and Thumb Ring in the Castle Age and Cranequins in the Imperial Age. Knights make a mobile front line; DragonstarAoE prefers them to Varangian Guards in the Castle Age. Jomsvikings are the answer when the opponent goes Knights, and they are the best building killers you have.

Add Town Centers behind your pressure. The Danes are comfortable booming once the opponent is busy defending.

## Imperial Age plan

The late game army is Halberdiers and Varangian Guards with Hamask in front, Heavy Mounted Crossbowmen or Elite Skirmishers behind, and Siege Onagers or Siege Rams to break walls and castles. The cheap gold on infantry and siege upgrades means you get there faster than most. Elite Jomsvikings are expensive to unlock (825 food, 825 gold) but a raiding party of 20 can delete a Town Center if the opponent looks away, which is very strong in team games and on Arena.

Buy Northmen's Fury only when the game is long and you are making a lot of siege.

## Matchups and what gives the Danes trouble

- Mounted archers and Hand Cannoneers beat Danish infantry and Jomsvikings. Answer with Skirmishers, Mounted Crossbowmen or Mangonels.
- Heavy infantry such as Teutonic Knights, Samurai and Jaguar Warriors beat Jomsvikings. Use Halberdiers with Hamask, ranged units, or siege.
- Cataphracts block the anti cavalry bonus of Jomsvikings and deal bonus damage to infantry.
- Monk civilizations can convert your Onagers since you lack Faith and Heresy. Keep Light Cavalry or Mounted Crossbowmen near the siege to kill Monks.
- Archer civilizations without good cavalry suffer against Skirmishers and Mangonels, which you do well.

## Common mistakes with the Danes

- Chasing loot instead of villagers. Hit buildings when the villagers are safe; kill villagers when you can reach them.
- Massing Jomsvikings against archers. They are an anti cavalry and anti building unit, and arrows still shred them.
- Forgetting that the economy lacks Two-Man Saw and Crop Rotation. Plan more woodcutters and reseed farms on time.
- Buying Northmen's Fury early. Siege Engineers and the Onager upgrade come first.
- Parking expensive siege where enemy Monks can reach it.

title: How to Play the Dravidians
summary: Dravidians get 200 wood with every age up, half price Barracks technologies and fast firing Skirmishers and Elephant Archers. This guide covers the Men-at-Arms into Archers opening, the Castle Age choices and why they get stronger the longer the game goes.
body:
The Dravidians are an infantry and archer civilization from the Dynasties of India expansion. They get a lump of wood every time they reach a new age, pay half price for Barracks technologies, and have faster firing Skirmishers and Elephant Archers. Their Stable is the weakest in the game, so they win by holding the map with foot units and strong siege, and they scale very well into the Imperial Age.

## What the Dravidians are good at

- You receive 200 wood each time you advance to the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age. In Feudal that pays for an Archery Range on the spot; in the Castle Age it covers most of a Town Center.
- Barracks technologies cost half, including the Man-at-Arms and Long Swordsman upgrades, Supplies, Squires and Arson.
- Skirmishers and Elephant Archers attack 25% faster. Dravidian Elite Skirmishers are among the best in the game against archers.
- Siege units cost a third less wood, and the siege workshop is nearly complete: Siege Onager, Heavy Scorpion, Bombard Cannon and the Armored Elephant line instead of rams.
- Fishermen and Fishing Ships carry 15 more food per trip, which makes Dravidians strong on water maps. The team bonus gives each Dock 5 population.
- Wootz Steel lets infantry and cavalry attacks ignore armor, which turns Champions and Urumi Swordsmen into fierce late game units. Medical Corps makes elephants heal over time.

The win condition is to survive the early cavalry pressure with Spearmen and Skirmishers, take the map with archers and infantry, and win the late game with Champions, Arbalesters, Elephant Archers and siege.

## Openings that suit them

The standard land opening is the Dravidians Men-at-Arms into Archers build on this site. The cheap Man-at-Arms upgrade makes a three Men-at-Arms harass almost free, and the 200 wood you receive on reaching Feudal builds the first Archery Range right away. Survivalist covers this exact plan, and it is a safe default on Arabia.

Hera also shows a Drush into Fast Castle with two Archery Ranges and an extra Town Center, which uses the Castle Age wood bonus. On water maps, put more villagers on fish and Fishing Ships than you normally would, because each trip brings back more food.

Scouts are a poor opening. Dravidians cap out at Light Cavalry without Bloodlines, so any Stable investment has no follow up.

## Castle Age plan

In the Castle Age you have three good options.

- Crossbowmen with Elite Skirmishers and Pikemen. This is the safe all round army and it handles most Castle Age threats.
- Elephant Archers. They fire 25% faster for Dravidians, they have lots of hit points and they beat archers and infantry. They are slow and expensive in gold, and Pikemen, Monks and Camel Riders counter them, so they work best as a second line behind Pikemen.
- Urumi Swordsmen from the Castle. Their charged attack hits several units at once, which is strong against groups of infantry and archers. They are fragile, so use them in short pushes with siege support.

Use the 200 wood from the age up for a second Town Center, and boom while your army holds the front. Mangonels and Armored Elephants cost less wood, so add them early when the opponent masses archers or builds towers.

## Imperial Age plan

Dravidians are one of the strongest late game civilizations. Their Champions and Halberdiers get every upgrade, Wootz Steel lets them cut through armored units like Paladins and Elite Teutonic Knights, and Arbalesters, Hand Cannoneers and fast firing Elite Skirmishers cover the ranged side. Siege Onagers, Bombard Cannons and Siege Elephants are all available. The usual end game army is Champions or Halberdiers in front, Arbalesters or Elite Elephant Archers behind and a few Siege Onagers. TheViper has a full video on why the civilization scales so well into the late game.

## Matchups

Ladder statistics show Dravidians struggle most against Khitans, Franks, Khmer, Malay, Romans and Chinese. The pattern is heavy cavalry and strong siege.

- Against Knights and Paladins (Franks, Khitans), mass Pikemen and later Halberdiers with full Barracks upgrades, which cost you half. Add Monks in the Castle Age, and get Wootz Steel in the Imperial Age so your Champions beat cavalry too.
- Against Battle Elephants (Khmer, Malay), Halberdiers and Monks are the answer. Keep the infantry upgrades current; they are cheap for you.
- Against strong siege and Scorpions (Romans, Khmer, Chinese), do not clump your infantry. Spread out, use Champions or a small group of Light Cavalry to snipe Scorpions and Mangonels, and bring Bombard Cannons of your own.
- Against archer civilizations you are in good shape: Elite Skirmishers firing 25% faster and Elephant Archers win most of those fights.

## Common mistakes

- Making cavalry. Dravidian Light Cavalry has no Bloodlines, and Battle Elephants never get the Elite upgrade, so Stable units are for scouting and sniping siege only.
- Forgetting the age up wood. Plan where the 200 wood goes before you click up, usually an Archery Range in Feudal and a Town Center in the Castle Age.
- Clumping Elephant Archers. They are slow, so Mangonels and Monks punish a tight group.
- Skipping Barracks upgrades. They cost half, so Squires, Supplies and Arson are cheap enough to get in every game where you make infantry.
- Ignoring the water. On maps with fish, the extra carry capacity is a big economic edge, and a Dock costs you only wood.

title: How to Play the Ethiopians
summary: Fast firing Archers, free resources at every age up and the best siege in the game. How to win with an early archer rush, carry the lead into Crossbowmen and finish with Arbalesters and Siege Onagers.
body:
The Ethiopians are an archer civilization with a strong late game siege workshop. Their bonuses are simple. The Archer line fires 18 percent faster, every new age gives you 100 food and 100 gold for free, and the Pikeman upgrade costs nothing. Their team bonus makes Outposts free and gives them extra line of sight.

## What the Ethiopians are good at

Faster firing works like extra attack, so Ethiopian Archers win even archer fights and shred Spearmen and villagers in the Feudal Age. The free resources make every age up cheaper in practice. The 100 gold you get on reaching the Feudal Age pays for your first two Archers without a single gold miner, and the Castle Age bonus covers most of the Crossbowman upgrade.

Later, they are the one civilization with every Siege Workshop unit and every upgrade for it, including Siege Onager, Heavy Scorpion, Siege Ram and Bombard Cannon. Torsion Engines, their Imperial Age unique technology, makes the splash of those units much larger. A fully upgraded Ethiopian Onager deletes clumps of infantry and archers that other Onagers only damage.

The weak spots are just as clear. Their cavalry lacks Bloodlines and Plate Barding Armor, there is no Paladin and no Champion, and they have no Hand Cannoneer. The Monastery lacks Redemption and Block Printing. Their economy has no lasting bonus, so if the early archer pressure does nothing, a civilization with a better boom pulls ahead in the Imperial Age.

The win condition is early pressure that turns into a lead you never give back. Hit in the Feudal Age with Archers, keep the pressure with Crossbowmen and free Pikemen, and close the game with Arbalesters and siege before the opponent's late game units arrive.

## Openings

- Ethiopians Archers (20 pop, two ranges) is the build on this site. Thanks to the free gold you click up with 19 villagers and far fewer miners than a normal archer rush, which puts Archers in the opponent's base before most opponents expect them. Hera's archer rush video and Morley Games' 20 pop build show how fast it can go.
- Men-at-Arms into Archers is a solid alternative, since the free food and gold soften the cost of the Dark Age militia.
- A Fast Castle is possible on closed maps. The free resources on arrival pay for a few Crossbowmen and Pikemen right away.

In team games, Age of Notes lists an 18 villager two range build that goes all in on the flank, relying on your pocket's cavalry to deal with enemy Skirmishers.

## Castle Age plan

Click up to the Castle Age with around 30 villagers while your Archers keep the opponent busy. When the age lands, the free 100 food and 100 gold go straight into the Crossbowman upgrade. Get Bodkin Arrow, Thumb Ring and Padded Archer Armor as you can afford them, and add a second or third Town Center behind the army.

Pikemen are free for you and they cover the Crossbowman's weak spot against Knights. Against Skirmishers, make a few Knights or Mangonels; your Knights lack Bloodlines and the last armor upgrade, but they still beat Skirmishers. Mangonels are also your answer to the enemy's massed archers.

The Shotel Warrior is the Castle unique unit. It costs 50 food and 30 gold, trains in a few seconds and hits very hard, but it has almost no armor and dies quickly to arrows. Use Shotels to raid an undefended economy, to kill rams that approach your Castle, or as instant defense when you are caught without an army. Royal Heirs makes Shotels and your Camel Riders take less damage from cavalry. They are a support unit and should not make up your main army.

## Imperial Age

The Imperial Age bonus helps with Arbalester. Your late army is Arbalesters with Halberdiers in front and siege behind. Siege Onagers with Torsion Engines are the strongest answer to infantry civilizations and to massed archers, and Bombard Cannons handle buildings and enemy siege. Torsion Engines is expensive, so research it once siege is a real part of your army.

When gold runs out, Halberdiers, Elite Skirmishers and Hussars are your trash units. Your Camel Riders stop at Heavy Camel Rider, so use them as a Castle Age answer to cavalry and stop making them later.

## Matchups

- Skirmisher civilizations and fast Mangonels make archer play hard. Answer Skirmishers with Knights or Men-at-Arms, and split your Archers when a Mangonel shows up while a few melee units charge it.
- Archer mirrors with the Britons, Maya or Vietnamese come down to micro and upgrades. Your faster fire helps, but their range or hit points can win. Get Fletching and Bodkin early and add Skirmishers if the fight stalls.
- Strong cavalry civilizations with Paladins beat your army if you lack Pikemen. Pikemen are free for you and Halberdier is in the tree, so keep a solid line of them.
- Infantry civilizations like the Goths or Japanese in the Imperial Age are where Siege Onagers with Torsion Engines earn their price.
- Cavalry Archer civilizations outrun your foot army. Use Skirmishers, a few Camel Riders and towers, and push them with Onagers and Rams into fights.

## Common mistakes

- Clicking Feudal with the usual 22 or 23 villagers. The free gold is what lets you go up earlier, so use it.
- Spending the Castle Age bonus on random units instead of the Crossbowman upgrade.
- Making Shotel Warriors as the main army. They die to Crossbowmen and towers.
- Staying on one Town Center after the rush. Without an economic bonus you need the extra Town Centers to keep up.
- Forgetting siege. The Ethiopian late game is built around it, and Arbalesters alone lose to a good mix of Skirmishers and Onagers.

title: How to Play the Franks
summary: Franks have the sturdiest Knights in the game, free farming upgrades and faster berry gathering, which makes them one of the easiest civilizations to learn. This guide covers their scout and fast castle openings, the Paladin late game and what to do when the opponent masses Halberdiers.
body:
## What the Franks are good at

Franks are the straightforward cavalry civilization. All their mounted units get 20% more hit points from the Feudal Age on, so Scout Cavalry, Knights, Cavaliers and Paladins outlast the same units of almost every other civilization. They miss Bloodlines, but the bonus is bigger than Bloodlines would be, and you save the research.

The economy is just as simple. Foragers work 15% faster, so a Mill on berries feeds a lot of the Dark Age. Horse Collar, Heavy Plow and Crop Rotation are free, which saves 75 food and 75 wood in the Feudal Age and much more later. Castles are 15% cheaper in the Castle Age and 25% cheaper in the Imperial Age, so a Frankish Castle on a gold pile or a forward hill is easy to afford. The team bonus gives Knights +2 Line of Sight.

The unique unit is the Throwing Axeman, an infantry unit from the Castle that throws axes at range 5 (6 as Elite) and deals melee damage. Since The Viking Sagas the old Bearded Axe tech is gone and Ordonnance Companies takes its place in the Castle Age: it cuts the gold cost of Mounted Crossbowmen by 40%. Franks now train Mounted Crossbowmen at the Archery Range instead of Cavalry Archers, and these get the 20% mounted hit point bonus too. The Imperial Age tech Chivalry makes Stables work 40% faster.

The weak spots are the Archery Range and siege. Franks have no Thumb Ring, Bracer or Ring Archer Armor, so foot archers stay poor. There is no Hussar, no Siege Ram and no Siege Onager, and the Monastery lacks Redemption and Atonement. Expect a gold-hungry late game built around Paladins, Champions or Halberdiers, Throwing Axemen and Bombard Cannons.

## Openings that suit them

The fast castle into Knights is the classic Frankish plan, and the free Horse Collar makes it faster than for other civilizations (see the build Franks Fast Castle Knights). Morley Games plays a version that reaches Castle Age around 12:45; the 26+2 build on this site lands a little later with more room for mistakes.

Scout rushes are the other common start. Morley's 19 population scout rush puts seven villagers on berries, uses the foraging bonus to feed early Scout Cavalry, and hits before most opponents finish their walls (see the build Franks 19 Pop Scouts). Frankish Scouts have enough hit points to fight a couple of Spearmen when they outnumber them.

Frankish foot archers are weak (Spirit Of The Law grades their Archery Range C minus), so if you need to fight archers in the Feudal Age, use Scouts and Skirmishers.

## Castle Age plan

Knights from two or three Stables are the default. Franks have no Bloodlines to research, so the first upgrades are Forging and Scale Barding Armor at the Blacksmith. Raid with all your Knights together and keep the Town Center making villagers.

When the opponent answers with Pikemen, add Throwing Axemen from a Castle, or Mounted Crossbowmen with Ordonnance Companies; both shoot from range and do not fight Pikemen in melee. A Castle at your gold pays for itself on open maps because the discount makes it cheap and it covers the villagers that pay for the Knights.

## Imperial Age plan

Research Paladin early; Chivalry speeds up the Stable, which also shortens the long Paladin upgrade. Paladins with full armor and the 20% bonus beat most other cavalry in straight fights. Add Elite Throwing Axemen or Champions and Halberdiers when the opponent goes for Halberdiers and camels, and Bombard Cannons or Trebuchets for buildings. Heavy Mounted Crossbowmen with Ordonnance Companies give you a ranged unit that moves with the Paladins.

## Matchups

Franks win a little over half their 1v1 random map games according to AoE2Insights. Their worst results come against Danes, Khitans, Romans, Armenians, Teutons and Malay, and their best against Muisca, Varangians, Britons, Dravidians, Khmer and Portuguese.

Most of the hard matchups have cheap, well-armored infantry or very good Halberdiers. Romans, Armenians and Teutons all field Pikemen and Halberdiers that trade well against Knights, and Malay have cheap Halberdiers. Against them, keep Knights for raiding and switch the main army to Throwing Axemen, Hand Cannoneers or Mounted Crossbowmen, and use Bombard Cannons against the infantry clumps.

Against archer civilizations such as Britons, Knights from the start of the Castle Age catch the archers before they reach large numbers, and the hit point bonus wins that fight. DauT's guide to the Franks walks through separate plans against cavalry and archer civilizations for every age.

## Common mistakes

- Going Knights into a wall of Pikemen. Switch to ranged units or Bombard Cannons when you see massed spears.
- Building Archers in the Feudal Age. Frankish foot archers are weak; use Scouts and Skirmishers instead.
- Looking for Bloodlines. Franks do not have it, so go straight to Forging and the Barding armor.
- Letting the gold run out. Paladins and Throwing Axemen both cost gold, so take map gold early and use Relics.
- Skipping a Castle. Frankish Castles are cheap and give the Knights a safe base to fall back to.

title: How to Play the Georgians
summary: Georgians start with a Mule Cart, raid with regenerating cavalry and boom behind Fortified Churches. This guide covers the fast Scout opening, Knights and Monaspas in the Castle Age, the Imperial Age deathball and how to avoid the classic Mule Cart mistakes.
body:
The Georgians are a cavalry and defense civilization from The Mountain Royals with an unusual start. Instead of building Lumber Camps and Mining Camps, they use Mule Carts, mobile drop sites for wood, gold, stone and hunted meat, and they begin the game with one. Their mounted units regenerate 2, 8 and 14 hit points per minute in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Ages. Fortified Churches replace the Monastery and give villagers nearby 10% faster work. Units and buildings on higher ground take 20% less damage on top of the normal hill bonus. The plan is simple to say: raid with cavalry that heals between fights, boom behind churches, and fight on the hills.

## What the Georgians do well

- Cavalry. Full Cavaliers and Hussars, Bloodlines and every armor upgrade. Regeneration means a group of Knights can raid, retreat and come back healthy without Monks.
- The Monaspa. This Castle unit gets stronger when other Monaspas or Knight line units are near it. Mixed with Knights it adds damage to the whole group.
- Economy in the Castle Age. A Fortified Church next to your farms boosts every villager in a large square around it, and the Mule Cart follows the woodline as trees fall.
- Defense. Svan Towers give defensive buildings +2 attack and let towers shoot arrows that pass through units. A Keep or Castle on a hill is very hard to take.

The archery range is weak: no Thumb Ring, no Ring Archer Armor and no Arbalester, so Hand Cannoneers are the only good foot ranged unit. The navy is poor. The Siege Workshop has Siege Onagers and Siege Rams but no Bombard Cannon.

## Openings

Georgians Scouts (17 pop), the build on this site, is the default. The Mule Cart counts as one of the two Dark Age buildings you need for Feudal Age, so you only build a Mill. Put every villager on food, click up very early, then send most of them to wood during the age up to pay for the Stable and Double-Bit Axe. The Mule Cart doubles as a second scout in the first minutes; Survivalist uses it to find the opponent while the Scout Cavalry pushes deer.

A fast Castle Age into Knights or Monaspas is the other main plan, especially on closed maps. The Mule Cart saves the wood other civilizations spend on camps, so you can click up a little earlier than usual.

## Castle Age plan

Knights are the standard Castle Age unit. Make them from two or three Stables, keep raiding and pull back before Pikemen or Camels catch you; the regeneration does the rest. Build a Fortified Church (200 wood) in the middle of your farms as soon as you can afford it, and a second one at your next Town Center. Monaspas come from the Castle and cost less gold than Knights; a large enough group of Monaspas and Knights together hits much harder than either alone.

Against archers, Knights and Light Cavalry are enough. Against Pikemen and Camels, switch to Hand Cannoneers or Long Swordsmen for a while, or bring Mangonels. Siege Rams later and Onagers give the army a way into a walled base. Get Svan Towers when you expect to defend, since it makes Town Centers and towers much more dangerous.

## Imperial Age

The Georgian late game is a heavy mounted army: Cavaliers and Elite Monaspas, Siege Onagers and Siege Rams, Keeps with Svan Towers to hold ground, and Fortified Churches for Monks if the opponent relies on gold units. Aznauri Cavalry makes mounted units take 20% less population space, so a full population army has noticeably more horses in it. Hussars and Halberdiers keep you fighting when gold runs out.

## Matchups

- Camel and Pikeman civilizations such as Saracens, Hindustanis and Byzantines blunt Knights. Mix in Hand Cannoneers, Champions or Onagers, and keep raiding instead of attacking into the counters.
- Mass archer civilizations late in the game are hard because you cannot answer with Arbalesters. Use Cavaliers, Hussars and Siege Onagers, and fight near your hills.
- Monk civilizations can convert your expensive cavalry. Light Cavalry or Hussars hunt Monks well.
- Early aggression, especially Men-at-Arms or Scouts that go for the Mule Cart, can cost you the whole wood economy. Protect it.

## Common mistakes

- Losing the Mule Cart. It has 300 hit points and does not run away. Keep it behind your woodcutters and garrison it if the enemy reaches it. A new one costs 80 wood and 20 food.
- Forgetting the Mill. The Mule Cart is only one of the two buildings needed for Feudal Age.
- Placing Fortified Churches away from farms or wood. The bonus only works in the square around the building.
- Fighting on flat ground when a hill is near. The extra damage reduction is a real advantage.
- Copying a standard build without adjusting. Georgians need fewer wood villagers early, and the Mule Cart moves with the trees, so your woodline never drifts far from the drop site.

title: How to Play the Goths
summary: The Goths flood the map with cheap infantry and Huskarls, and they get stronger with every age. How to open, how to survive the Castle Age and how to set up the Imperial Age infantry spam, plus the matchups that give them trouble.
body:
The Goths are the infantry flood civilization. Their infantry gets cheaper with every age, their Barracks work faster, and in the Imperial Age they get ten extra population and Perfusion, which doubles Barracks speed. A Goth player who survives to the Imperial Age with a working economy can replace losses faster than almost anyone. They are a good civilization to learn with, because the plan is simple and a lot of their power comes from producing units, which beginners already practise.

## What the Goths are good at

Goth infantry is 15% cheaper in the Dark Age, 20% in the Feudal Age, 25% in the Castle Age and 30% in the Imperial Age. Their infantry also gets +1, +2 and +3 attack against standard buildings in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Ages, so Men-at-Arms and Long Swordsmen take down houses, towers and Town Centers quickly. The team bonus makes Barracks work 20% faster, and that applies to you as well.

The economic bonuses are small but real. Hunters carry 15 more food and hunt lasts 20% longer, so maps with boar and deer are better for you. Loom is researched instantly, which saves about 25 seconds of Town Center time compared to other civilizations.

The Huskarl is one of the best anti-archer units in the game. It has very high pierce armor and a big attack bonus against archers. With Anarchy you can train Huskarls at the Barracks, so you are not limited to Castles. Late in the game, Perfusion and the +10 population cap let you keep a huge infantry army on the field.

The weaknesses are just as important. Goth infantry lacks Gambesons and Plate Mail Armor, so each unit is fragile; you win with numbers. There is no Arbalester or Thumb Ring, no Paladin, no Siege Ram and no Siege Onager. Defenses are poor: no Guard Tower, no Keep, no Bombard Tower and no Fortified Wall. Monks miss Redemption, Block Printing and Atonement. The Viking Sagas patch gave the Goths Treadmill Crane back.

## Openings that suit them

- Goths Men-at-Arms (civ-goths-men-at-arms) uses cheap Militia, instant Loom and faster Barracks for an early hit that you can keep feeding with more infantry.
- Goths Scouts with Hunt (civ-goths-scouts-hunt) is for maps with deer. The hunting bonus gives you enough food for a fast Feudal Age and a good number of Scout Cavalry.
- A forward Barracks Militia rush with a stolen boar, as Capoch plays it, is a riskier option for players who like messy games.

## Castle Age plans

The Castle Age is where the Goths are weakest. Their discount is good but their infantry still lacks armor, and a Castle Age Knight or Crossbowman army can beat Long Swordsmen. Keep the army mixed. Long Swordsmen and Pikemen in front, Skirmishers against archers, and a Castle for Huskarls once the opponent commits to archers. The Goths have Bloodlines and Husbandry, so a few Knights are a fine way to defend raids in this age.

Spend the Castle Age getting your economy ready for the Imperial Age: two or three more Town Centers, Wheelbarrow, Bow Saw and Gold Mining. Then click up with three or four Barracks already built.

## Imperial Age

This is the age the Goths play for. Research Perfusion, add Barracks until you have six or more, and get Anarchy so every Barracks can train Huskarls. A typical army is Huskarls against archers, Halberdiers against cavalry and Champions against infantry, with Hand Cannoneers behind. Bombard Cannons kill the Onagers that would otherwise shred your infantry blob. With the +10 population cap and cheap units, trading two of your units for one of theirs is a good trade.

## Matchups

Strong infantry civilizations are a problem because they beat Goth infantry one on one and do not fall behind in numbers as fast as others. On AoE2Insights the Goths' worst ladder matchups are Vikings, Malians, Romans, Celts, Japanese and Teutons. Celt Siege Onagers are especially bad for a Goth blob. Against these civilizations, rely more on Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons and avoid fighting under Onagers.

Unique heavy cavalry and melee units, such as Cataphracts and Teutonic Knights, also trade well against Goth infantry. Answer Cataphracts with Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons, and keep Teutonic Knights busy with Hand Cannoneers and Huskarls.

Archer civilizations do poorly against Goths once Huskarls come out. The Goths' best matchups include Britons, Wei, Maya, Lithuanians, Koreans and Magyars.

## Common mistakes

- Turtling. Goth defenses are poor, so walls and towers will not hold a determined push. Defend with units and keep attacking.
- Too few Barracks. Cheap units do nothing if you cannot make them fast. Four Barracks in the late Castle Age and six or more in the Imperial Age is normal.
- Men-at-Arms against archers. Without Gambesons, Goth Militia line melts to arrows. Use Skirmishers and later Huskarls.
- Forgetting Loom. It is instant for you, so research it whenever you have 50 gold, for example while luring a boar.
- Running out of gold. Huskarls, Champions and Hand Cannoneers all need gold; take extra gold mines with your Town Centers and protect them.

title: How to Play the Gurjaras
summary: The Gurjaras win with a food economy built on forage bushes and sheep in the Mill, and with camels, Shrivamsha Riders and elephants that hit harder than anyone else's.
body:
## What the Gurjaras are good at

The Gurjaras start with two forage bushes under the Town Center, 175 food each, and a Camel Scout instead of Scout Cavalry. Their Mills can hold sheep and other herdables, which then produce a slow trickle of food for as long as they stay inside. Each extra animal adds a bit less than the one before, so the first few in a Mill give the most. Their mounted units deal 20% more bonus damage in the Feudal Age, 30% more in the Castle Age and 40% more in the Imperial Age, and the team bonus trains camel and elephant units 25% faster.

That bonus damage is why Gurjara camels and elephants feel so strong. A Camel Rider's bonus against cavalry, a Siege Elephant's bonus against buildings and the Hussar's bonus against Monks all grow with it. Kshatriyas, the Castle Age unique technology, cuts the food cost of every military unit by 25%, and Frontier Guards in the Imperial Age gives Camel Riders and Elephant Archers 4 more melee armor.

The unique units each have a narrow job. The Shrivamsha Rider is a fast Stable unit with a shield that dodges a few projectiles before it takes damage, which makes it the Gurjara answer to archers. The Chakram Thrower, from the Castle, throws discs that pass through every enemy in a line and wrecks packed infantry, Pikemen above all. The Camel Scout turns into a Camel Rider for free when you reach the Castle Age.

The gaps are large. There is no Knight line, no Battle Elephant, no Cavalry Archer, no Arbalester, no Champion and no Pikeman upgrade, and the Blacksmith lacks Blast Furnace and Ring Archer Armor. Rams are missing as well, so the Armored Elephant and Siege Elephant do that job. The Gurjaras want to end the game before the gold runs out, because their trash units are poor.

## Openings that suit them

The Gurjaras Scouts build on this site covers the unusual start: villagers on the bushes under the Town Center, sheep into a Mill at the main berries, and Scout Cavalry from the Feudal Age. A two Archery Range opening also works on open maps, and on closed maps like Arena a fast Castle Age into Camel Riders, Shrivamsha Riders or Elephant Archers is the common plan.

Decide early how many sheep to eat. Eating a sheep gives 100 food now; garrisoning it gives food slowly for the rest of the game. Aggressive builds eat most of them, booms keep more inside the Mill. Protect that Mill, because if it falls the animals come out and the opponent can take them.

## Castle Age plan

Research Kshatriyas as soon as your economy allows, since almost every Gurjara unit costs food. From there, pick by what the opponent makes:

- Against Knights and other cavalry, Camel Riders. Your Camel Scouts already became Camel Riders on reaching the age.
- Against archers, Shrivamsha Riders, which are also fast enough to raid and catch Trade Carts.
- Against infantry, especially Pikemen and Spearmen that stop your cavalry, Chakram Throwers in a tight group.
- For a heavier push, Elephant Archers, which are cheap for the Gurjaras after Kshatriyas.

Add Armored Elephants when you need to take down towers or a Castle.

## Imperial Age

The Gurjaras peak here. Heavy Camel Riders with Frontier Guards hold the front against almost any cavalry, Elite Elephant Archers deal steady damage, Siege Elephants break buildings very fast, and Chakram Throwers plus Hand Cannoneers deal with infantry. Bombard Cannons and Hussars handle enemy siege. Keep your gold mines busy and look for a decisive fight before the map runs dry.

## Matchups

- Cavalry civilizations like the Franks, Huns or Lithuanians have a hard time, because Gurjara camels are among the best in the game.
- Fast infantry rushes and Men-at-Arms openings are the danger in the early game, since the Barracks is weak. Use towers, walls and Archers or Skirmishers until Chakram Throwers come online.
- Heavy infantry civilizations in the late game, such as the Goths or Malians, need Chakram Throwers and Hand Cannoneers. Do not try to fight them with Two-Handed Swordsmen.
- Strong archer civilizations like the Britons are handled by Shrivamsha Riders, but those riders lose to anything in melee, so keep Camel Riders close.
- Monks are a problem for elephants. Heresy is available, so research it before an elephant-heavy push.

## Common mistakes

- Putting every sheep into the Mill in a rush build, then running out of food for villagers in the Dark Age.
- Leaving the Mill full of sheep and unprotected while raiders roam.
- Making Militia-line units or Spearmen as a core army. They lack the upgrades to trade well.
- Sending Shrivamsha Riders into melee units. Their dodge works only against projectiles.
- Clumping Chakram Throwers under enemy Mangonels, or spreading them so far apart that the discs miss.
- Forgetting Kshatriyas, which is the single biggest saving in the Gurjara tech tree.

title: How to Play the Hindustanis
summary: Hindustani villagers get cheaper every age and their Camel Riders attack faster than anyone's. This guide covers safe openings, the Castle Age choice between camels, archers and Ghulams, and the Imperial army of camels and long range Hand Cannoneers.
body:
The Hindustanis are a camel and gunpowder civilization with one of the best economies for long games. Their villagers get cheaper with every age, their Camel Riders attack faster than anyone else's, and in the Imperial Age they field Imperial Camel Riders, Hand Cannoneers with extra range and armor, and Ghulams against archers. The plan is to stay safe and keep booming, then win a late game where each of your units has a clear job.

## What the Hindustanis are good at

Villagers cost 8 percent less food in the Dark Age, 13 percent in the Feudal Age, 18 percent in the Castle Age and 23 percent in the Imperial Age. That does not change your opening much, but it adds up: every extra Town Center pays off faster than usual, and you can keep making villagers much longer into the game. Aim for a large villager count, around 100 or more in a full population game.

Camel Riders attack 20 percent faster, and the Hindustani team bonus gives Camel Riders and the Scout Cavalry line +2 attack against buildings, which also helps your own Feudal scouts knock down houses and camps. Gunpowder units get +1 melee and +1 pierce armor, and Shatagni gives Hand Cannoneers +2 range. Grand Trunk Road speeds up all gold income by 10 percent and cuts the Market fee to 10 percent, so selling extra food or wood for gold works well. In the Imperial Age you can also build Caravanserais, which heal and speed up allied Trade Carts.

The Ghulam, trained at the Castle, is a fast spear infantry unit with high pierce armor whose attack also hits the unit behind its target. It shines against massed archers.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

The Hindustanis have no Knight line at all. Camel Riders do part of that job but have less pierce armor and less damage against non cavalry. The Archer line stops at Crossbowman, the Spearman line stops at Pikeman, and infantry lacks Plate Mail Armor. There are no rams; the Siege Elephant replaces them. Defenses lack Architecture and Keeps, the navy lacks Shipwright, Dry Dock and the Fast Fire Ship, and there is no Heresy, so expensive Imperial Camel Riders are easy targets for Monks.

## Openings that suit them

- Scout Cavalry, written up as "Hindustanis Scouts into Castle Age Camels". Cheap villagers let you keep the Town Center busy while you pay for a Stable and scouts, and the team bonus helps the scouts against buildings.
- Archers on open maps. You have every archer technology except the Arbalester upgrade and Parthian Tactics, so Feudal and Castle Age archers are solid.
- A drush or Men-at-Arms opening into a fast Castle Age when you want to boom early.
- On closed maps, a straight fast Castle Age into three Town Centers is often the best use of the villager discount.

## Castle Age plan

Decide your army from what you scout. Against cavalry, mass Camel Riders, which shred Knights with their fast attack. Against archers, use Skirmishers, a few Light Cavalry, and Ghulams once you have a Castle. Against a passive opponent, add Town Centers and keep both Town Centers and the army growing.

Cavalry Archers are a good mobile option because they are fully upgraded in the Castle Age, and they cover the lack of Knights against infantry. Monks are also strong: the Hindustanis have most Monastery technologies, and Monks help hold a Knight push while your economy grows. Keep Camel Riders away from Castles and towers; they have to get close and die quickly to building fire.

## Imperial Age plan

The late army is Imperial Camel Riders and Hand Cannoneers. The camels handle cavalry and elephants in moderate numbers, the Hand Cannoneers with Shatagni outrange most infantry and kill it from behind the camels, and Ghulams mixed in soak arrows and punish archers. Bombard Cannons with extra armor are the main siege, with Trebuchets against Castles. Hussars are your trash cavalry when gold runs out, together with Elite Skirmishers.

Keep villager production going far longer than feels normal. At 23 percent off, villagers are cheap enough to replace after raids and to push the population near half villagers.

## Matchups

- Armored infantry civilizations such as the Goths, Japanese, Malians or Aztecs are uncomfortable before the Imperial Age. You lack an armored melee answer, so lean on archers, Cavalry Archers and walls until Hand Cannoneers arrive.
- Battle Elephant civilizations such as the Khmer, Burmese and Vietnamese push into your camels, which have a smaller bonus against elephants than Halberdiers do. Use Monks and a large camel count, and fight near your Castles.
- Knight civilizations such as the Franks, Lithuanians and Persians are the matchup you want. Camels and Monks beat Knights, and you outlast them late.
- Mass archer civilizations are fine if you get Ghulams and Skirmishers out in time. Do not fight Crossbowmen with Camel Riders alone.

## Common mistakes

- Stopping villager production at 60 or 70. The discount rewards a bigger economy than you are used to.
- Building camels against an archer or infantry army because camels are the famous unit.
- Forgetting that you have no Heresy. Keep Light Cavalry or Hussars around to kill enemy Monks near your Imperial Camel Riders.
- Losing a water map. With a weak late navy, either fight early with Galleys or pick a land map plan.
- Skipping Grand Trunk Road. The extra gold income and cheap Market trades fund the gold heavy Imperial Age army.

title: How to Play the Huns
summary: The Huns never build Houses, train cavalry faster than anyone and get cheap Cavalry Archers. This guide explains how to turn that into nonstop pressure on open maps, when to make Tarkans, and what to avoid.
body:
The Huns are a cavalry civilization made for open land maps. Their economy never stalls on housing, their Stables work faster and their Cavalry Archers get cheaper as the game goes on. A good Hun player is always attacking somewhere.

## What the Huns are good at

- No Houses. The population cap starts at its maximum, so you never get housed. You start with 100 less wood to pay for it, but over a whole game you save several hundred wood and a lot of villager time that other civilizations spend on building Houses.
- Stables work 20% faster. That is the team bonus, and it speeds up your own Scout Cavalry, Knights and Tarkans.
- Mounted archers cost 10% less in the Castle Age and 20% less in the Imperial Age.
- Trebuchets have 35% more accuracy against units, which wins Trebuchet duels.

The unique unit is the Tarkan, a cavalry unit with high pierce armor and bonus damage against buildings. Marauders, the Castle Age unique technology, lets you train Tarkans at the Stable, so they come out of every Stable you own. Atheism in the Imperial Age slows down enemy Relic and Wonder victories and halves the gold enemies get from Relics.

The tech tree is generous for cavalry: fully upgraded Hussars, Paladins and Heavy Cavalry Archers with Parthian Tactics. Since The Viking Sagas the Huns are one of the civilizations that kept the Cavalry Archer, which makes them stand out more than before. The holes are in infantry (no Champion, no Plate Mail Armor), foot archers (no Arbalester, no Ring Archer Armor), siege (no Onager, Heavy Scorpion or Bombard Cannon, and no Siege Engineers), Monks (no Redemption, Block Printing or Theocracy) and defenses (no Keep, Guard Tower, Architecture or Fortified Wall).

Put together, the Huns want to win before the late game turns into Halberdiers and siege: map control in the Feudal Age, a big cavalry or Cavalry Archer push in the Castle Age, and Tarkans or Paladins to finish.

## Openings that suit the Huns

Almost every Feudal opening works because you skip Houses and keep villagers gathering. The two most common are written up on this site.

- Huns Scouts: Scout Cavalry from one or two fast Stables, then Knights or Cavalry Archers.
- Huns Fast Castle into Cavalry Archers: a faster Castle Age with two or three Archery Ranges of cheap Cavalry Archers.

Straight archers are also good on open maps, and a Drush into Fast Castle works when your base is easy to wall. Hera recommends avoiding the pre mill Drush, because you start the game with 100 less wood.

## Castle Age plan

Against archer civilizations, Knights from two or three Stables are the default and they come out 20% faster than usual. Against infantry or cavalry, Cavalry Archers with Thumb Ring, Ballistics and Bloodlines are the main army. Three Archery Ranges are realistic for the Huns because of the discount. Get Husbandry for speed and Parthian Tactics before the Imperial Age.

Research Marauders when you want Tarkans. They are a surprise tool against archer civilizations and a fast way to take down Town Centers and Castles. Do not wall heavily; your bonus makes Houses unnecessary, and your army is your defense.

## Imperial Age plan

Heavy Cavalry Archers with Hussars are the classic Hun late game. Paladins come in against archers and against armies that have few Halberdiers. Elite Tarkan is a fast upgrade that needs no Cavalier step, so it is a strong tech switch against Arbalesters. Add Siege Rams for buildings and Trebuchets for anything defended by Castles; your Trebuchets win duels thanks to their accuracy.

## Matchups and what gives the Huns trouble

- Halberdier and Skirmisher civilizations. The Huns lack good infantry and strong siege against massed Halberdiers, so keep your army on Cavalry Archers and raid where the pikes are not.
- Camel civilizations. Use Cavalry Archers or Hussar numbers rather than Knights.
- Closed maps such as Arena. Your weak defenses and siege make long sieges hard. Go Fast Castle with Knights or Cavalry Archers and boom; do not play a slow game into Bombard Cannons.
- Siege Ram pushes late in the game. You have no Onager or Bombard Cannon, so kill rams with Hussars, Paladins or Tarkans before they reach your Town Centers.
- Monk heavy opponents. Your Monks are weak, so make Light Cavalry to hunt theirs.

## Common mistakes with the Huns

- Forgetting that the base has no House walls. Use palisades early against a rush, especially around the woodline.
- Sitting at home. The no House bonus and fast Stables only pay off if you are pressuring.
- Making Champions or Arbalesters for the late game. The Huns do not have them.
- Skipping Thumb Ring and Parthian Tactics. Hun Cavalry Archers depend on those upgrades.
- Going into a long Imperial Age against civilizations with Siege Onagers and Halberdiers while your economy is behind.

title: How to Play the Inca
summary: Since The Last Chieftains the Inca play with Settlements, Champi Scouts and no cavalry. This guide covers the Champi drush that most Inca players open with, the Kamayuk, Champi Warrior and Slinger army, and how to handle infantry and siege heavy opponents.
body:
The Inca changed a lot with The Last Chieftains expansion. They now use the South American setup: the Settlement replaces the Mill, Lumber Camp and Mining Camp, the Champi Scout line replaces the Militia line and the Eagle Scout, and the civilization has no cavalry at all. What stayed is the core identity, an infantry civilization with cheap military food costs, tough villagers and Houses that hold twice the population.

## What the Inca are good at

- Military units cost 15% less food in the Dark Age, 20% in Feudal, 25% in the Castle Age and 30% in the Imperial Age. Champi Scouts, Spearmen, Kamayuks and Slingers all get cheaper as the game goes on.
- Houses and Settlements support 10 population. One House and one Settlement cover you until 25 population, which saves wood and builder time all game.
- Villagers receive the Blacksmith infantry armor and attack upgrades from the Castle Age on. Inca villagers win fights against light raiders and are hard to tower rush.
- Buildings cost 15% less stone, so towers, Castles and extra Town Centers are cheaper.
- You start with a free Llama, which is extra food under the Town Center.
- Fabric Shields gives Champi Warriors, Kamayuks and Slingers +1/+1 armor, and Andean Sling gives Slingers +1 attack and removes the minimum range of Slingers and Skirmishers.

The Settlement is a drop site for every resource and counts as two buildings for the Feudal Age requirement. It costs 125 wood and has more hit points than normal camps. You place fewer of them, so choose spots that touch two resources when you can.

## Openings that suit them

The opening most Inca players use right now is the Champi drush. Champi Scouts are the most produced Inca unit on the ladder by a wide margin. The Inca Instant Champi Drush build on this site spends the starting wood on a House and a Barracks right away, then sends three or four Champi Scouts with your starting Champi Scout to harass the opponent. The Champi Scout is a fast infantry unit with good pierce armor and a bonus against cavalry, and it can build Outposts. Your starting gold pays for the first four.

After the drush you have two common follow ups. One is Feudal pressure with the Champi Runner upgrade and archers or Skirmishers. The other is a fast Castle Age with Kamayuks and Slingers. On closed maps a straight Fast Castle into a boom is also fine, because the House bonus makes extra Town Centers cheap to support.

## Castle Age plan

Your Castle Age army is built from three parts.

- Kamayuks from the Castle. They have a short reach of one tile, a bonus against cavalry and, with Fabric Shields, good armor against arrows. They are the answer to Knights and Camel Riders.
- Champi Warriors from the Barracks. They are fast, they resist arrows and they have bonus damage against siege. Use them to raid, to kill Mangonels and to chase archers.
- Slingers from the Archery Range. They cost food and wood with no gold, and they shred infantry and Monks. Crossbowmen and Elite Skirmishers handle enemy archers.

Get a Castle early for Kamayuks and Fabric Shields; the stone discount brings the price down to about 550 stone. Add a second and third Town Center as your army holds the map. Your villagers start getting the infantry armor upgrades in this age, so Scale Mail Armor protects your economy as well as your army.

Siege Rams and Onagers are available. Use them against Castles and massed archers.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age the discount reaches 30% food, so a mass of Elite Kamayuks, Elite Champi Warriors and Slingers is very cheap to rebuild. Arbalesters with full upgrades and Halberdiers fill gaps. Siege Rams, Onagers, Heavy Scorpions and Trebuchets cover the siege side; there are no Bombard Cannons or Siege Onagers. Monks are good, and the Inca can take relics and heal their infantry. On water maps, Inca now have the Catapult Galleon and fully upgraded Galleons.

## Matchups

Ladder statistics show the hardest matchups for the Inca are Romans, Wu, Vikings, Celts, Jurchens and Shu. These civilizations bring strong infantry, strong siege or both.

- Against heavy infantry (Romans, Vikings), use Slingers in large numbers. Their bonus against infantry is big, and they cost no gold. Keep Kamayuks in front so the infantry has to walk through them.
- Against siege armies (Celts, Romans), Champi Warriors are your answer. Send a group around the side to kill Mangonels and Scorpions before they fire on your infantry.
- Against strong archers, Champi Warriors and Kamayuks with Fabric Shields take arrows well, and Elite Skirmishers back them up.
- Because you have no cavalry, mobile civilizations with Cavalry Archers can be hard to catch. Use Skirmishers and Champi Warriors, which are faster than most infantry, and fight near your towers and Castles.

## Common mistakes

- Placing the first Settlement badly. It is your only drop site apart from the Town Center, so put it where berries and wood or gold are close together.
- Building too many Houses. They hold 10 population each, so one House every 10 villagers is enough.
- Drushing without a follow up. The Champi drush is strong, but it delays your economy; decide before you send the Champis whether you go into Feudal archers or a fast Castle Age.
- Leaving villagers as targets in the Castle Age. With infantry armor upgrades they can fight back, so pull them together and attack small raiding groups instead of always garrisoning.
- Ignoring the Slinger. It costs no gold, and it is often the cheapest way to beat the opponent's infantry and Monks.

title: How to Play the Italians
summary: Cheaper age ups, tougher foot archers, discounted gunpowder and one of the best navies. How to use the Italian bonuses on land and water, when to make Genoese Crossbowmen and what to do about the missing Halberdier.
body:
The Italians are an archer and navy civilization with a strong Imperial Age. Advancing to the next age costs 15 percent less, foot archers (except Skirmishers) and Condottieri get +1 melee and +1 pierce armor, Dock and University technologies cost 25 percent less, Fishing Ships are 15 percent cheaper and gunpowder units cost 20 percent less. Their team bonus gives every ally the Condottiero at the Barracks.

## What the Italians are good at

The age up discount looks small but works in every game. The Feudal Age costs 425 food instead of 500, and the Castle Age 680 food and 170 gold. That is roughly one villager less in the Dark Age and an earlier Castle Age click with the same economy, without any special micro.

The archer armor is the land bonus you feel most. Italian Archers and Crossbowmen take less damage from enemy archers, Town Center arrows and towers, so they win even archer fights and can stay near a Town Center a little longer when raiding. Genoese Crossbowmen, the Castle unique unit, carry bonus damage against cavalry, camels and elephants and are one of the few ranged units that actually beat Knights.

In the Imperial Age, Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons are cheap, and Pirotechnia makes Hand Cannoneers accurate and lets their shots pass through to hit units behind the target. The Condottiero is a fast infantry unit that takes reduced bonus damage from gunpowder units and hits them hard, available at the Barracks with no upgrade.

The gaps: no Halberdier, no Paladin, no Camel Rider, no Heavy Cavalry Archer, no Siege Ram or Siege Onager, and no Siege Engineers. The Italians also have no economic bonus on land beyond the cheaper ages.

The win condition on land is a steady archer game that gets ahead on age timings, then a strong Imperial Age with Arbalesters, Hand Cannoneers and cheap Bombard Cannons. On water, you have a full Dock and pay less for every upgrade there, so you should own the sea.

## Openings

- Italians Archers (21 pop) uses the cheaper Feudal Age to put two ranges of armored Archers on the map a little earlier than a standard archer rush.
- Italians Water Galleys is the full water opening, with cheaper Fishing Ships and cheaper Dock upgrades.

For newer players, a 23 pop Feudal Age build with no deer pushing that goes into either Archers or Scout Cavalry also works well, and an AOE2 Builds video from 2026 shows exactly that with the Italians. A Fast Castle into a boom is fine on closed maps, since the Castle Age is cheaper for you.

## Castle Age plan

Crossbowmen with Bodkin Arrow and Thumb Ring are your core unit, and their extra armor lets them stand against enemy archers. Against Knights, add Pikemen early and build a Castle for Genoese Crossbowmen. Massed Genoese with a few Pikemen in front beat most cavalry armies, but they are expensive and weak against Skirmishers and infantry, so make them when cavalry shows up.

Your Stable has Cavaliers and Hussars with all the usual upgrades, so Knights are a good second unit when the opponent goes Skirmishers. Monks are good too.

Add Town Centers as soon as the army is safe. University technologies are a quarter cheaper, so Ballistics, Chemistry and Murder Holes all come early. Silk Road halves the cost of Trade Carts and Trade Cogs, which matters in team games with long trade routes.

## Imperial Age

Arbalesters, Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons form the main late army. Research Pirotechnia as soon as you have a group of Hand Cannoneers; without it they miss moving targets often. Bombard Cannons handle buildings and enemy siege, and you can afford more of them than most civilizations.

Without Halberdiers, your answer to late cavalry is Genoese Crossbowmen, Pikemen and Cavaliers. Condottieri are the answer to enemy gunpowder: Janissaries, Hand Cannoneers, Conquistadors or Organ Guns melt in front of them. They are also fast enough to raid with.

## On water

Fishing Ships cost about 64 wood instead of 75, so the fishing boom is cheaper from the first minute. Gillnets, Careening, Dry Dock, Shipwright and the War Galley and Galleon upgrades all cost a quarter less, and Cannon Galleons get the gunpowder discount. Italians usually win an even water fight because they reach every upgrade sooner. On hybrid maps, use the cheaper fish and the extra wood to fight for the water first, and only then put your land army in place.

## Matchups

- Paladin civilizations like the Franks, Lithuanians or Persians are dangerous late because you lack Halberdiers. Build Castles and Genoese early, and keep Pikemen in the army.
- Skirmisher heavy armies blunt both Crossbowmen and Genoese. Switch to Knights in the Castle Age and to Hand Cannoneers and Hussars in the Imperial Age.
- Cavalry Archer civilizations such as the Mongols, Huns or Magyars outrun your foot army. Skirmishers, Hussars and towers buy time until Arbalesters with full upgrades outrange them.
- Gunpowder civilizations like the Turks or Spanish are where the Condottiero earns its place.
- Strong early aggressors, for example Mongol Scout Cavalry, hit you before your bonuses kick in. Spearmen and the Archer armor bonus are enough if you wall.

## Common mistakes

- Clicking up with the same villager count as other civilizations. Go up a villager earlier, or keep the same count and spend the saved food on Loom or a Farm.
- Making Genoese Crossbowmen against archers or infantry. They are an anti-cavalry unit.
- Skipping Pirotechnia and wondering why Hand Cannoneers miss.
- Ignoring Dock technologies on water maps. Cheaper upgrades are only an advantage if you buy them.
- Treating Condottieri as a Champion replacement. Your Champions are fully upgraded, and they are the better general infantry.

title: How to Play the Japanese
summary: Japanese infantry attacks a third faster from the Feudal Age, their drop sites cost half and their Fishing Ships can take a beating. This guide covers the Men-at-Arms into Archers opening, Castle Age plans with Samurai and Crossbowmen, and how to play the matchups that trouble them.
body:
## What the Japanese are good at

Japanese infantry attacks 33% faster from the Feudal Age on. That applies to Militia, Men-at-Arms, Spearmen, Champions, Halberdiers and the Samurai, so every Barracks unit deals about a third more damage per second than the same unit of another civilization. Feudal Men-at-Arms kill villagers fast, and Spearmen win their fights against Scouts and Knights more cleanly.

The economy bonus is small but useful every game. Mills, Lumber Camps and Mining Camps cost 50 wood instead of 100, so you can put drop sites right next to every resource and keep walking distances short. On water, Fishing Ships have double hit points, +2 pierce armor and work up to 20% faster in the Imperial Age, and the team bonus gives Galleys +4 Line of Sight. The newer bonus gives Cavalry Archers +2 attack against archers, which makes Heavy Cavalry Archers a real option against foot archer civilizations.

The Samurai is the Castle unique unit: a fast-attacking infantry unit with bonus damage against unique units and, since a recent update, a short charge with extra speed and attack when it runs at an enemy. It is the answer to enemy unique units such as Conquistadors, Mangudai or Teutonic Knights. Yasama in the Castle Age gives towers two extra arrows, and Kataparuto in the Imperial Age makes Trebuchets pack, unpack and fire faster.

The weak side is the Stable and siege. Japanese have no Paladin, no Hussar, no Siege Ram, no Siege Onager and no Bombard Cannon, and miss Crop Rotation and Plate Barding Armor. The Archery Range is complete with Arbalester, Thumb Ring and Bracer, so the usual late game is infantry plus archers with Trebuchets.

## Openings that suit them

The standard land opening is Men-at-Arms into Archers (see the build Japanese Men-at-Arms into Archers). The faster attack makes three Men-at-Arms a real threat, the cheap Mill and Mining Camp save wood for the Archery Range, and the archers then keep the pressure on. St4rk shows a fast version that aims to end games around the 11 or 12 minute mark, and SamuelAoE has an 18 population version for maps with chickens.

A fast castle is the other land option. TheViper tested a fast castle into Samurai, and it works best on closed maps or against civilizations whose unique units are their main army.

On water and hybrid maps, Japanese are one of the strongest picks. Their Fishing Ships survive harassment that kills other civilizations' fishermen, so you can boom from the sea and fight with Galleys and Fire Galleys from a safe base.

## Castle Age plan

After the Feudal archers, the common follow-up is Crossbowmen with Long Swordsmen or Pikemen in front. Both Barracks units benefit from the attack speed bonus, and the Archery Range has every upgrade, so you can keep the Feudal army and simply upgrade it.

Against cavalry civilizations, Pikemen with Crossbowmen behind them handle Knights better than any Japanese Stable unit. Against unique unit armies, build a Castle and add Samurai. Yasama is worth it on closed maps and when you rely on towers to protect a boom.

## Imperial Age plan

Arbalesters and Champions or Halberdiers form the core, with Samurai against enemy unique units and Trebuchets with Kataparuto for buildings. Kataparuto makes Japanese Trebuchets much quicker to set up, which matters when you push into Castles. Heavy Cavalry Archers with the +2 bonus against archers are a good second army against Britons, Maya and other foot archer civilizations. Onagers and Capped Rams round out the siege.

## Matchups

AoE2Insights shows the Japanese at about a 50% win rate in 1v1 random map. Their worst results come against Shu, Huns, Romans, Ethiopians, Britons and Vietnamese, and their best against Aztecs, Goths, Gurjaras, Varangians, Muisca and Teutons.

The pattern is easy to read. Japanese do well against infantry civilizations, since their Barracks units win straight infantry fights. They struggle against massed archers and fast cavalry. Against Britons, Ethiopians and Vietnamese, rely on Skirmishers and Men-at-Arms in Feudal, then Heavy Cavalry Archers or Onagers. Infantry walking into massed Crossbowmen loses no matter how fast it attacks. Huns make Pikemen and Skirmishers the base of your army, because you cannot win a cavalry fight against Tarkans and Cavalry Archers.

Romans have infantry with double Blacksmith armor and cheap Scorpions. Avoid the infantry mirror there and go archers with Mangonels, or Samurai against Legionaries and Centurions.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting the cheap drop sites. Build a Lumber Camp at every new woodline and a Mining Camp at every gold mine; at 50 wood each, long walks are never worth it.
- Making Knights. The Japanese Stable is weak; Pikemen and archers do the anti-cavalry work.
- Using Samurai as a general infantry unit. They are expensive and shine against unique units; Champions are better against generic armies.
- Ignoring water. On hybrid maps a few Docks with tough Fishing Ships give a large food lead.
- Walking slow infantry into massed archers without Skirmishers or siege.

title: How to Play the Jurchens
summary: Jurchens hit hard with fast attacking cavalry early, then grind opponents down with cheap siege, Grenadiers and Iron Pagodas. This guide covers Scout and Steppe Lancer openings, the Castle Age siege push, the late game army and the matchups that give them trouble.
body:
The Jurchens arrived with the Three Kingdoms expansion as a cavalry, siege and gunpowder civilization. Their mounted units and Fire Lancers attack 25% faster from the Feudal Age on, which makes their Scout Cavalry and Steppe Lancers some of the most dangerous in the game. Meat from hunted animals and sheep never decays, so deer and boar can be killed early and eaten later without losing food. On top of that, siege and fortification technologies cost 75% less wood and research twice as fast, Siege Engineers are available in the Castle Age, and their own units take half damage from friendly fire.

## What the Jurchens do well

- Early cavalry. Faster attacks let Jurchen Scouts win scout fights and kill villagers quickly. Steppe Lancers, with their extra reach, raid and fight in groups better than for almost anyone else.
- Siege. They have a nearly complete Siege Workshop with Rocket Carts in place of Mangonels, Siege Rams, Heavy Scorpions and Bombard Cannons, all upgraded cheaply and early.
- Gunpowder. The Grenadier from the Archery Range throws explosives that deal area damage and some bonus damage to buildings. In the Imperial Age, Thunderclap Bombs make Grenadiers, Rocket Carts and Lou Chuans explode on death and add extra blasts to their attacks.
- Defense. Fortified Bastions let walls, towers, Town Centers and Castles regenerate 500 hit points per minute, which saves a lot of stone and repair time.

The weak side: infantry stops at Man-at-Arms and lacks Plate Mail Armor, the Archery Range has no Arbalester or Thumb Ring, and there is no Knight line at the Stable. The Iron Pagoda from the Castle is the heavy cavalry. Monks miss Faith, Heresy and Redemption, so gold heavy late armies are open to conversion.

## Openings

Jurchens Fast Castle Steppe Lancers (21+2), written up on this site, is the signature build. Thanks to the meat that never rots you can skip early farms, click Feudal Age at 21 villagers and Castle Age two villagers later, and start Steppe Lancers from a Stable built in Feudal. Morley Games reaches the Castle Age at about 13:40 with it.

A straight Feudal Age Scout rush is the other main opening. The 25% faster attack wins Scout fights and lets a small group kill villagers before the Town Center responds. Push deer early with your scout, since the meat will wait for you.

On closed maps, a fast Castle Age into Fire Lancers and Battering Rams is a strong option.

## Castle Age plan

With Steppe Lancers, research Bloodlines on the way up, keep five gold miners per Stable, and raid in one group. Add a Siege Workshop and a few Rocket Carts behind the Lancers to break armies of Spearmen or archers. Get Siege Engineers early; it is cheap for you and gives every siege unit more range.

Grenadiers start slowly in the Castle Age, but they scale very well. Once your gold income is solid, begin massing them from two or three Archery Ranges. Iron Pagodas periodically ignore a melee hit, which makes them a good frontline against Knights and infantry.

Defensively, towers and walls are cheap to upgrade, and Fortified Bastions means a damaged Castle or Town Center heals itself.

## Imperial Age

The late game army is Grenadiers with Thunderclap Bombs behind a frontline of Iron Pagodas or Elite Steppe Lancers, supported by Heavy Rocket Carts, Siege Rams and Bombard Cannons. Your units take reduced friendly fire, so you can mix siege and melee units closely. Hussars and Halberdiers are the trash units. On water, Lou Chuans are strong even without Shipwright.

## Matchups

- A Men-at-Arms opening is awkward for a fast Castle Age build. Build a tower at your gold and a Barracks for Spearmen during the age up, as Morley suggests, and do not skip Loom.
- Camel and Pikeman civilizations such as Saracens, Hindustanis and Byzantines trade well against Steppe Lancers. Switch to Grenadiers and Rocket Carts, which beat infantry and Camels at range.
- Monk heavy civilizations like Aztecs and Spanish can convert your Iron Pagodas and siege. Use Hussars or Steppe Lancers to hunt Monks.
- Late game archer civilizations such as Britons or Mayans outrange your Grenadiers. Use Siege Rams, Bombard Cannons and Hussars to close the distance.

## Common mistakes

- Sending Steppe Lancers into Pikemen. They are raiders; go around the Pikemen and hit villagers.
- Ignoring the siege bonus. Many Jurchen players forget that Siege Engineers and the ram upgrades cost almost no wood for them.
- Making Cavalry Archers as a main army. Without Thumb Ring and Parthian Tactics they fall off badly.
- Leaving deer unused. Meat does not decay, so pushing every deer under the Town Center early is free food.
- Building too few Archery Ranges once you switch to Grenadiers. They train slowly at first; three ranges is common.

title: How to Play the Khitans
summary: The Khitans farm with Pastures, get double value from their melee attack upgrades and peak in the Castle Age with Steppe Lancers and early Heavy Cavalry Archers. How to open, how to use the Castle Age lead and why to finish before the late game.
body:
The Khitans are a cavalry and infantry civilization from The Three Kingdoms with an unusual food economy. They build Pastures instead of Farms, their melee attack upgrades count double, and their trash units train faster. They are at their best from the Feudal Age to the early Imperial Age and want to win before their late-game gaps show. On the current ladder they sit near the top of the win rate charts.

## What the Khitans are good at

Pastures replace Farms. A Pasture costs 110 wood, takes two villagers at once and holds three animals of 115 food each, 345 food in total. That works out to 55 wood per villager, a little cheaper than a Farm, and you do not need a Mill to build one. The Mill technologies are replaced by Domestication, Pastoralism and Transhumance, which add one, two and three animals to new Pastures. Per villager, a Pasture holds about as much food as a Farm, and a little less once the upgrades kick in, so you rebuild them at least as often. Keep wood coming in.

The Khitan Blacksmith is unusual. Forging and Iron Casting have double effect, so your melee units get +2 attack in the Feudal Age and +4 in the Castle Age. There is no Blast Furnace, so the late-game total ends up the same as everyone else's; the advantage is that you have it earlier and cheaper.

Skirmishers, Spearmen and the Scout Cavalry line train and upgrade 15% faster. The Heavy Cavalry Archer upgrade is available in the Castle Age at half price, which gives your horse archers more HP, attack and armor than anyone else's in that age. The team bonus gives infantry +2 attack against archers, and it applies to your own units too.

The unique units are the Liao Dao, a tough Castle infantry unit for 40 food and 40 gold whose hits cause bleeding damage, and the Mounted Trebuchet, a mobile siege unit that replaces the Bombard Cannon. Lamellar Armor makes infantry and Skirmishers reflect 25% of melee damage. Ordo Cavalry lets melee cavalry regenerate HP while it fights.

The gaps: no Bloodlines, no Knight line, no Halberdier, no Arbalester, no Hand Cannoneer, no Mangonel line and no Heavy Scorpion. Defenses lack Architecture, Hoardings, Arrowslits and the Keep. Monks lack Redemption. The navy has no Galleon, Shipwright or Dry Dock, so stay off the water.

## Openings that suit them

- Khitans Scouts with Pastures (civ-khitans-scouts-pastures) is the most common ladder start. Scout Cavalry is the Khitans' most produced unit, and Forging gives your scouts +2 attack in the Feudal Age, which more than makes up for the missing Bloodlines.
- Men-at-Arms with double Forging is a strong alternative, since Khitan infantry also hits archers harder.
- On closed maps, a fast castle into Heavy Cavalry Archers or Steppe Lancers uses the Castle Age power spike directly.

## Castle Age plans

The Castle Age is the Khitans' peak. Steppe Lancers with Iron Casting hit very hard and can attack over other units thanks to their reach. They are your Knight replacement for raids and fights against archers. Heavy Cavalry Archers, researched early and at half price, are the other main option and are hard for most civilizations to answer in this age.

Liao Dao are good against infantry and cavalry thanks to their melee armor and bleeding, and the team bonus helps them against archers. Skirmishers and Pikemen are cheap support that trains fast. Get Lamellar Armor if your army is infantry or Skirmisher heavy.

Use the strong Castle Age to take map control, add Town Centers and do as much damage as you can before the opponent's Imperial Age upgrades arrive.

## Imperial Age

Research Ordo Cavalry and Hussar, keep Steppe Lancers or Heavy Cavalry Archers as the core, and add Champions or Liao Dao where you need infantry. Siege Rams, Trebuchets and the Mounted Trebuchet take down buildings. Your late game is weaker than your middle game: without Bloodlines your cavalry has less HP, without Halberdiers elephants are hard to stop, and without Blast Furnace your melee attack no longer leads. Close the game before that point if you can.

## Matchups

On AoE2Insights the Khitans' hardest matchups are Mapuche, Muisca, Romans, Armenians, Vikings and Malay. Many of these field strong infantry or cheap mass units that trade well with Steppe Lancers and lightly armored cavalry. Against heavy infantry, lean on Heavy Cavalry Archers and keep your melee units out of bad fights.

Elephant civilizations are another problem, since Pikemen without Halberdier and Heavy Camel Riders are your only real answer. Use Pikemen with Lamellar Armor in numbers and raid with cavalry rather than fighting the elephants head on.

The Khitans do very well against cavalry civilizations that rely on Knights and lose to archers. Their best matchups include Georgians, Lithuanians, Poles, Slavs, Khmer and Berbers.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting to rebuild Pastures. Two villagers stand on each one, so a dead Pasture idles twice as many villagers as a dead Farm.
- Skipping the Mill. Pastures do not need one, but berries are still faster food in the Dark Age.
- Fighting late. The Khitans lose value in the Imperial Age; use the Castle Age lead.
- Taking scout mirror fights without Forging. Your scouts have no Bloodlines, so get Forging first.
- Going to the water. The Khitan Dock is one of the worst in the game.
