title: How to Play the Khmer
summary: The Khmer can age up and place any building without the usual requirements, farm without a Mill, and hide villagers in Houses. Use that freedom for fast, unpredictable openings into Battle Elephants, Knights and Scorpions.
body:
## What the Khmer are good at

The Khmer need no buildings to advance to the next age or to unlock other buildings. You can click the Feudal Age without a Lumber Camp or Mill, build a Stable without a Barracks, and click the Castle Age without the two Feudal Age buildings everyone else has to place. A fast Castle Age saves the wood of a Blacksmith and a Market, and a scout rush saves the 175 wood of a Barracks.

Khmer farmers put food straight into the stockpile without walking to a drop site, at the cost of working 5% slower. You can place Farms anywhere, even without a Mill, which lets you farm in safe corners or next to a forward Castle. Villagers can also garrison in Houses, so a House next to every woodline and gold mine is a free shelter against raids. Battle Elephants move 10% faster, and the team bonus gives Scorpions 1 extra range.

The unique unit is the Ballista Elephant, an elephant carrying a Scorpion that shoots bolts through every unit in a line and can cut down trees. Tusk Swords (Castle Age) gives Battle Elephants 3 more attack, and Double Crossbow (Imperial Age) makes Ballista Elephants and Scorpions fire a second bolt at half strength.

The weak side of the tree is infantry and some upgrades: no Champion, no Squires, no Plate Mail Armor, no Thumb Ring, no Bombard Cannon, no Siege Onager, no Paladin and no camels. The Monastery lacks Heresy, so Monks are a real threat to your elephants.

The win condition is tempo. The Khmer reach the Castle Age earlier and with more resources than most, and their Battle Elephants, Knights and Scorpions punish an opponent who is not ready.

## Openings that suit them

This site has two Khmer builds. The no-Barracks Scout rush clicks up at 18 population and builds the Stable straight away. The Khmer Fast Castle skips both Feudal Age buildings, clicks up again shortly after reaching the Feudal Age, and goes into Knights or Battle Elephants. A fast Archer rush with no Barracks works the same way, and on Arena a fast Castle into several Town Centers is common.

Some players skip berries completely and go straight to Farms around the Town Center, since Khmer farming needs no Mill and is safer from early raids. It costs a bit of speed but makes the economy hard to hurt.

## Castle Age plan

Knights are the simplest follow-up to a fast Castle Age. Battle Elephants hit much harder and, with Husbandry and the Khmer speed bonus, are fast enough to raid, so a Battle Elephant push with Tusk Swords is the strongest Khmer timing against civilizations without good camels or Halberdiers. Crossbowmen are fine early in the Castle Age, but they get worse later because of the missing Thumb Ring.

Ballista Elephants work well against massed archers and infantry and pair nicely with Hussars. Heavy Scorpions with the extra range are hard to approach for archer and infantry armies. Keep using the House shelter: when raiders come, garrison the villagers, then send them back to work.

## Imperial Age

Elite Battle Elephants with Hussars, or Elite Ballista Elephants with Heavy Scorpions and Double Crossbow, are the two main Khmer armies. Halberdiers make a cheap screen even without the last armor upgrades. Siege Rams and Trebuchets take buildings, since there is no Bombard Cannon. Hand Cannoneers and Elite Skirmishers fill in against infantry and archers.

## Matchups

- Monk civilizations such as the Aztecs, Burmese or Spanish convert elephants easily because you have no Heresy. Bring Light Cavalry or Hussars to kill Monks and do not send elephants alone.
- Camel and Halberdier civilizations stop Battle Elephants. Switch to Scorpions, Ballista Elephants and Crossbowmen against them.
- Strong Onagers or Bombard Cannons beat clumped Scorpions and Ballista Elephants. Spread your siege and keep Hussars ready to dive.
- Fast Feudal pressure punishes a Khmer player who skipped too many buildings. If you see a rush coming, build the Archery Range or Barracks you skipped and wall.
- On water maps you can skip the Mill and focus on a Dock and fish early, but the navy lacks Shipwright, so the late water game is weaker than the land game.

## Common mistakes

- Skipping every building just because you can. The savings are real, but you still need Spearmen, Skirmishers or towers when the opponent attacks.
- Placing Farms far from the Town Center because they work anywhere. Safe Farms near the Town Center or Houses are worth the extra planning.
- Forgetting that Horse Collar and the other farming upgrades still need a Mill, even if your Farms do not.
- Sending Scorpions or Ballista Elephants into a fight without a front line to protect them.
- Massing Arbalesters late. Without Thumb Ring they miss too often.
- Ignoring the House garrison. Build Houses next to woodlines and gold so villagers can hide from raiders.

title: How to Play the Koreans
summary: Korean archers and infantry cost half the wood, archer armor is free and towers upgrade themselves. This guide covers the archer and tower openings, War Wagons and Rocket Carts in Castle Age, and how to hold a late game without good cavalry.
body:
The Koreans are an archer, tower and navy civilization. Their foot archers and infantry cost half the usual wood, every archer armor upgrade is free, and their towers upgrade themselves. They are at their best on closed maps and water maps, and they have one of the strongest archer openings on Arabia.

## What the Koreans are good at

Archer and infantry units cost 50 percent less wood. An Archer, a Skirmisher or a Spearman costs only about half its normal wood, so you need fewer lumberjacks to keep two or three Archery Ranges busy, and your trash units are cheap in the late game. Padded Archer Armor, Leather Archer Armor and Ring Archer Armor are free, so your archers win archer duels against civilizations that have not spent on armor yet. The Archery Range is fully upgraded, Arbalester and Thumb Ring included.

Stone miners work 20 percent faster, and the Watch Tower line upgrades for free, with Bombard Towers free once you have Chemistry. The Castle technology Eupseong gives Watch Towers, Guard Towers and Keeps +2 range. Korean towers are a real threat in a tower rush, and on closed maps a few towers on your resources make you very hard to raid. Warships cost 20 percent less wood, Galleons and Fast Fire Ships are fully upgraded, and the Turtle Ship is an armored ship that fires cannonballs and rockets.

The War Wagon, trained at the Castle, is a tough mounted ranged unit that plays like a slower, much sturdier Arbalester. The Koreans replace the Mangonel line with Rocket Carts, whose rockets ignore the armor of land units, and Shinkichon gives Rocket Carts and Turtle Ships +1 range and more rockets. Fire Lancers at the Barracks give you a wood and gold answer to cavalry. The team bonus gives villagers +3 line of sight.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

Korean cavalry is poor: no Bloodlines, no Plate Barding Armor, no Paladin, no Camel Rider, and no Blast Furnace for cavalry or infantry. There is no Siege Ram, no Mangonel line and no Demolition Ship. Monks lack Heresy, Redemption and Atonement, and the economy has no farming or wood bonus and lacks Crop Rotation. The Koreans win with ranged units, towers and siege, and they rarely win a cavalry raiding war.

## Openings that suit them

- Archers, written up as "Koreans Archers (21 pop)". The wood discount means two Archery Ranges are easy to keep busy, and free armor makes your archers win the first fights.
- Tower rush, written up as "Koreans Tower Rush (19 pop)". Faster stone mining and free tower upgrades make the Korean tower rush one of the strongest in the game. Save it for the occasional surprise game.
- Spearmen and Skirmishers for defense. Both cost little wood, so a cheap trash army holds early cavalry while you boom.
- A fast Castle into Fire Lancers and Rocket Carts is another option, especially on maps with no deer to push.

## Castle Age plan

Keep making Crossbowmen and add Thumb Ring when you have three or more ranges. Pikemen or Fire Lancers go in front against cavalry. Rocket Carts are your answer to massed archers, Skirmishers and infantry; their rockets ignore armor and they punish packed groups. Build a Castle for War Wagons, which handle most Castle Age armies and survive Town Center fire while they shoot villagers. They are expensive, slow and clumsy, so they work best as a front line for your archers. Research Eupseong if you play defensively or use towers on your resources.

## Imperial Age plan

The late army is Arbalesters or Elite War Wagons with Halberdiers in front and Heavy Rocket Carts or Bombard Cannons behind. Korean Halberdiers and Elite Skirmishers are cheap in wood, which helps once gold runs out. Fully upgraded Keeps with Eupseong outrange most Bombard Cannons, so a line of towers and Castles protects your army and your economy. On water, mass Galleons and Fast Fire Ships with a few Turtle Ships in the middle of the fleet, and keep Fast Fire Ships near the Turtle Ships because you have no Demolition Ships against enemy Fire Ships.

## Matchups

- Cavalry archer civilizations such as the Mongols, Tatars and Magyars kite your foot army. Use Skirmishers, War Wagons, towers and Castles, and push with Rocket Carts and Bombard Cannons so they have to fight.
- Heavy cavalry civilizations such as the Franks or Lithuanians are fine with Pikemen and Fire Lancers in front, but you cannot match their Paladins with your own cavalry. Keep your army together.
- Elephant civilizations need Halberdiers, Fire Lancers and Monks; your Monks are weak, so rely on infantry and Bombard Cannons.
- Siege heavy civilizations with Siege Onagers or many Bombard Cannons punish a tower defense. Kill the siege with Bombard Cannons, cavalry or War Wagons.

## Common mistakes

- Making cavalry as the main army. Without Bloodlines and the armor upgrades it loses to most units.
- Tower rushing every game. A Korean tower rush is strong, but opponents learn quickly, and a failed rush leaves you far behind.
- Researching archer armor at the Blacksmith. It is free; spend that time and money on Fletching and Bodkin Arrow.
- Forgetting that Rocket Carts replace Mangonels. They are worse against buildings, so bring Bombard Cannons or Trebuchets for Castles.
- Losing the water without Demolition Ships. Keep Fast Fire Ships in your fleet to answer enemy Fire Ships.

title: How to Play the Lithuanians
summary: Lithuanians start with extra food, field fast Spearmen and Skirmishers, and their Knights grow stronger with every Relic. This guide covers the quick scout opening, the Relic plan in the Castle Age and how to finish with Paladins, Leitis and Winged Hussars.
body:
The Lithuanians are a cavalry and Monk civilization with one of the most flexible starts in the game. Their extra food lets them reach the Feudal Age early with almost any opening, and their Relic bonus gives their Knights a reason to fight for the map in the Castle Age.

## What the Lithuanians are good at

- Each Town Center, including the one you start with, gives 100 food. At the start that is a head start on the age up, and every Town Center you build in the Castle Age pays back part of its cost.
- Spearmen, Pikemen, Halberdiers and Skirmishers move 10% faster, so your cheap units can actually catch Scout Cavalry and archers.
- Each Relic in a Monastery gives Knights and Leitis +1 attack, up to +4.
- Monasteries work 20% faster. That is the team bonus, and it helps your own Monks and Relic hunt.

The Leitis is the Castle unique unit: a horseman for 70 food and 50 gold whose attack ignores melee armor, which makes it very good against Paladins, Cataphracts, Boyars and heavy infantry. Light Cavalry upgrades to the Winged Hussar in the Imperial Age. Hill Forts gives your Town Centers +3 range in the Castle Age, and Tower Shields adds +2 pierce armor to Spearmen and Skirmishers in the Imperial Age.

Missing pieces: no Arbalester, Parthian Tactics, Plate Mail Armor or Blast Furnace, so Champions and the final Paladin attack upgrade are out. Siege is limited to Capped Rams, Onagers and Bombard Cannons, without Siege Engineers. Gold Shaft Mining is also missing, which matters in long games.

The win condition is simple to say: take the map in the Feudal Age, collect Relics in the Castle Age, and hit with Knights that do more damage than anyone else's.

## Openings that suit the Lithuanians

- Lithuanians Scouts: the extra food lets you click up with 17 villagers without luring deer and still get Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar on arrival. Hera compares the Lithuanian uptime to the Mongols, and Morley Games calls it one of the fastest scout rushes there is.
- Lithuanians Fast Castle into Knights and Monks: a quick Castle Age with one Stable and a Monastery to take the Relics.

Spearmen and Skirmishers are also a good defensive opening, since your fast Spearmen and Skirmishers win most Feudal fights against Scout Cavalry and archers. The famous early Drush, sometimes called the 3 minute rush, uses the starting food to make Militia almost at once; it is fun but less common today.

## Castle Age plan

The default is Knights from one or two Stables, with a Monastery built as soon as you can afford it. Two to four Monks pick up Relics while the Knights protect them. Each Relic adds attack to your Knights, and four Relics give them +4, which wins most Knight fights and kills villagers faster.

Build Town Centers behind the Knights; each one gives 100 food back. Hill Forts makes those Town Centers much harder to raid, which is useful if you are playing against a Cavalry Archer or Knight civilization. Against archers, add Skirmishers; against Camels or Halberdiers, use Monks and Skirmishers with your Knights, or switch to Crossbowmen.

Leitis come from the Castle and are the unit to make when the opponent has heavy melee units: Knights and Paladins of other civilizations, Boyars, or infantry with high melee armor.

## Imperial Age plan

Paladins with Relic attack are the main heavy cavalry, and Winged Hussars are cheap, fast raiders and Monk hunters. Leitis cover melee heavy enemies. Behind them, Halberdiers and Elite Skirmishers with Tower Shields hold the line cheaply, and Bombard Cannons answer enemy Castles and siege. Since you lack Blast Furnace and Plate Mail Armor, avoid a Champion army.

## Matchups and what gives the Lithuanians trouble

- Camel and Halberdier civilizations. Your Knights lose to them; use Monks, Skirmishers and archers to clear them, or Leitis against Halberdiers.
- Strong archer civilizations in the Imperial Age. You have no Arbalester, so beat Arbalesters with Paladins, Winged Hussars, Skirmishers and Bombard Cannons.
- Monk and siege pushes from civilizations with Siege Onagers. Kill the Onagers with Winged Hussars or Bombard Cannons before they reach your army.
- Relic denial. If the opponent takes the Relics first, your Knights lose their edge; fight for them early with Knights near your Monks.

## Common mistakes with the Lithuanians

- Floating the starting food. Use it to click up earlier or to keep the Town Center busy without luring deer.
- Forgetting the Monastery. Without Relics the Lithuanian Knight is an ordinary Knight.
- Sending Monks for far Relics without an escort.
- Building Champions or Arbalesters for the late game; neither is fully available.
- Never building more Town Centers. Each one pays you 100 food back.

title: How to Play the Magyars
summary: Magyars get cheap scouts, free attack upgrades and longer range Cavalry Archers. This guide covers the Scout opening, the Knight or Cavalry Archer Castle Age, the gold free Huszar late game and the anti-cavalry civilizations that give Magyars trouble.
body:
The Magyars are a cavalry civilization with a very short list of bonuses that all point the same way. Their Scout Cavalry are cheaper, their melee units get free attack upgrades, and their mounted archers gain range and attack from a unique technology. They have no economic bonus, so they win by attacking early and trading well, and that simple plan makes them a good civilization for newer players.

## What the Magyars are good at

- Forging, Iron Casting and Blast Furnace are free. You get the attack upgrade for your melee units and cavalry as soon as each age arrives, which saves well over 600 food and 300 gold across the game and makes your Feudal Scout Cavalry hit harder.
- The Scout Cavalry line costs 15% less: Scout Cavalry, Light Cavalry and Hussars all cost 68 food instead of 80.
- Villagers kill wolves and other predators in a single hit, so wolves never cost you a villager.
- Recurve Bow, the Imperial Age unique technology, gives Cavalry Archers +1 attack and +1 range.
- The Magyar Huszar is a cheap light cavalry unit from the Castle with a bonus against siege. With Corvinian Army its gold cost turns into extra food, so a late game Huszar army costs no gold at all.
- The team bonus trains mounted archers 25% faster for the whole team.

Their tech tree is full on the cavalry side: Paladin, Hussar, Heavy Cavalry Archer, Bloodlines, Husbandry and all barding armors. Arbalesters with Thumb Ring are also available.

The win condition is to take map control with cheap scouts, keep raiding into the Castle Age with Knights or Cavalry Archers, and finish with Paladins or Huszars and Heavy Cavalry Archers.

## Openings that suit them

The opening that fits the civilization best is the Magyars Scouts build on this site. With free Forging your Scout Cavalry hit for one more damage than usual right as Feudal arrives, and each scout is 12 food cheaper. The build clicks up at 19 population and has three scouts out quickly.

Archers are also fine; Magyar foot archers have every upgrade except the Hand Cannoneer. Some players go for a Fast Castle into Magyar Huszars and a Castle drop, which St4rk shows in a recent video, but the Castle needs a lot of stone and the opponent can attack your stone miners.

## Castle Age plan

From a scout opening, the usual next step is Knights from two or three Stables. Free Iron Casting makes them hit hard, and Bloodlines and Husbandry are worth getting early. Against archers, Knights do the job; against Pikemen and Camel Riders, change to Cavalry Archers with Thumb Ring and Ballistics. They get even better in the Imperial Age once Recurve Bow is in.

Light Cavalry is very cost effective for Magyars because of the discount. Use a group of Light Cavalry to raid and to kill Monks and siege while the Knights or Cavalry Archers fight.

Build a Castle once you have spare stone. It trains Magyar Huszars, which are strong against Skirmishers, Mangonels and Scorpions, and researches Corvinian Army.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age, Magyars have one of the best cavalry armies in the game. Paladins with free Blast Furnace, Hussars, Elite Magyar Huszars and Heavy Cavalry Archers with Recurve Bow all reach full strength. A common end game is Heavy Cavalry Archers plus Elite Magyar Huszars with Corvinian Army: almost no gold is needed for the Huszars, so you can keep both lines going on a thin gold income.

The siege is weak, with no Siege Ram, Siege Onager or Bombard Cannon. Use Capped Rams, Trebuchets and Onagers. Magyar infantry lacks Plate Mail Armor and Squires, so it is a support unit at best.

## Matchups

The hardest matchups on the ladder are Khitans, Hindustanis, Saxons, Persians, Berbers and Gurjaras. Most of them have strong anti-cavalry tools.

- Against Camel Rider civilizations (Hindustanis, Berbers, Gurjaras), stop making Knights early. Switch to Arbalesters or Cavalry Archers with Recurve Bow, and keep the Huszars for raiding and killing siege.
- Against elephants (Persians, Gurjaras), mass Arbalesters and Monks. Elephants are slow, so kite them with Cavalry Archers.
- Against strong infantry with Pikemen, Cavalry Archers and Huszars avoid the bad trade. Do not run Knights into a wall of Halberdiers.
- Against archer civilizations Magyars are in good shape: Light Cavalry, Knights and Huszars all beat archers for low cost.

## Common mistakes

- Booming like an economy civilization. Magyars have no economic bonus and lack Guilds and Stone Shaft Mining, so they fall behind in a slow game.
- Ignoring the discount. Light Cavalry and Hussars are cheap, and they are your best raiding units; many players forget to use them in the Castle Age.
- Forgetting Recurve Bow. It is the main reason Magyar Cavalry Archers are better than generic ones.
- Making Knights into Camel Riders or Halberdiers. Watch what your opponent is making and switch production before the fight is lost.
- Fighting under enemy defenses. Your siege is weak, so open towers and Castles with Trebuchets instead of throwing cavalry at them.

title: How to Play the Malay
summary: The Malay age up much faster than anyone else, get free infantry armor and cheap Battle Elephants. How to turn the short age ups into earlier power spikes on land, and why Fish Traps make them so strong on water.
body:
The Malay are a navy and infantry civilization whose main land bonus is speed. Advancing to the next age is 66 percent faster, so the Feudal Age takes about 78 seconds instead of 130, the Castle Age about 96 seconds instead of 160 and the Imperial Age just under two minutes. Fish Traps cost a third less and hold three times as much food. Battle Elephants are 25 percent cheaper in the Castle Age and 35 percent cheaper in the Imperial Age, and infantry armor upgrades at the Blacksmith are free. Their team bonus gives Docks extra line of sight.

## What the Malay are good at

Faster age ups give you time, and you choose how to spend it. You can click at the normal moment and arrive a minute earlier than your opponent, or keep making villagers longer and arrive at the same time with a bigger economy. Either way you reach every power spike first, whether that is Feudal Age Archers, Castle Age Battle Elephants or an Imperial Age army.

Free infantry armor makes Militia, Men-at-Arms and later Two-Handed Swordsmen tougher than they look, and Forced Levy, the Imperial unique technology, removes the gold cost of the Militia line in exchange for more food. That gives the Malay one of the best trash armies in the game. The Karambit Warrior, the Castle unique unit, is very cheap and takes only half a population slot. It is fragile, and works as a swarm that kills rams, villagers and unguarded buildings.

The weak side is the Stable. Apart from Battle Elephants, Malay cavalry lacks Bloodlines, the last two barding armor upgrades, Hussar and Paladin. There is no Champion, no Hand Cannoneer and no Heavy Cavalry Archer. Their siege workshop is limited as well.

The win condition is to use the time advantage while your opponent is weaker. On land you hit with an early power unit, keep the pressure up and fall back on cheap infantry and elephants once gold gets thin. On water you take the sea, then live off Fish Traps that rarely need replacing.

## Openings

- Malay Fast Feudal Archers (22 pop) clicks up with a villager or two more than a usual archer rush and still reaches the Feudal Age at about the same time.
- Malay Fast Castle into Battle Elephants is the Castle Age power play. You reach the Castle Age a minute before a normal fast Castle and start making discounted elephants from two Stables.

Militia and Men-at-Arms openings benefit from the free armor, and oSetinhas has a fast Feudal build with two militia that shows how tanky they get. On Arena, a Feudal boom that buys the Feudal economy upgrades minutes early, then goes to a Castle drop, Monks or a fast Imperial Age, is a strong plan; HaraKiri's 2026 guide walks through it, and Hera has a 2026 video on a Malay Arena plan as well.

## Castle Age plan

Your two main options are Crossbowmen and Battle Elephants. Crossbowmen are the safe choice against infantry and other archers, and they upgrade straight into fully upgraded Arbalesters later. Battle Elephants at about 90 food and 53 gold are cheaper in gold than a Knight and crush buildings, Knights and infantry. Mix in Crossbowmen or Long Swordsmen to deal with the Halberdiers and Monks that the opponent will make against them.

Karambit Warriors are worth making once you have a Castle anyway, especially to kill rams and siege that come close or to swarm a Castle drop. A few Monks are good support; the Malay Monastery is solid.

Use the faster Imperial Age click. Many Malay players go up earlier than their opponent with fewer Town Centers and win on upgrades.

## Imperial Age

Research Forced Levy as soon as gold starts running low. With it, Two-Handed Swordsmen cost no gold at all. Combined with free infantry armor, Halberdiers and Arbalesters, they make an army that keeps fighting long after the gold mines are empty. Elite Battle Elephants are 35 percent cheaper in this age, so a group of them in front of the infantry gives the trash army real punch. Bombard Cannons handle buildings.

## On water

Fish Traps with triple food barely ever need rebuilding, which saves huge amounts of wood for warships. The Malay navy lacks only the Heavy Demolition Ship, and Thalassocracy turns Docks into Harbors that shoot arrows, which protects your fishing and lets you deny an enemy shore. On water maps, win the first fights, then put most of your food economy on fish and Fish Traps and the villagers on wood and gold.

## Matchups

- Monk heavy civilizations such as the Aztecs or Spanish convert Battle Elephants easily. Bring Light Cavalry or Karambit Warriors to kill Monks and keep the elephants in groups.
- Halberdier and Camel Rider civilizations stop elephant play. Answer with Crossbowmen and infantry, and keep the elephants for buildings and raids.
- Cavalry Archer civilizations like the Mongols, Magyars or Tatars outmaneuver your slow army. Skirmishers and Arbalesters with full upgrades are your answer, plus walls and towers.
- Gunpowder and Onager civilizations punish massed infantry. Spread out and target their siege with elephants.
- On water, the Vikings, Italians and Portuguese have strong navies. The Fish Trap economy wins long naval games if you hold the first fights.

## Common mistakes

- Clicking up at the same population and the same moment as every other civilization, and wasting the bonus.
- Building the Feudal Age buildings too late. The age up is short, so place the Barracks or the Feudal buildings as you click, not halfway through.
- Making Knights or Light Cavalry as a main army. Your cavalry upgrades are poor; use Battle Elephants instead.
- Sending elephants into massed Halberdiers or Monks.
- Forgetting Forced Levy when the gold runs out.

title: How to Play the Malians
summary: Malians save wood on every building, mine gold faster and field Barracks units that shrug off arrows. This guide covers their archer and fast castle openings, Gbeto and Farimba cavalry plans, and the matchups where their flexible tech tree has to work hardest.
body:
## What the Malians are good at

Malians are a flexible civilization with an economy that pays off all game. Every building except Farms and the starting Town Center costs 15% less wood, so Houses, drop sites, Archery Ranges, Stables and new Town Centers are all cheaper. Villagers drop off 10% more gold, which in practice means gold miners work faster, carry more and every gold mine holds 10% more. In long games that extra gold is the difference between running out of Champions and still making them.

The military bonus sits in the Barracks. Militia line, Spearmen and the unique Gbeto get +1 pierce armor in the Feudal Age, +2 in the Castle Age and +3 in the Imperial Age. Malians lack Gambesons, but the bonus more than makes up for it, so Malian Men-at-Arms and Long Swordsmen walk through arrow fire that would stop other infantry. The team bonus makes Universities work 80% faster.

The Gbeto is a fast light infantry unit from the Castle that throws a hard-hitting ranged attack. It raids well, kills archers and villagers, and is fragile in melee. Tigui in the Castle Age makes Town Centers fire extra arrows even when nobody is garrisoned, which helps a boom survive raids. Farimba in the Imperial Age gives all cavalry +5 attack, turning Cavaliers, Light Cavalry and Heavy Camel Riders into strong late-game units.

There are gaps. Malians have no Halberdier, no Hussar, no Paladin, no Siege Ram and no Bracer, and miss Blast Furnace and Two-Man Saw. They make up for the missing Halberdier with Camel Riders and for the missing Bracer with Gbetos and Skirmishers.

## Openings that suit them

Cheap buildings make two-range archer openings attractive, since the second Archery Range costs less wood (see the build Malians Two Range Archers). Morley Games plays a 19 population version that rushes even faster.

On Arena and other closed maps, the fast castle into three Town Centers is the economic plan (see the build Malians Fast Castle Boom). Each extra Town Center costs about 234 wood instead of 275, which adds up to a free House or two every time.

Scout Cavalry is the most produced Malian unit according to AoE2Insights, and Militia openings are common too. Men-at-Arms with the pierce armor bonus are a good choice against opponents who open with archers, since arrows barely hurt them.

## Castle Age plan

The Castle Age gives you three paths, and you can switch between them because the economy is flexible. Knights from cheap Stables work against archers and siege. Gbetos from a Castle are strong against archer and infantry armies that do not have much cavalry. Long Swordsmen with +2 pierce armor plus Camel Riders handle many mixed armies.

On closed maps, research Tigui once you have three Town Centers; the extra arrows deter Knight and Gbeto raids. Use the faster gold income to get Gold Mining early and keep two or three Town Centers making villagers until about 100 population.

## Imperial Age plan

Research Farimba once your cavalry count grows. Cavaliers and Heavy Camel Riders with +5 attack beat most cavalry they face. Champions with +3 pierce armor are almost immune to archers, and Elite Gbetos clean up anything that tries to kite them. Mix in Siege Onagers or Bombard Cannons for buildings and groups of infantry, and Trebuchets for Castles.

## Matchups

AoE2Insights puts Malians at a little over 51% in 1v1 random map, around tenth of 57 civilizations. Their weakest results come against Shu, Ethiopians, Mongols, Chinese, Huns and Tupi, and their best against Mapuche, Burgundians, Goths, Aztecs, Armenians and Poles.

The hard matchups are mostly mobile ranged armies and strong archers. Mongol Mangudai and Hun Cavalry Archers outrun Malian infantry; answer with Skirmishers, Light Cavalry and Camel Riders, and with Gbetos once you have a Castle. Ethiopian and Chinese archers are powerful, but Malian Men-at-Arms and Long Swordsmen can walk up to them with the pierce armor bonus; add Mangonels and Knights to finish the fight.

Malians do well against infantry civilizations. Goths, Aztecs and Mapuche rely on foot soldiers that Malian Barracks units and Gbetos handle, and Malians also have one of their best records against Armenians and Poles.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the pierce armor bonus as melee armor. Malian infantry still loses to Cavaliers and Champions in melee; bring Spearmen or camels.
- Forgetting there is no Halberdier. Use Camel Riders and Pikemen in the Castle Age and plan for Heavy Camel Riders later.
- Building archers into the late game. Without Bracer, Malian Arbalesters fall behind; switch to Gbetos and Skirmishers.
- Not spending the saved wood. Cheaper buildings only help if you use the difference on extra Town Centers, Farms or production.
- Skipping Tigui on closed maps. It costs no gold and makes every Town Center a tower.

title: How to Play the Mapuche
summary: Mapuche have no Stable, yet their Bolas Riders and Konas are among the best mounted units in the game, backed by tough trash units trained from Settlements. This guide covers the Champi and trash openings, the fast Castle Age into Bolas Riders and how to deal with the matchups that hurt them.
body:
The Mapuche are one of the three South American civilizations from The Last Chieftains. Like the Inca, Muisca and Tupi, they use the Settlement in place of the Mill, Lumber Camp and Mining Camp. It costs 125 wood, accepts every resource, gives 5 population and counts as two buildings for the Feudal Age requirement. They start with a Champi Scout instead of Scout Cavalry, and their Barracks line is the Champi line (Champi Scout, Champi Runner, Champi Warrior) in place of Militia.

What makes the Mapuche different is the mix of cheap counter units and two mounted unique units, even though they have no Stable at all. Their bonuses:

- Foragers drop off 25% more food, so berries are worth more for them than for anyone else.
- Settlements can train Spearmen and Skirmishers. Production is slow in the Feudal and Castle Ages (about 2.15 and 1.6 times the normal time) and normal in the Imperial Age, and upgrades for both lines can be researched there.
- Infantry, Slingers and Skirmishers get +5, +10 and +15 hit points in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Ages.
- Mounted units gain 3 gold for every enemy military unit they kill.
- Enemy Castles are revealed on the map when they finish.

## The unique units

The Bolas Rider is trained at the Archery Range in the Castle Age and replaces the Cavalry Archer. It is cheaper and far more accurate, and it needs no Bloodlines, Husbandry or Thumb Ring, only the archer Blacksmith upgrades. Every 30 seconds it throws a charged shot that deals extra damage and slows the target. It has bonus damage against cavalry and Camels, and with Malon its shots pass through to units behind the target. Spirit of the Law notes it is the unit most Mapuche players switch to in the Castle Age.

The Kona is the Castle unit and fills the Knight's role. It is cheap, fast, has 125 hit points and good pierce armor, deals more damage to injured targets and has a bonus against gunpowder units. Use it to kill Skirmishers, siege and archers, or to raid late in the game.

## Openings

The Mapuche Champi Runner rush is the Men-at-Arms style opening, written up as a build on this site. Three Champi Scouts are made during the Feudal Age up, upgraded to Champi Runners on arrival, and Skirmishers from a Settlement join them. Champi units are fast and resist arrows, so they are good at pinning villagers and stopping walls.

A Skirmisher and Spearman trash rush is also common at lower ratings. Settlements near the front produce Skirmishers and Spearmen with their extra hit points, and you save the wood of an Archery Range.

The Mapuche Fast Castle into Bolas Riders, also on this site, skips most Feudal fighting. You put many villagers on berries, click up with Blacksmith and Archery Range, and arrive with two ranges of Bolas Riders. Against an opponent who walls and booms, it is the most reliable plan.

## Castle Age plan

Bolas Riders do best in large groups that can kite. Research Fletching and Bodkin Arrow, then Ballistics early; LegendaryAoE2 points out that Bolas miss a lot of shots against moving targets without it. Keep seven or eight villagers on gold for two ranges. Get Malon once you face massed Crossbowmen or Skirmishers in clumps, since the pass-through damage turns those fights around.

Support the Bolas with trash. Pikemen and Elite Skirmishers from Settlements and Barracks protect the army from Knights and archers, and Slingers with extra hit points handle infantry. Add Konas when the opponent masses Skirmishers or siege, and use the Castle reveal to know exactly where the enemy Castles stand.

## Imperial Age

The late game army is Elite Bolas Riders and Elite Konas in front of Halberdiers, Elite Skirmishers and Slingers, with Onagers or Trebuchets for sieges. Settlements now train trash at normal speed, so every Settlement in your base becomes a production building. Butalmapu makes Bolas Riders and your team's Castle unique units 15% cheaper. It pays off quickly in team games; in 1v1 it is a long term investment.

## Matchups

- Men-at-Arms openings are the Mapuche's worst early matchup, and their win rate in short games is low. Answer with Skirmishers and Champi Runners at home, walls and an archer response, then move to Castle Age.
- Civilizations with strong Elite Skirmishers and siege, such as Vietnamese or Ethiopians, are the hard counter to Bolas Riders. Switch part of the army to Konas and Champi Warriors to reach those units.
- Heavy infantry like Champions and Teutonic Knights beat the Mapuche trash in melee. Use Slingers and Bolas Riders to shoot them down.
- Monk civilizations can convert Konas, and Mapuche Monks are weak, missing Redemption and Block Printing.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the Settlement like a Mill. Place it where it touches two resources and you save a whole drop site.
- Expecting fast Feudal production from Settlements. It is slow until the Imperial Age, so build a real Archery Range or Barracks when you need numbers.
- Forgetting there is no Bracer. Bolas Riders and Skirmishers have shorter range than usual, so pick fights where pass-through damage matters.
- Buying Butalmapu early in a 1v1 instead of more units and upgrades.

title: How to Play the Maya
summary: The Maya start with an extra villager, their resources last longer and their archers get cheaper every age. How to open with archers or eagles, what to build in the Castle and Imperial Ages, and how to play without any cavalry.
body:
The Maya are an archer and Eagle Warrior civilization with one of the best economies in the game. They start with an extra villager, every resource they gather lasts 15% longer, their foot archers get cheaper with every age, and their walls cost half. They have no cavalry at all, so they win with archers, Eagle Warriors and good walls, and they need to plan carefully against siege and heavy cavalry.

## What the Maya are good at

The Maya start with four villagers and an Eagle Scout instead of three villagers and a Scout Cavalry, but with 50 less food. That puts you about one villager ahead from the first second. Because the four villagers and the Eagle Scout fill the Town Center's five population, you start housed. Build a House right away; the Town Center cannot train until it is up, which is why many Maya players click Loom at the very start.

Resources last 15% longer. That covers sheep, boar, berries, wood, gold, stone, fish and Farms, so you need fewer drop sites and fewer moves. Over a long game it means more gold, which is what an archer civilization runs out of first.

Foot archers except Skirmishers are 10% cheaper in the Feudal Age, 20% in the Castle Age and 30% in the Imperial Age. Mayan Arbalesters are fully upgraded. The Plumed Archer, trained at the Castle, is a faster and tougher archer with more HP and pierce armor; it costs 44 wood and 44 gold in the Castle Age after the discount. Hul'che Javelineers makes Skirmishers throw a second projectile, which helps a lot in archer mirrors. Holcans gives Eagle Warriors +40 HP.

The team bonus makes Palisade and Stone Walls and gates half price, and it applies to you too. Cheap walls are a big part of playing Maya safely.

What they lack: there are no mounted units and no gunpowder units. Infantry has no Champion and no Gambesons, Monks lack Redemption, and siege stops at Onager and Siege Ram with no Siege Onager or Bombard Cannon.

## Openings that suit them

- Maya Archers (civ-maya-archers) is the classic opening and the most common on the ladder. Archers are the Maya's most produced unit, and the discount and longer-lasting resources make a two-range archer start very strong.
- Maya Eagle and Archers (civ-maya-eagle-archers) uses Eagle Scouts from the Barracks together with archers. Eagles are good against Skirmishers, Spearmen and Scout Cavalry, and archers cover their weakness to Men-at-Arms.
- An archer opening that turns into a fast Castle Age is a good option when the opponent walls well. Your economy supports it and Crossbowmen are 20% cheaper.

## Castle Age plans

Crossbowmen with Bodkin Arrow and Ballistics are your main unit, made from two or three Archery Ranges. Eagle Warriors are the front line: fast, good against archers, siege and Monks, and decent against light units. Halberdiers come later, but Pikemen are your answer to Knights in this age.

Plumed Archers win archer fights against Crossbowmen and move faster on the map, but they need a Castle and more gold. Many players stay on Crossbowmen until they have a Castle for other reasons, then add Plumed Archers.

The Maya are a good booming civilization behind walls. Add a second and third Town Center in the early Castle Age if you are not under pressure.

## Imperial Age

The late-game army is Arbalesters or Elite Plumed Archers behind Halberdiers or Elite Eagle Warriors with Holcans. Halberdiers are cheaper and better against cavalry; Elite Eagle Warriors are better at raiding and at killing archers and siege. Siege Rams and Trebuchets take buildings. Heavy Scorpions help in large infantry fights.

The weakness is enemy Onagers and Bombard Cannons, since you have no cavalry to dive them and no Bombard Cannon to answer them. Use Elite Eagle Warriors to kill siege, keep your archers spread, and pressure the opponent before they get many Onagers.

## Matchups

On AoE2Insights the Maya's hardest matchups are Wu, Romans, Goths, Hindustanis, Khmer and Franks. Goths are the classic problem: Huskarls shrug off arrows and Goth infantry is cheap. Against them, use Eagle Warriors, Halberdiers and Heavy Scorpions instead of mass archers. Strong cavalry civilizations like the Franks are dangerous once they have Paladins; mass Halberdiers and pull back behind walls.

The Maya do well against civilizations that rely on slow units or weak archers. Their best matchups include Gurjaras, Mapuche, Saracens, Tatars, Burmese and Armenians.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting the first House. You start housed, so the first villager waits until a House is done.
- Leaving gaps in the walls. Walls cost half for you; wall your wood and gold early in every game.
- Eagle Warriors against Men-at-Arms or Long Swordsmen. Eagles lose to heavy infantry; use archers.
- No plan for siege. Decide early which units will hunt Mangonels and Onagers.
- Waiting too long. The Maya have the gold to win the Castle Age; use it before the opponent's Imperial Age units arrive.

title: How to Play the Mongols
summary: The Mongols hunt 40% faster, which gives them some of the fastest Feudal Age times in the game. They want to pressure early, survive a weak Castle Age economy and win the late game with Mangudai, Hussars and fast siege.
body:
## What the Mongols are good at

Mongol hunters work 40% faster. Boars, deer and other huntables are gone sooner and your Town Center keeps training villagers with fewer of them on food, so the Mongols click up to the Feudal Age earlier than almost anyone with the same number of villagers. Their Scout Cavalry line and Steppe Lancers get 20% more hit points in the Castle Age and 30% more in the Imperial Age, and Cavalry Archers (including Mangudai) fire 25% faster. The team bonus gives the Scout Cavalry line 2 extra line of sight.

The unique unit is the Mangudai, a Castle unit that costs 55 wood and 65 gold. It has more attack and hit points than a Cavalry Archer, a short attack delay that makes it easy to micro, and bonus damage against siege. Nomads (Castle Age) lets Houses keep their population space when destroyed, and Drill (Imperial Age) makes Siege Workshop units move 50% faster, so Mongol Onagers and rams can keep up with horse archers.

The tech tree has holes outside cavalry and siege. There is no Halberdier, no Paladin, no Hand Cannoneer and no Bombard Cannon, and the Blacksmith lacks Ring Archer Armor and Plate Barding Armor. The economy has no bonus after the hunt runs out and misses Crop Rotation, Two-Man Saw and Guilds, and the Monastery is one of the weakest in the game.

The win condition is pressure. Use the fast Feudal Age to take map control or hurt the opponent's economy, then reach the Imperial Age where Mangudai, Hussars and Siege Onagers with Drill are very hard to deal with.

## Openings that suit them

Scout Cavalry is the classic Mongol opening, and the Mongols Scouts build on this site clicks up at 18 population thanks to the hunt bonus. A fast Castle Age into Steppe Lancers, also on this site, uses the same hunt bonus to reach the Castle Age quickly and hit with tanky lancers. Men-at-Arms into Archers or Skirmishers is a safe option for players who prefer foot units.

Push deer to your Town Center when the map has them. On maps where chickens replace deer, the chickens cannot be pushed, and the patch stopped players from funnelling them into the Town Center, so build a Mill next to them and send the villagers there. The hunt bonus still works on chickens.

## Castle Age plan

The Castle Age is the weakest Mongol stage. You have no economic bonus left, so you need to choose between booming and fighting. Cavalry Archers are strong for the Mongols even before the Imperial Age because of the faster firing, and they work well for hit-and-run on Pikemen and slow armies. Steppe Lancers with 20% more hit points are great for raids and for picking off clumped units, and Light Cavalry kills Monks and siege cheaply. Knights and Crossbowmen are available if you need them, but they do not grow into anything special later.

Start a Castle when you can and add Thumb Ring before you mass horse archers. Many Mongol players boom to three Town Centers behind a small Cavalry Archer or Steppe Lancer group.

## Imperial Age

Mass Mangudai are the core of the late Mongol army. Pair them with Hussars, which have 30% more hit points, to absorb Skirmishers and Pikemen, and add Siege Onagers and Siege Rams with Drill. Fast siege lets you strike a group of archers or infantry and leave before the opponent reacts, and the Mangudai kill enemy siege that tries to answer. Elite Steppe Lancers are an option for players who prefer melee cavalry.

## Matchups

- Berbers with Camel Archers and Genitours, and civilizations with good Elite Skirmishers, are uncomfortable for a horse archer army. Lean on Hussars and siege.
- Civilizations with strong Onagers or Bombard Cannons punish clumped Mangudai. Spread out and use the Mangudai's speed to snipe their siege first.
- Defensive openers who wall and tower early blunt the scout rush. Do not keep making scouts into towers; go up to the Castle Age instead.
- Halberdier civilizations make Steppe Lancers and Hussars expensive to use head-on. Use Cavalry Archers and Mangudai against them.
- Strong Feudal archer civilizations like the Britons can be raided with scouts, but avoid fighting their archers on even ground.

## Common mistakes

- Not using the hunt. Lure both boars early and push the deer; without them the Mongol economy is ordinary.
- Making scouts for too long. Five to eight with Bloodlines is plenty, then think about the Castle Age.
- Forgetting to boom in the Castle Age. The Mongols need extra Town Centers to afford Mangudai and siege later.
- Massing Cavalry Archers without Thumb Ring, or moving them as a ball into Mangonels.
- Ignoring the missing armor upgrades. Mongol Hussars and Mangudai die faster than you expect against archers, so fight on your terms.

title: How to Play the Muisca
summary: The Muisca pay half the gold to age up, get extra melee armor on their archers and run their economy on healing Settlements. This guide explains Settlements, the Champi Runner and fast Castle openings, and how to play without cavalry.
body:
The Muisca are one of the South American civilizations from The Last Chieftains. They play with foot archers, Champi infantry and Monks, they have no cavalry at all, and their economy runs on Settlements instead of Mills, Lumber Camps and Mining Camps. Their two standout bonuses are cheap age ups and extra melee armor on everything that comes out of the Archery Range.

## What the Muisca are good at

Advancing to the next age costs 50 percent less gold. The Castle Age costs you 100 gold instead of 200, and the Imperial Age 400 instead of 800, which makes fast Castle and fast Imperial plans easy to afford with only a couple of gold miners.

Settlements are the drop site for every resource, support 5 population like a House, and count as two buildings for the Feudal Age requirement. The Muisca pay a third less for them, 84 wood, and they heal allied units within 3 tiles by 5, 10, 15 and 15 hit points per minute in the Dark, Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age. That healing helps your villagers recover after a raid and gives a forward army a place to patch up. Because Settlements also add population, you build fewer Houses than other civilizations.

The Champi Scout line and Archery Range units get +1, +2 and +3 melee armor in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age. Archers, Skirmishers and Slingers with extra melee armor shrug off Scout Cavalry and Men-at-Arms much better than usual. Monks regain faith twice as fast, and Caravan and Guilds are free. The team bonus makes natural gold sources last 15 percent longer.

The unique units are the Guecha Warrior, a fast javelin thrower from the Castle that heals nearby Guecha Warriors when it dies, and the Temple Guard, an anti cavalry infantry unit that attacks faster the longer it fights and can be trained at the Barracks or the Monastery. Herbalism at the Castle makes the Archer line and the Champi line 15 percent faster, and Huaracas in the Imperial Age gives Slingers +1 range and faster training.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

There is no Stable, so no cavalry of any kind, and no gunpowder. The Muisca have the fewest Blacksmith technologies in the game: no cavalry armor, no Blast Furnace and no Ring Archer Armor. Your archers win melee fights thanks to the armor bonus but struggle in long range archer duels late in the game. The Spearman line stops at Pikeman, and there is no Siege Ram. Most of your good units cost gold, so long games on a map with little gold are dangerous.

## Openings that suit them

- Champi Runner rush, written up as "Muisca Champi Runner Rush (17 pop)". It plays like a Men-at-Arms rush, and a Settlement near the front heals the runners between fights.
- Fast Castle, written up as "Muisca Fast Castle (25 pop)". The Castle Age costs only 100 gold, so you need very few gold miners and can put the extra villagers on food.
- Feudal archers. With +1 melee armor, Muisca archers handle Scout Cavalry better than most, and Settlements next to your gold and wood keep the economy safe.
- A Champi Scout drush in the Dark Age to stop the enemy walls, followed by a quick Feudal Age. Since Update 188329 the Champi Scout also deals +2 bonus damage to the Scout Cavalry line.

## Castle Age plan

The flexible plan is Crossbowmen with Herbalism, Elite Skirmishers and Slingers behind a few Pikemen or Temple Guards. Against an archer civilization, add Guecha Warriors: they move as fast as Herbalism archers, stand in front because of their shorter range and deal bonus damage to archers. Against cavalry, Temple Guards are your strongest answer; they hold up against Knights and attack faster during a long fight. Champi Warriors are your raiders and siege killers; send them with rams or Slingers.

A Monk push with Temple Guards from the same Monastery is another strong option, because your Monks recover faith twice as fast and you have every Monastery technology. Use the cheap Imperial Age to jump ahead once you have 2 or 3 Town Centers running.

## Imperial Age plan

Arbalesters, Elite Champi Warriors and Elite Temple Guards make the core, with Siege Onagers and Heavy Scorpions as siege. Huaracas Slingers, with 9 range in the Imperial Age, are your gold free unit against infantry, Monks and siege, and Elite Skirmishers take care of archers. Watch your gold carefully. The team bonus helps, but once the mines run dry the Muisca have to live on Slingers, Skirmishers and Pikemen without the Halberdier upgrade.

## Matchups

- Cavalry heavy civilizations with Hussars late in the game, such as the Magyars, Huns or Lithuanians, punish the missing Halberdier upgrade. Finish them before the gold runs out, and keep Temple Guards and Monks against their Knights.
- Archer civilizations such as the Britons, Ethiopians and Vietnamese outrange you in the late game without Ring Archer Armor. Use Guecha Warriors, Champi Warriors and Onagers rather than straight archer duels.
- Infantry civilizations are good matchups: Slingers, archers with extra melee armor and Monks all trade well.
- Siege heavy civilizations are hard because your counters to siege are Champi Warriors and Slingers; keep them ready near your army.

## Common mistakes

- Building Houses as if you played a normal civilization. Settlements add 5 population each, so plan them as Houses too.
- Putting Settlements in bad spots. Place each one where it touches two resources if possible, and never too far from the Town Center against an early rush.
- Forgetting the cheap age ups. Many Muisca players sit in Feudal Age too long when Castle Age costs only 100 gold.
- Fighting archer duels in the Imperial Age without Ring Archer Armor.
- Spending all the gold in Castle Age on Guecha Warriors. They are expensive and short ranged; use them against archers and keep the rest of the army cheaper.

title: How to Play the Persians
summary: Persian Town Centers work faster every age, which builds a villager lead, and their Knights hit archers extra hard. This guide covers the Fast Castle Knight plan, gold free Crossbowmen, War Elephants and the Savar, and how to deal with the Persian weak spots.
body:
The Persians are a cavalry civilization with an economy bonus that never switches off. Their Town Centers work faster in every age, so as long as you keep producing villagers you pull ahead, and their Knight line is built to punish archer armies.

## What the Persians are good at

- You start with 50 extra food and 50 extra wood.
- Town Centers and Docks have double hit points and work 5% faster in the Dark Age, 10% in the Feudal Age, 15% in the Castle Age and 20% in the Imperial Age. Faster work means faster villagers, Fishing Ships and technologies such as Loom, Wheelbarrow and the age ups themselves.
- Parthian Tactics is available one age early, in the Castle Age.
- In the Imperial Age you can build the Caravanserai, which heals and speeds up nearby Trade Carts.
- The Knight line has +2 attack against archers. This is the team bonus, and it applies to your own Knights, Cavaliers and Savars.

The War Elephant is the Castle unique unit: very slow, very expensive (170 food, 85 gold) and very strong in a straight fight. The Cavalier upgrades to the Savar in place of the Paladin; it has more armor than a Paladin and a cheaper upgrade. Kamandaran, the Castle Age unique technology, makes the Archer line cost 50 wood and no gold, so Persian Crossbowmen become a cheap support unit. Citadels in the Imperial Age makes Castles hit much harder, especially against rams and infantry.

The Persians also have fully upgraded Hussars, Halberdiers, Heavy Camel Riders and Hand Cannoneers, plus Siege Rams and Bombard Cannons. They lack Two-Handed Swordsman, Arbalester, Bracer, Siege Onager, Siege Engineers and Shipwright. Their Monks are weak (no Redemption, Sanctity, Illumination or Heresy), and their defenses lack Keep, Arrowslits, Bombard Tower and Fortified Wall.

The win condition is a villager lead turned into a cavalry army: reach the Castle Age early, raid with Knights while booming, and finish with Savars, Hussars and Camels backed by gold free Crossbowmen.

## Openings that suit the Persians

The opening most coaches suggest is a Fast Castle into Knights, written up as Persians Fast Castle Knights on this site. The faster Town Center makes the Castle Age arrive sooner and the extra starting resources smooth out the Dark Age. Morley Games adds a forward Monastery to convert enemy villagers while the Knights fight.

Scout Cavalry openings also suit the Persians on open maps. Two Persian tricks exist as well: a very early Drush into Fast Castle, and the Town Center drop known as the Persian douche, where you delete your Town Center and rebuild it next to the enemy's. The double hit points make the drop possible, but Hera warns that it loses to a good reaction more often than it wins, so keep it for the occasional surprise.

## Castle Age plan

Make Knights from two Stables and raid with them. Against Crossbowmen they trade very well thanks to the +2 bonus. Add Town Centers as soon as the Knights have the opponent busy; with faster Town Centers each one is worth more to you than to others.

Research Kamandaran when you need a ranged unit. Gold free Crossbowmen deal with Camels, Pikemen and Monks that would otherwise stop your Knights, and they leave your gold for cavalry. Against heavy infantry or cavalry civilizations, War Elephants from a Castle can end a fight, but they are slow and a target for Monks and Halberdiers, so only make them with a strong economy behind.

## Imperial Age plan

Savars and Hussars are the core, with Heavy Camel Riders against enemy cavalry and Halberdiers or Hand Cannoneers as support. Elite War Elephants are an option in long games, especially in team games where you can protect them. Use Siege Rams or Bombard Cannons for buildings and Trebuchets against Castles. Get the Imperial Age early; your Town Center bonus is at its highest there.

## Matchups and what gives the Persians trouble

- Monk civilizations. Your Savars and War Elephants are prime targets for conversion and you have no Heresy. Keep Hussars or Light Cavalry with the army to kill Monks.
- Halberdier and Camel heavy armies. Answer with Kamandaran Crossbowmen, Hand Cannoneers or Elite Skirmishers.
- Late game archer civilizations. Your own archers are weak without Bracer and Arbalester, but Savars with +2 vs archers do the job; get to them early.
- Water maps late in the game. Your Docks work faster, which wins the early water fight, but without Shipwright your Imperial navy falls behind.

## Common mistakes with the Persians

- Letting the Town Center idle. The bonus only gives a lead if it is always working.
- Making a War Elephant army in the Castle Age against Monks or Halberdiers.
- Forgetting Kamandaran. Gold free Crossbowmen fix many of the matchups Knights cannot handle.
- Going for long infantry games; the Persians have no Two-Handed Swordsman or Champion.
- Using the Town Center drop as your main strategy. A good wall and villager fight beats it.

title: How to Play the Poles
summary: Poles farm with the Folwark, mine stone that also gives gold and field cheap Knights after Szlachta Privileges. This guide covers the scout opening, the Castle Age Knight plan, the Obuch and Winged Hussar late game and the matchups against camel civilizations.
body:
The Poles are a cavalry civilization with an unusual economy. Their Folwark replaces the Mill and gives extra food from every Farm, their stone miners also produce gold, and their villagers heal themselves from the Feudal Age on. With Szlachta Privileges their Knights cost very little gold, so the usual Poles plan is a Castle Age with many cheap Knights backed by a strong farming economy.

## What the Poles are good at

- The Folwark is a free upgrade of the Mill. It costs the same 100 wood, supports 5 population and instantly collects 10% of a Farm's food every time a Farm next to it is built or reseeded. Over a long game that adds thousands of food; Hera's video on the last Folwark buff puts the gain at about 5000 food by the 30 minute mark.
- Stone miners generate an extra 33% of what they mine as gold. Stone mining is never wasted for the Poles, which makes Castles, towers and extra Town Centers cheaper in practice.
- Villagers regenerate 10, 15 and 20 hit points per minute in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age. Raids that do not kill villagers outright do much less lasting damage.
- Bloodlines and the Light Cavalry upgrades cost half the food.
- Szlachta Privileges cuts the gold cost of the Knight line by 60%, so a Knight costs only 30 gold.
- Lechitic Legacy gives the Scout Cavalry line trample damage, and the Winged Hussar replaces the Hussar in the Imperial Age.
- The Obuch is an infantry unit from the Castle whose hits remove armor from the target.

The weak spots are the missing Plate Barding Armor, Halberdier, Paladin and Hand Cannoneer. Poles cavalry takes more damage from arrows than most, and the civilization has no strong late game spear unit.

## Openings that suit them

The Poles Scouts into Castle Age Knights build on this site is the most common plan. It opens with a standard 21 population scout rush, mines stone from the Feudal Age for the gold bonus, and reaches the Castle Age with enough stone for a Castle and Szlachta Privileges. Morley Games built a three Stable version of this plan around the Polish stone bonus.

Fast Castle into Knights also works well, especially on closed maps. Scouts are the most produced Polish unit on the ladder, followed by Knights, which matches what players actually do. Archers are possible because Poles get Arbalester, but the civilization's bonuses favor cavalry.

## Castle Age plan

Put your first Folwark next to the Town Center and plant Farms around it. Build a second Folwark with each new Town Center. Because the instant food comes when a Farm is reseeded, it pays to queue Farm reseeds at the Folwark.

Make Knights from two or three Stables as soon as you reach the Castle Age. Mine stone instead of gold where you can, since each stone miner also gives you gold. Once you have 650 stone, build a Castle and research Szlachta Privileges. From that point your Knights cost 60 food and 30 gold, and you can keep three Stables running on a small gold income.

Obuchs from the Castle are a good second unit. They chew through armored units like Knights and Teutonic Knights and they hold up well against Camel Riders. Add Pikemen or Obuchs against enemy cavalry, and Skirmishers or Light Cavalry against archers.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age the Poles have Cavaliers, Winged Hussars with Lechitic Legacy, Heavy Mounted Crossbowmen, Arbalesters, Champions and Bombard Cannons. A good late game army is Cavaliers with Szlachta Privileges mixed with Winged Hussars, which are cheap and trample groups of archers and infantry. Siege Rams handle massed archers and buildings, and Bombard Cannons break Castles.

Without Halberdiers, your anti-cavalry is Obuchs, Pikemen and Winged Hussars in numbers. Without Plate Barding Armor, keep your cavalry away from massed Arbalesters unless Siege Rams or Onagers are in front.

## Matchups

Ladder statistics show the Poles struggle most against Khitans, Berbers and Hindustanis. All three bring strong anti-cavalry options.

- Against Camel Riders (Berbers, Hindustanis), stop making Knights and switch to Obuchs and Arbalesters. Obuchs reduce the camels' armor and beat them for less gold.
- Against archer heavy armies, get Siege Rams early and use Winged Hussars or Light Cavalry with their bonus against archers from the Polish team bonus.
- Against strong cavalry civilizations in the Imperial Age, your Cavaliers lose to Paladins head on. Use Obuchs and mass Pikemen with Bombard Cannon support, and win with economy and numbers.
- Against slower civilizations, the cheap Knight timing after Szlachta Privileges is very hard to stop.

## Common mistakes

- Placing Farms away from the Folwark. Only Farms next to it give the instant food, so build compact farm rings.
- Mining gold when stone would do the same job. For the Poles, a stone miner is also a gold miner.
- Skipping Szlachta Privileges. Knights without it cost full gold, and that is where the Polish late game power comes from.
- Fighting Arbalesters with cavalry alone. Without Plate Barding Armor, Polish Knights melt to massed arrows.
- Forgetting villager regeneration. Damaged villagers heal on their own, so you can pull them away from a raid and send them back later instead of losing them.

title: How to Play the Portuguese
summary: Every Portuguese unit costs 20 percent less gold, foragers bring in wood and research is faster. How to use the berry wood in the Dark Age, build a gold efficient army in the Castle Age and turn the Imperial Age into a gunpowder fortress.
body:
The Portuguese are a flexible civilization with one of the best navies and a strong gunpowder late game. All their units cost 20 percent less gold, ships have 10 percent more hit points, and villagers foraging berries also generate wood, about one wood for every three food. Their team bonus, which also applies to themselves, makes all technologies research 25 percent faster.

## What the Portuguese are good at

The gold discount touches every unit you make. Archers cost 36 gold instead of 45, Knights 60 instead of 75, Monks 80 instead of 100, and expensive late units such as Arbalesters, Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons save even more. Over a long game that adds up to several hundred gold, and in the late game it means you can keep making real units after other civilizations have switched to trash.

The berry bonus is the early game bonus. Six berry bushes give roughly 250 wood over the Dark and Feudal Ages, about what one lumberjack brings in. Many Portuguese builds place the Mill before the Lumber Camp because of it, and you can run a Feudal opening with fewer villagers on wood.

The unique units fill gaps. The Organ Gun, from the Castle, fires a spray of bullets that tears apart lightly armored infantry and archers. The Caravel is a warship whose shots pass through several ships. In the Imperial Age, Arquebus lets gunpowder units hit moving targets, and the Feitoria is a building that costs 20 population and slowly produces food, wood, gold and stone with no villagers.

The holes in the tree: no Hussar, no Paladin, no Heavy Cavalry Archer, no Camel Rider, no Siege Ram or Siege Onager, and no Squires. The army is strong and gold efficient but slow, and it has trouble chasing mobile units.

The win condition is a steady game that gets ahead on efficiency. You trade evenly in the Feudal Age, get more out of every gold mine in the Castle Age, and grind down the opponent in the Imperial Age with a fully upgraded ranged and gunpowder army that never runs out of gold.

## Openings

- Portuguese Mill First Scouts (18 pop) builds the Mill before the Lumber Camp so the berry wood starts early, then clicks up very fast with a hunt heavy Dark Age. It is an advanced build based on a Survivalist video.
- Portuguese Archers (20 pop) is the simpler land opening. The gold discount means two ranges need only five or six gold miners.

A Fast Castle with a Castle drop on Arena is another popular choice; Organ Guns and Monks with a gold discount make a strong closed map army. Hera also tried a defensive economic fortress plan with them in two 2026 videos.

## Castle Age plan

Crossbowmen are the usual core, with Knights alongside them against Skirmishers and Monks. Your Monastery is excellent, Monks are cheap, and faster research gets you Redemption and Atonement early. Against masses of infantry or archers, a few Organ Guns behind your Crossbowmen are very effective, but they are slow and have a minimum range, so keep Pikemen or Knights in front of them.

Use the faster research. Bodkin Arrow, Ballistics, Wheelbarrow and the farming upgrades all finish sooner, which means less time with an idle Town Center and earlier power spikes. Add a second and third Town Center as soon as your army can hold the map.

## Imperial Age

The late Portuguese army is Arbalesters or Hand Cannoneers with Halberdiers in front and Bombard Cannons behind, plus Organ Guns against infantry. Research Arquebus once you have a group of gunpowder units; Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons become far more accurate against moving targets. Bombard Towers and Keeps make your bases very hard to break.

Feitorias are for the late game once you are near the population limit and gold is running low. Each one takes 20 population space, so build them only when you can afford to give up those units.

## On water

Ships with 10 percent more hit points and a 20 percent gold discount make the Portuguese one of the best water civilizations. Fire Galleys and Galleys come out sturdier, Circumnavigation reveals the whole map and makes ships train faster, and the Caravel is great against groups of ships. You lack Shipwright and the Fast Fire Ship, so fight with War Galleys and Galleons where you can.

## Matchups

- Cavalry Archer civilizations such as the Mongols, Magyars or Tatars are hard, because you have no Heavy Cavalry Archer or Hussar to chase them. Use Elite Skirmishers, Arbalesters, towers and walls, and push them with siege so they have to fight.
- Paladin civilizations hit your slow army hard. Halberdiers and Monks are your answer, and Arbalesters behind them.
- Siege Onager civilizations punish Organ Gun and Hand Cannoneer clumps. Spread out, and use Bombard Cannons or a few Cavaliers to snipe their siege.
- Early aggressors like the Huns or Aztecs test your Dark Age. Wall, and keep your Archers home until Fletching is done.
- On water, the Vikings, Italians and Malay are the main rivals. Your ship hit points win even fights if you keep up on Dock upgrades.

## Common mistakes

- Placing the Mill late. The berry wood is your only early economic bonus, so use the berries early.
- Moving out with Organ Guns or Bombard Cannons and no units in front of them.
- Building Feitorias in the middle game while you still need the army.
- Making Cavalry Archers for the Imperial Age. They cannot be fully upgraded.
- Forgetting that your research is faster. Queue upgrades early and keep buildings busy.

title: How to Play the Romans
summary: Romans have faster villagers, infantry that gets double value from every Blacksmith armor upgrade and Scorpions at half the gold cost. This guide covers the Men-at-Arms and fast castle Scorpion openings, Centurions and Legionaries, and the civilizations that give Romans trouble.
body:
## What the Romans are good at

Romans are an infantry civilization with a simple, strong economy. Villagers gather, build and repair 5% faster, which is small per second but works on every resource from the first sheep onward, so Roman timings come out a little earlier without any extra effort.

The army bonus is in the Blacksmith. Every infantry armor upgrade gives Roman infantry twice its normal effect, so Scale Mail Armor alone turns a Man-at-Arms into a unit with +2 melee and +2 pierce armor in the Feudal Age. Militia line units and Spearmen become very hard to kill with arrows or in melee. Scorpions cost half the gold, so a Siege Workshop full of Scorpions behind your infantry is cheap, and the team bonus cuts their minimum range to 1.

Romans have two unique units. The Centurion is a heavy cavalry unit from the Castle that makes nearby Militia line units attack and move faster, so it leads infantry pushes. The Legionary replaces the Two-Handed Swordsman and Champion upgrades: it is a sturdier infantry unit you upgrade to from the Long Swordsman in the Imperial Age. Ballistas, the Castle Age tech, makes Scorpions fire 33% faster and gives the Galley line +2 attack. Comitatenses in the Imperial Age makes Militia line units, Knights and Centurions train 50% faster and gives them a charge attack.

The Archery Range is the weak building. Romans have no Arbalester, Thumb Ring or Bracer, and no Hand Cannoneer. The Stable stops at Cavalier and Light Cavalry, and the siege has no Bombard Cannon or Siege Onager. That pushes Roman armies toward infantry, Scorpions, Skirmishers and Centurions.

## Openings that suit them

Feudal Men-at-Arms are the natural start (see the build Roman Men-at-Arms). One Scale Mail Armor upgrade makes them very tough against archers and towers. For the follow-ups into Long Swordsmen and Scorpions, Hera's Roman Long Swordsman videos and TheViper's Roman guide are good to watch.

The fast castle into Scorpions is the other famous Roman opening (see the build Roman Fast Castle Scorpions). YouPudding made it popular as an all-in with no villagers after Castle Age, using the Market to buy what is missing. The version on this site keeps the economy going and adds Long Swordsmen in front of the Scorpions.

Romans are one of the easiest civilizations for beginners, since the bonuses work without any special micro.

## Castle Age plan

Long Swordsmen with Chain Mail Armor (another doubled upgrade) and Scorpions behind them are the standard Roman army. The infantry soaks the damage, and Scorpions pierce through enemy lines and kill archers and infantry clumped up in front of them. Get Ballistas once you have a Castle; with it Scorpions fire a third faster.

Add Skirmishers against archers and Pikemen against Knights. Centurions are expensive, but two or three with a group of Long Swordsmen make the infantry faster and hit harder; keep them just behind the front line so they survive.

## Imperial Age plan

Upgrade to Legionary and research Comitatenses, then push with Legionaries, Halberdiers and Heavy Scorpions. Use Trebuchets for Castles and Capped or Siege Rams for other buildings. Elite Skirmishers handle archers. Against heavy cavalry, Halberdiers with doubled armor and Scorpions behind them hold well. On water, Ballistas, the doubled Galley armor and the extra attack make Roman Galleys strong.

## Matchups

According to AoE2Insights, Romans have the highest win rate of all civilizations in 1v1 random map, close to 54%. The few matchups below 50% are Mongols, Spanish, Malians and Shu, with Ethiopians and Italians close to even.

The common theme is mobility and gunpowder. Mongol Mangudai and Steppe Lancers raid around slow infantry, so wall early and use Skirmishers, Pikemen and Scorpions at home instead of chasing. Spanish Conquistadors and Italian Genoese Crossbowmen or Hand Cannoneers punish infantry; answer with Skirmishers, Knights or Cavaliers, and Scorpions against foot units. Malian Barracks units ignore much of the Scorpion damage thanks to pierce armor; switch to Long Swordsmen and Knights there.

Romans crush slower infantry and Eagle civilizations such as Mapuche, Gurjaras, Inca, Muisca and Aztecs, where doubled armor wins every melee fight.

## Common mistakes

- Making foot archers. Without Arbalester or Thumb Ring they fall off quickly; use Skirmishers and Scorpions instead.
- Skipping the Blacksmith. The armor upgrades are the Roman bonus; infantry without them is just ordinary infantry.
- Leaving Scorpions alone in front. They need infantry ahead of them, since Knights and Mangonels kill unprotected Scorpions fast.
- Buying the Legionary upgrade too early. It costs 800 food and 400 gold, so make sure you have the economy first.
- Chasing mobile units with Long Swordsmen. Walls and a defensive Scorpion line work better against Mongols and other raiding armies.
