title: How to Play the Saracens
summary: Saracens trade at a 5% market fee, field the tankiest Camel Riders and have a full archer tree with bonus damage against buildings. This guide explains how to open with archers and a Market, when to make Mamelukes and how to use the Market without wrecking your economy.
body:
The Saracens are a flexible civilization built around one unusual tool: the Market. Their Markets cost only 75 wood, and buying or selling resources costs a flat 5% fee instead of the usual 30%. That turns the Market into a second economy. You can sell starting stone for gold, swap a surplus of wood for food, or keep a gold heavy army running when your mines are thin. Around that sit solid military bonuses. Camel units have 25% more hit points, Galleys attack 25% faster, Transport Ships are sturdier and carry more, and foot archers on the Saracen team deal +3 damage to standard buildings.

## What the Saracens do well

- Archers. The Archery Range is complete, with Arbalester, Thumb Ring and Parthian Tactics. Feudal archers that knock down houses and towers faster are a real threat.
- Camels. Saracen Camel Riders and Heavy Camel Riders survive far longer than normal ones and are the main answer to cavalry, since there is no Halberdier and no Cavalier.
- The Mameluke. This Castle unit is a camel that throws its sword at short range, with bonus damage against cavalry. It costs a lot of gold but beats Knights, Paladins and most cavalry unique units.
- Monks and siege. Every Monastery technology is available, Bimaristan lets Monks heal several nearby units at once, and Counterweights adds 15% attack to Trebuchets and the Mangonel line.

The weak points are the economy outside the Market (no Crop Rotation, no Stone Shaft Mining, no Guilds), no Shipwright for late game navies, and no Halberdier, which makes the trash game against cavalry depend on Camels.

## Openings

Saracens Archers with a Market, written up on this site, is the go to plan for many players. St4rk calls archers and a Market his default with this civilization. You open with archers from two ranges, build a cheap Market early in the Feudal Age, sell the 200 starting stone for gold, and use the extra gold for more archers and Fletching. Your archers knock down houses and palisades quickly, so a small group can stop an opponent from walling.

Tatoh's all in Tati rush is the extreme version: three ranges and villager production stopped in Feudal Age. It wins fast or loses, so save it for when you know the matchup.

Scouts and a fast Castle Age into Mamelukes or Knights are also possible, and Hera has shown fast Mamelukes working at the top level. Most players use archers, though.

## Castle Age plan

Crossbowmen with Ballistics and a few Camel Riders cover almost everything in the Castle Age. If the opponent goes Knights, add a Stable or two and make Camels; with extra hit points they win even against upgraded Knights. Against infantry, keep the Crossbowmen and add Mangonels. Use Monks with Bimaristan to keep your army healthy between fights.

The Market keeps working all game. Sell stone you do not need, sell the resource you have too much of, and buy the one your production is missing. Spirit of the Law showed that the 5% fee makes mining stone just to sell it a real option, although prices drop fast if you sell in large amounts. Keep trades small and steady.

Add Town Centers when you have control of the map. The Saracen economy has no gathering bonus, so a boom behind a good army is how you stay even.

## Imperial Age

The late game core is Arbalesters with Thumb Ring, Heavy Camel Riders or Mamelukes, and Siege Onagers or Trebuchets with Counterweights. Hussars are the cheapest way to deal with Monks and siege. When gold runs low, sell wood and food at the Market for gold instead of switching fully into trash, since Saracens lack the Halberdier. Heavy Cavalry Archers are also an option, as Saracens have every upgrade for them.

## Matchups

- Strong infantry armies are a problem for Camels. Use archers, Mangonels and Monks, and avoid sending Camels into Champions or Eagles.
- Booming civilizations punish a slow archer opening. Keep your first archers aggressive and hit their wood and gold.
- Skirmisher heavy opponents take the archer plan apart. Switch to Scouts or Knights in Feudal and Castle Age, or add Mangonels to crush Skirmisher groups.
- On water, the faster Galleys and strong Fire Ships give you a good early navy, but the lack of Shipwright shows in long naval games.

## Common mistakes

- Selling or buying in huge chunks. Prices move with every trade; small trades keep the price fair.
- Treating the Market as a replacement for villagers. It is a buffer; you still need farms and miners.
- Making Mamelukes without enough gold income. They are strong but expensive, so use them where Camels are not enough.
- Forgetting the archer bonus against buildings. Shoot down houses and palisades when no villagers are in reach.

title: How to Play the Saxons
summary: The Saxons get food and stone from every drop site, cheaper foot soldiers for every Town Center and Castle, and towers that fire double arrows from the Castle Age. How to open, how to reach the full discount and how to use Hearth Troops and Varangian Guards.
body:
The Saxons arrived with The Viking Sagas as an infantry and defensive civilization. Every drop site you build gives a little food and stone, every Town Center and Castle makes your foot soldiers cheaper, and from the Castle Age your towers and Castles fire twice the base arrows. The plan that follows from those bonuses is to boom behind towers, get to three or four Town Centers or Castles, and then flood the map with discounted infantry and foot archers. The civilization is new, so treat the meta below as early and expect it to shift.

## What the Saxons are good at

Each Mill, Lumber Camp and Mining Camp gives you 35 food and 10 stone when it is built. With a normal opening of a Mill, two Lumber Camps and a Mining Camp, that is 140 food and 40 stone before the Feudal Age. The food helps you click up a little earlier. The stone adds up to a Watch Tower in the Feudal Age and still enough for a Town Center in the Castle Age without any stone mining.

Foot soldiers, meaning infantry and foot archers, cost 5% less for each Town Center or Castle you control, up to 20%. Your starting Town Center already counts, so you have 5% from the first minute. The discount only counts finished buildings.

From the Castle Age, Saxon towers fire two arrows with nobody inside and Castles fire ten. Repairers work 25% faster through the team bonus, which helps you hold a tower or a forward Castle. Longships and Catapult Galleons have 20% more HP.

The unique unit is the Hearth Troop, a heavy infantryman with high pierce armor that throws a javelin before it closes in. The javelin does bonus damage to archers and recharges after 15 seconds. It costs wood and gold, which is easier to afford in the Castle Age than food. Saxons also get the Varangian Guard at the Barracks, a strong Castle Age infantry unit that generates gold while it fights other units. Shield Wall gives infantry +1/+1 armor for every 15 infantry nearby, up to +3/+3. Clerical Recruitment gives Monks +1 conversion range and makes them train 33% faster.

The gaps are in the late game. There is no Blast Furnace, so infantry hits less hard than other infantry civilizations. Cavalry lacks Plate Barding Armor and the Paladin. There is no Siege Onager, Bombard Cannon or Hand Cannoneer, and no Stone Shaft Mining.

## Openings that suit them

- Saxons Archers with Tower (civ-saxons-archers-tower) is the opening Hera showed when the civilization came out. The drop site stone pays for a tower on your gold, and the archers pressure while you wall.
- Saxons Fast Castle into Town Centers (civ-saxons-fast-castle-town-centers) goes straight to the Castle Age and builds two Town Centers at once, which brings the foot soldier discount to 15%.
- Men-at-Arms and tower rushes also work well, since the stone from drop sites covers a tower without mining.

## Castle Age plans

Get your extra Town Centers first. Three Town Centers give a 15% discount, and a fourth Town Center or a Castle takes you to the full 20%. A Castle also lets you train Hearth Troops.

The common Castle Age army on the ladder is Varangian Guards with Skirmishers or Crossbowmen. Varangian Guards trade well with most units and pay back part of their cost in gold while fighting. Get Gambesons so they hold up against Skirmishers. Hearth Troops replace them against archer-heavy armies. Pikemen deal with Knights.

Use your towers. A tower near your gold or a forward position fires double arrows in this age, and garrisoned archers add more. Fight near them when you can.

## Imperial Age

Research Shield Wall and keep your infantry together, since the armor bonus counts the infantry around each unit. A large group of Hearth Troops, Varangian Guards and Halberdiers with Arbalesters behind is hard to break with arrows. Add Siege Rams and Trebuchets for buildings and Monks with Clerical Recruitment to convert siege from a distance. Your Onagers are fine, but you lack the Siege Onager.

## Matchups

The Saxons are still new, and the matchup data on AoE2Insights rests on a small number of games. Early results show them doing well against Persians and Varangians and struggling most against the Khmer, whose elephants and strong farming are hard for an infantry army to handle. Against elephants, mass Halberdiers and use Monks with the extra range.

Some things hold from the units themselves. Hand Cannoneers beat both Hearth Troops and Varangian Guards. Mounted archers can kite slow infantry, so keep Skirmishers and Crossbowmen with your army. Champions and other units with bonus damage against shock infantry beat Varangian Guards, so use Hearth Troops or Halberdiers against them.

## Common mistakes

- Building camps only for the bonus. A Lumber Camp costs 100 wood for 35 food and 10 stone, which is a poor trade by itself. Build a new camp whenever your villagers would otherwise walk far.
- Spending the drop site stone early. Keep enough for your Castle Age Town Centers.
- Counting unfinished Town Centers. The discount starts when the building is done.
- Splitting the infantry. Shield Wall needs 15 infantry together for each step.
- Relying on cavalry late. Without Plate Barding and Blast Furnace it falls behind.

title: How to Play the Shu
summary: The Shu are a slow, hard-hitting archer and siege civilization. Lumberjacks that also make food pay for a wood-heavy army of Archers and War Chariots, protected by White Feather Guards that slow everything they hit.
body:
## What the Shu are good at

Shu lumberjacks generate 0.7 food for every 10 wood they bring in. Ten lumberjacks give roughly the food of one farmer, which is not huge, but it adds up over the whole game and lets you keep more villagers on wood. Archery Range and Blacksmith technologies for archers cost 25% less, and land siege and Lou Chuans move 10% faster in the Castle Age and 15% faster in the Imperial Age. The team bonus gives foot archers except Skirmishers 2 extra line of sight.

The unique units both serve the archer and siege plan. The War Chariot replaces the Scorpion line at the Siege Workshop: a tough, mobile bolt thrower with cavalry armor and two attack modes, Focus Fire for one target and everything behind it, and Barrage for spreading bolts over a wide area. Since the Viking Sagas patch it costs 75 food and 90 gold. The White Feather Guard, trained at the Castle for 60 food and 15 gold, is a cheap and durable spear unit whose attacks slow enemies, so cavalry that dives your archers gets stuck. Coiled Serpent Array (Castle Age) gives Spearmen and White Feather Guards extra hit points when they stand near each other, and Bolt Magazine (Imperial Age) makes the Archer line, War Chariots and Lou Chuans fire extra projectiles. Liu Bei, the hero, heals nearby units.

The Shu also get the Three Kingdoms regional units: Hei Guang Cavalry instead of the Knight line, the Traction Trebuchet instead of the Trebuchet, and the Lou Chuan at the Dock.

The weak side is mobility and melee damage. There is no Hussar, no Bloodlines, no Iron Casting, no Blast Furnace and no Parthian Tactics, so Shu cavalry is poor and their infantry hits softly. The Monastery lacks Sanctity, Redemption, Herbal Medicine and Block Printing, and there is no Bombard Cannon or Hand Cannoneer.

The win condition is a slow push that the opponent cannot break: a wall of White Feather Guards or Halberdiers in front, Arbalesters and War Chariots behind, and fast siege to take buildings.

## Openings that suit them

The Shu Archers build on this site is the standard opening and plays to every bonus: extra villagers on wood, cheaper Fletching, archers that see further. The other well-known plan is a fast Castle Age into War Chariots, also written up here, which became famous through Red Phosphoru and caught many opponents off guard. Expect a better prepared opponent now that the chariot costs more and trains slower.

In the Dark Age, many Shu players put only five villagers on sheep and send the next ones to wood, because the lumberjacks start the food trickle early.

## Castle Age plan

After an archer opening, keep making Archers into Crossbowmen and take the cheap upgrades early. Add White Feather Guards once your Castle is up, or Pikemen before that, so enemy Knights and Scout Cavalry cannot reach your archers. War Chariots fit into any Castle Age army: Barrage mode against a spread-out mass, Focus Fire against a tight line or a single strong unit.

A ram push is also good for the Shu, since faster rams reach the enemy Town Center quickly. Fill them with infantry and send White Feather Guards alongside.

## Imperial Age

Research Bolt Magazine soon after the Imperial Age arrives; it is the strongest Shu upgrade. Arbalesters with extra bolts, War Chariots, and a front line of Halberdiers and White Feather Guards with Coiled Serpent Array make the core army. Traction Trebuchets take down Castles and can hit units as well, and Siege Rams with the speed bonus are dangerous. Bring Liu Bei with the main army to heal it between fights. On water, Lou Chuans with Bolt Magazine are fast and dangerous.

## Matchups

- Onagers and Siege Onagers punish massed Shu archers, and you have weak cavalry to dive them. Split your archers, and send Hei Guang Cavalry or your own Onagers at the siege.
- Skirmisher-heavy opponents slow the archer plan. Switch to White Feather Guards, Champions and rams, which Skirmishers cannot hold.
- Fast raiding civilizations like the Mongols or Magyars run circles around a slow Shu army. Wall early, keep towers at the gold and wood, and let the archers defend rather than chase.
- Eagle Warriors from the Aztecs or Maya beat archers. Answer with White Feather Guards and Champions.
- Prepared opponents answer the War Chariot rush with fast melee units such as Knights or Camel Riders that catch the chariots before they mass, so do not expect it to work twice against the same player.

## Common mistakes

- Counting on the lumberjack food as your main food source. It helps, but you still need sheep, boars, berries and Farms.
- Building Hei Guang Cavalry as if they were Knights. They have low hit points, no Bloodlines and lose badly to Pikemen and camels, so use them to snipe siege and clean up.
- Leaving War Chariots in the wrong mode, or sending them without a front line.
- Forgetting Bolt Magazine, or researching it late.
- Chasing raiders with a slow army. Hold positions and let towers and archers do the work.

title: How to Play the Sicilians
summary: Sicilian units take 40 percent less bonus damage, and Donjons give them a tower that trains Serjeants. This guide covers the Donjon rush and Donjon scout openings, Castle Age Knights and booms with fast Town Centers, and the matchups to watch.
body:
The Sicilians are an infantry and cavalry civilization built around one defensive trick and one unusual building. Their land units take 40 percent less bonus damage, so counter units hurt them less, and they build Donjons, small forts that shoot like towers and train their unique infantry, the Serjeant. They are flexible enough to rush, boom or turtle, and they need more game knowledge than most civilizations to play well.

## What the Sicilians are good at

The bonus damage reduction applies to every land military unit except siege. A Spearman deals its anti cavalry bonus to your Scout Cavalry and Knights at 60 percent strength, Skirmishers do less to your archers, and Camel Riders and Halberdiers lose a lot of their edge against your Cavaliers. The effect lasts all game, into the late trash fights.

Donjons replace the Watch Tower line. A Donjon costs 50 wood and 175 stone, can be built from the Dark Age and starts shooting in the Feudal Age. It trains Serjeants and the Spearman line, and it unlocks the Stable and Archery Range in place of a Barracks. Serjeants are armored infantry that cost 55 food and 25 gold, get a big free upgrade when you reach the Castle Age, and can build more Donjons themselves. You also start with 100 extra stone, enough for a first Donjon without mining.

The economy bonuses come later. Farm upgrades give 125 percent more food than normal, so Horse Collar, Heavy Plow and Crop Rotation are worth more to you. In the Castle Age your Town Centers build twice as fast and your Castles and other fortifications 50 percent faster, which makes a quick boom or a fast forward Castle easier. First Crusade at the Castle spawns five Serjeants at each Town Center, up to five Town Centers, and makes your units harder to convert. Hauberk in the Imperial Age gives the Knight line +1 melee and +2 pierce armor. The team bonus makes Transport Ships 50 percent cheaper with more line of sight.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

The Sicilians have no Paladin and no Hussar, so the Cavalier with Hauberk is your heavy cavalry and Light Cavalry is your raider. The Archer line lacks Thumb Ring and Ring Archer Armor, and there is no Hand Cannoneer or Bombard Cannon. Since The Viking Sagas, the Mounted Crossbowman replaces the Cavalry Archer and can be upgraded with Cranequins. Monks miss Redemption, Atonement, Theocracy, Block Printing and Heresy. Donjons stand in for every tower and Keep, and the economy lacks Two-Man Saw and Treadmill Crane. Early on there is no economic help at all, so a strong Dark Age rush can hurt you.

## Openings that suit them

- Donjon rush, written up as "Sicilians Donjon Rush (21 pop)". A few villagers build a Donjon near the enemy woodline or gold, then Serjeants take over and build more Donjons. It is a tower rush that needs fewer villagers once it starts.
- Scouts from a Donjon, written up as "Sicilians Scouts from a Donjon (19 pop)". The Donjon unlocks the Stable, so you skip the Barracks, save wood, and get a home tower that protects the berries. Your Scout Cavalry also takes much less damage from Spearmen.
- Fast Castle into Knights or a Town Center boom. The quick Town Center build time and the farm bonus suit a greedy Castle Age, and Sicilian Knights shrug off Pikemen and Camel Riders better than most.

## Castle Age plan

After a Donjon opening, Serjeants become solid main infantry after the free Castle Age upgrade, and every Serjeant can keep building Donjons near your resources and the front. After a scout or fast Castle opening, Knights are the standard choice. The reduced bonus damage lets them stay in fights against Pikemen and camels much longer. Add Crossbowmen or Mounted Crossbowmen for ranged support, and Mangonels against massed archers.

Use the fast Town Center build time. A Town Center that takes half as long to finish pays back sooner, so drop one or two behind your first push. If you are under pressure, First Crusade with three or more Town Centers puts 15 or more Serjeants on the field at once.

## Imperial Age plan

Hauberk Cavaliers are among the toughest cavalry in the game, and they pair well with Siege Onagers, Elite Serjeants or Champions, and Halberdiers. Siege Rams handle buildings. Arbalesters are usable thanks to the reduced bonus damage from Skirmishers, but they lack two archer technologies, so use them as support behind your Cavaliers. Trash wars also favor you, because your Halberdiers, Skirmishers and Light Cavalry all take less bonus damage from the enemy's trash.

## Matchups

- Strong Dark Age and early Feudal rushers such as the Aztecs, Goths or Japanese hit you before your bonuses matter. Scout early, wall and keep a Donjon at home.
- Archer civilizations such as the Britons or Ethiopians outrange your Donjons and outshoot your archers late. Use Knights, Light Cavalry and Siege Onagers, and do not try to win a long archer duel.
- Monk heavy civilizations can be a problem without Heresy; First Crusade gives some conversion resistance, and Light Cavalry should hunt Monks.
- Counter unit civilizations such as the Byzantines are a good matchup, because their trash and camels lose much of their bonus damage against you.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the Donjon like a Watch Tower. It costs 175 stone and trains units, so place it where its Serjeants can reach the next target.
- Forgetting the extra 100 stone. Either spend it on a Donjon or sell it early in the Feudal Age for a faster Castle Age.
- Booming in the Castle Age with one builder per Town Center. Sicilian Town Centers build twice as fast; use that to take more of them.
- Making Hussar style raids with Light Cavalry late. You have no Hussar, so raid with Cavaliers or Serjeants instead.
- Skipping farm upgrades. With the Sicilian bonus they are among the best technologies you can buy.

title: How to Play the Slavs
summary: Slavs have the fastest farmers in the game, cheap siege and free infantry upgrades, but almost no archers. This guide explains how to survive the early game, push with cavalry and siege in the Castle Age and win the late game with Boyars and Druzhina infantry.
body:
The Slavs are an infantry and siege civilization with a strong cavalry side. Their economy bonus works on farms, so they start slow and get stronger the longer the game runs, and their military plan is to hit with cheap siege behind a solid melee army.

## What the Slavs are good at

- Farmers work 15% faster. That is one of the largest farming bonuses in the game, and it kicks in as soon as your villagers move to farms in the Feudal Age.
- Arson and Gambesons are free. Arson (Feudal Age) helps infantry burn buildings, Gambesons (Castle Age) gives the Militia line extra pierce armor.
- Siege Workshop units cost 15% less, so Mangonels, Battering Rams and Scorpions are cheaper, and so is every later Onager or Siege Ram.
- Monks move 20% faster.
- Barracks, Archery Ranges, Stables and Siege Workshops each give +5 population. That is the team bonus, and it means you build fewer Houses as you add production.

The unique unit is the Boyar, a heavily armored Castle cavalry unit that takes little melee damage and fills the role of the Paladin, which the Slavs lack. Detinets, the Castle Age unique technology, replaces 40% of the stone cost of Castles and towers with wood. Druzhina in the Imperial Age gives infantry splash damage to the units next to their target, which wins large infantry fights.

The weak spot is archers. Slavs have no Thumb Ring, Bracer or Arbalester, so their Crossbowmen and Skirmishers fall off. They also lack Hand Cannoneer, Bombard Cannon, Paladin, Keep and Bombard Tower, and their navy is poor without Bracer and Shipwright. Their Monks are excellent apart from Fervor.

The win condition is a mid game push. You want to survive the Feudal Age, reach the Castle Age with a strong farm economy, then attack with Knights or infantry plus discounted siege before the opponent's Town Centers pay off. In the Imperial Age, Boyars, Druzhina Champions and Siege Onagers carry you.

## Openings that suit the Slavs

The usual opening is Scout Cavalry, written up as Slavs Scouts into Castle Push on this site. The Stable gives +5 population, which saves one House in the Feudal Age, and a second Stable saves another. Hera plays it with double Stables and Bloodlines in the Feudal Age, then a one Town Center push with Knights and siege.

Men-at-Arms are also good, since Arson is free and your infantry is fully upgraded. On closed maps such as Arena, a Fast Castle into Knights or Boyars with siege is common. Avoid archer openings; the Slavs are the wrong civilization for them.

## Castle Age plan

Your strongest Castle Age move is a push. Make Knights from two Stables, add a Siege Workshop and bring Mangonels or Battering Rams with them. Mangonels kill the Skirmishers, Crossbowmen and Pikemen that stop Knights, and rams take down towers and Town Centers. The 15% discount makes losing a siege unit hurt much less.

Long Swordsmen and Pikemen are a cheaper alternative. They get Gambesons for free, so they handle archer fire better than most infantry, and they pair well with rams.

Boom with farms behind the push. Your farmers are 15% faster, so the same number of farms supports a larger army than for other civilizations. Detinets is useful when you want towers or Castles while short on stone.

## Imperial Age plan

Boyars replace the Paladin as heavy cavalry, and fully upgraded Hussars cover raiding and Monk hunting. Champions and Halberdiers with Druzhina become very strong in large fights. Add Siege Onagers or Siege Rams, both cheaper for you, and Trebuchets for Castles. Monks with full upgrades and extra speed can turn fights against expensive units such as Elephants or Paladins.

## Matchups and what gives the Slavs trouble

- Archer civilizations in the late game. Arbalesters with Thumb Ring outshoot anything ranged you make. Use Onagers, Hussars, Boyars and Gambesons infantry, and close the distance quickly.
- Cavalry Archer and Mounted Crossbowman civilizations. Your Skirmishers lack upgrades; rely on Hussars, Knights and siege to force fights.
- Water and hybrid maps. Your navy is below average and fish hide your farming bonus.
- Fast aggressive starts. Your economy is behind until farms are up, so wall the woodline and keep a few Spearmen in the Feudal Age.

## Common mistakes with the Slavs

- Waiting too long to start farms. Your bonus only works on farms, so move hunters there early.
- Building archers because the opponent has infantry; use siege and cavalry instead.
- Building Houses you do not need. Each military building already gives 5 population.
- Booming three Town Centers instead of pushing. Hera's games show the Slavs do best when they force the fight in the Castle Age.
- Leaving siege without protection; cheap siege is still siege.

title: How to Play the Spanish
summary: Spanish play a safe early game, use fast builders to drop a Castle and win the Castle Age with Conquistadors, then scale with gold free Blacksmith upgrades and fast firing gunpowder. This guide covers the openings, unit choices and the matchups that trouble them.
body:
The Spanish are a gunpowder and Monk civilization with one of the strongest Castle Age unique units in the game, the Conquistador. Their early game has no economic bonus, so the usual Spanish plan is to play a safe Dark and Feudal Age, reach the Castle Age on time and build a Castle for Conquistadors. In the late game they have a near complete tech tree and very strong gunpowder.

## What the Spanish are good at

- Builders work 30% faster (20% on Wonders). Castles, towers, walls and Town Centers go up quickly, which makes Castle drops and tower plays safer.
- Blacksmith upgrades cost no gold. You pay only food for every attack and armor upgrade.
- You receive 20 gold for every technology you research, including economy upgrades. Over a game this adds up to a lot of free gold.
- Gunpowder units fire 18% faster, so Spanish Hand Cannoneers, Bombard Cannons and Conquistadors deal more damage than other versions.
- The Conquistador is a mounted Hand Cannoneer from the Castle (75 food and 60 gold). It kills infantry, archers and Monks very fast and does not need many upgrades to work.
- The Missionary is a mounted Monk, and Inquisition makes Spanish Monks and Missionaries convert faster.
- Supremacy turns villagers into fighters in the Imperial Age with more attack, armor and hit points.
- The team bonus gives Trade Carts and Trade Cogs 25% more gold.

The tech tree has every trash unit fully upgraded (Hussar, Halberdier, Elite Skirmisher), Paladins and Champions. The gap is foot archers: the Spanish have no Crossbowman, so Feudal archers have no follow up. Since The Viking Sagas they also train the Mounted Crossbowman instead of the Cavalry Archer.

## Openings that suit them

The opening most players use now is the Spanish Fast Castle Conquistadors build on this site. It mines stone during the Feudal Age, clicks up to the Castle Age with an all-in on one strong unit and uses the builder bonus to put a Castle down quickly. Spanish reach the Castle Age earlier on average than most civilizations on the ladder, which fits this plan. On Arena and other closed maps the Castle can go right next to the opponent's base.

On Arabia, Hera recommends a safer start. Scouts into Knights, a tower rush that leaves you mining stone, or a quick wall into Fast Castle all work. The main rule is to avoid a long Feudal Age war. Without Crossbowmen and without any Feudal bonus, the Spanish lose that kind of game to civilizations built for it.

## Castle Age plan

Once you have a Castle, Conquistadors are the main unit. Use them in groups of five or more and target archers, infantry and Monks. They are mounted, so they can retreat when Skirmishers or Camel Riders come. Research Bloodlines, Husbandry and the barding armors; the armors cost only food for you.

The other common Castle Age choices are Knights with Elite Skirmishers, or a Town Center boom behind a few Conquistadors. Monks with Inquisition are strong against slow armies, and Hera has a video making the case that Missionaries, which move faster than Monks, are now a real option.

Every economy upgrade gives 20 gold back, so research Double-Bit Axe, Horse Collar, Bow Saw, Heavy Plow and the mining upgrades early.

## Imperial Age plan

The late game army is flexible. Paladins and Hussars with free gold Blacksmith upgrades handle most armies, Hand Cannoneers and Elite Conquistadors with faster firing shred infantry and archers, and Bombard Cannons break buildings. Champions and Halberdiers round out the Barracks. Trade is a strong win condition in team games because of the trade bonus. Supremacy makes your villagers defend themselves well against late raids.

The siege workshop is weaker than the rest: no Siege Engineers, Heavy Scorpion or Siege Onager. Rely on Bombard Cannons and Siege Rams.

## Matchups

Ladder statistics show the hardest matchups for the Spanish are Tupi, Italians and Huns.

- Against Cavalry Archers (Huns), you cannot answer with Crossbowmen. Use Elite Skirmishers and Hussars, and bring Conquistadors when you can force a fight near your own base.
- Against Genoese Crossbowmen and Condottieri (Italians), Knights and Conquistadors both have trouble. Use Elite Skirmishers and Champions, and Siege Rams against the crossbows.
- Against early Champi raids from the Tupi, defend with Spearmen and towers in Feudal, which build quickly for you, and reach the Castle Age to use Conquistadors.
- Civilizations that rely on infantry and foot archers suffer against Conquistadors, which is why the Spanish do well against many of them.

## Common mistakes

- Feudal archer play. The Spanish cannot upgrade to Crossbowman, so archers waste gold.
- Going Conquistadors every game in the same way. A good opponent who expects them prepares Skirmishers and Camel Riders, so vary the timing and the support units.
- Forgetting the builder bonus. Quick walls, towers and Castles all benefit from it.
- Researching techs late. Each one refunds 20 gold, so economy upgrades pay for themselves faster for the Spanish.
- Leaving Conquistadors alone against Skirmishers. Pull them back and send Knights or Hussars in instead.

title: How to Play the Tatars
summary: Extra food from sheep, free Thumb Ring and Parthian Tactics and a strong hill bonus make the Tatars one of the best Cavalry Archer civilizations. How to open, when to switch to Cavalry Archers and how to use the high ground.
body:
The Tatars are a mounted archer civilization with a food rich start. Sheep and other herdable animals contain 50 percent more food, units deal 50 percent bonus damage from higher ground instead of the usual 25, and Thumb Ring and Parthian Tactics are free. From the Castle Age on, every new Town Center spawns two sheep. Their team bonus gives mounted archers extra line of sight.

## What the Tatars are good at

The sheep bonus adds roughly 400 food over the eight starting sheep, and every Castle Age Town Center adds two more fat sheep. That food goes into Scout Cavalry, an earlier age up or later Farms, which saves wood for Archery Ranges and Town Centers. It makes every early plan a little easier.

Free Thumb Ring is the reason Tatar Cavalry Archers are strong the moment the Castle Age lands; other civilizations have to spend 300 food and 250 gold and research time first. Silk Armor, the Castle unique technology, gives the Scout Cavalry line, Steppe Lancers and mounted archers +1 melee and +1 pierce armor. Add free Parthian Tactics in the Imperial Age and Tatar Heavy Cavalry Archers are among the best in the game.

The Keshik, the Castle unique unit, is a sturdy medium cavalry unit that earns a little gold every time it hits an enemy unit. It is cheaper in gold than a Knight and good at raiding. The Flaming Camel, made at the Siege Workshop in the Imperial Age, explodes on contact and deals heavy bonus damage to cavalry and elephants. Timurid Siegecraft gives Trebuchets two extra range.

The weak spots are infantry and Monks. The Tatars have no Champion, no Chain Mail Armor and no Supplies, and their Monastery lacks Redemption, Heresy and Faith. They also lack Arbalester, Paladin, Bombard Cannon and Siege Onager.

The win condition is mobility. You stay on the move with Cavalry Archers and light cavalry, fight from hills, refuse fights you cannot win and wear the opponent down until a Trebuchet and Siege Ram push finishes the game.

## Openings

- Tatars Scouts (20 pop) uses the extra sheep food to keep two Stables busy in the Feudal Age without hurting the Castle Age timing.
- Tatars Fast Castle into Cavalry Archers (25+2) reaches the Castle Age with two Archery Ranges and the starting stone for two more Town Centers, each of which spawns two sheep.

Steppe Lancer rushes are another option; Morley Games has a build that hits with Lancers at around 14 minutes and leans on the hill bonus. Archer openings also work, since the free Thumb Ring helps foot archers too, although you lack the Arbalester.

## Castle Age plan

Cavalry Archers from two or three ranges are the default. Get Bloodlines, Husbandry and Silk Armor, plus Bodkin Arrow and Padded Archer Armor. Keep them in one group and use hit and run: shoot, step back, shoot again. Against Skirmishers, add Light Cavalry, Steppe Lancers or Keshiks, which beat them easily, and against Pikemen simply shoot from range.

Steppe Lancers with Silk Armor are excellent raiders. A small group in the opponent's woodline while your Cavalry Archers hold the army forces bad fights. Keshiks fill a similar role and earn gold while fighting, which helps once mines get thin.

Use the Castle Age sheep bonus. Each new Town Center spawns two sheep worth 150 food each, so a second and third Town Center pay part of their cost back right away.

## Imperial Age

Heavy Cavalry Archers with free Parthian Tactics and Silk Armor are the core. In front of them, use Hussars when gold is short, or Elite Steppe Lancers or Elite Keshiks when it is not. For buildings, Trebuchets with Timurid Siegecraft outrange every Castle and Bombard Tower, and Siege Rams break walls. Against heavy cavalry and elephants, a few Flaming Camels driven into the enemy blob do a lot of damage for their cost.

## The hill bonus

Units on higher ground deal 50 percent more damage for you instead of 25. That applies to all your units and to the first arrow of towers and Castles, though not to Town Center arrows. Take fights from hills whenever you can, place towers and Castles on high ground, and pull your Cavalry Archers back uphill when the opponent chases.

## Matchups

- Skirmisher and Pikeman armies from civilizations like the Vietnamese or Byzantines are slow but hard to kill with arrows. Kill the Skirmishers with Light Cavalry, Steppe Lancers or Keshiks, then shoot the Pikemen.
- Strong foot archer civilizations, such as the Britons and Ethiopians, outrange you late because you lack the Arbalester. Fight them with Cavalry Archers on the move and Hussars or Keshiks that dive onto the archers.
- Monk civilizations convert your cavalry easily because you lack Heresy and Faith. Kill Monks with Light Cavalry and never leave units standing near a Monastery.
- Cavalry Archer mirrors against the Mongols, Turks or Magyars come down to upgrades, hills and micro. Silk Armor and free Thumb Ring give you the edge in the Castle Age.
- Heavy infantry civilizations like the Goths or Japanese are fine if you stay mobile, but avoid getting cornered.

## Common mistakes

- Making infantry. Without the second armor upgrade and Champions, your foot soldiers lose to almost anything.
- Ignoring elevation. The hill bonus is half of what makes Tatar armies win fights.
- Splitting Cavalry Archers into small groups that get caught by Skirmishers or Knights.
- Forgetting Silk Armor in the Castle Age; it is the upgrade that lets your light units survive arrows.
- Leaving cavalry near enemy Monks.

title: How to Play the Teutons
summary: Teutons are slow but very hard to kill: cheap Farms, free Murder Holes, extra melee armor for infantry and cavalry from the Castle Age, and Monks that heal from twice the range. This guide covers their fast castle openings, the Knight and Teutonic Knight plans, and how to cope with faster civilizations.
body:
## What the Teutons are good at

Teutons are the classic turtle civilization that hits back hard. Farms cost 40% less wood (36 instead of 60), which saves hundreds of wood during the switch from hunt and berries to farming and makes fast castle builds smooth. Murder Holes and Herbal Medicine are free, Town Centers hold 10 more villagers and towers hold twice as many units, so Teuton bases are difficult to raid. Monks heal from twice the normal range, and the team bonus makes units and buildings harder to convert.

Since The Viking Sagas the armor bonus covers both infantry and mounted units: +1 melee armor in the Castle Age and +2 in the Imperial Age. Knights, Paladins, Halberdiers and Champions all shrug off melee hits better than their counterparts, which makes Teuton Knights strong against Pikemen and Teuton Halberdiers strong against everything that hits in melee.

The unique unit is the Teutonic Knight, a slow, heavily armored infantry unit from the Castle with very high melee attack. It wins almost every melee fight it reaches but struggles to catch anything that runs. Ironclad in the Castle Age gives siege weapons +4 melee armor, so Teuton rams and Trebuchets survive enemy infantry and cavalry much longer. Crenellations in the Imperial Age gives Castles +3 range and lets garrisoned infantry shoot arrows.

The weak side is speed. Teutons have no Husbandry, no Light Cavalry and no Hussar, and their archers miss Thumb Ring, Bracer and Arbalester. They also lack Siege Ram and Gold Shaft Mining. The Viking Sagas replaced their Cavalry Archers with Mounted Crossbowmen. Plan for Knights or Paladins, Halberdiers, Teutonic Knights, Skirmishers, Monks and siege.

## Openings that suit them

A fast castle into Knights is the common open-map plan (see the build Teutons Fast Castle Knights). The cheap Farms let you put more villagers on wood and gold in the Feudal Age, so the click to Castle Age comes on time even though Teutons have no early military bonus. Morley Games adds Monks to the Knights to break through walls and keep the Knights healed.

On Arena and other closed maps, Teutons are one of the best boom civilizations. CiaoPlatforma's 23+2 fast castle into a Town Center boom uses the cheap Farms and the safe base (see the build Teutons Arena Fast Castle Boom).

HeBroGaming plays a 19 villager Feudal tower rush on Arena. Teuton towers hold ten villagers and get Murder Holes for free, which suits that plan.

## Castle Age plan

Knights are the main unit at most levels. The +1 melee armor in the Castle Age makes them hard for Pikemen to stop, and the free Murder Holes and garrison bonuses keep your base safe while they are away. Add Monks: with double healing range they can keep a group of Knights fresh between fights, and they convert enemy Knights or elephants.

Against archers and siege, Knights do the job. Against heavy infantry or other Knight civilizations, make Teutonic Knights from a Castle and back them with Halberdiers. Research Ironclad if you plan to push with Battering Rams or Capped Rams.

## Imperial Age plan

Paladins and Halberdiers with +2 melee armor make up a strong late army, with Elite Teutonic Knights in front when the opponent fights in melee. Siege Onagers and Bombard Cannons handle archers and buildings, and Trebuchets with Ironclad are hard to snipe with cavalry. Crenellations turns Castles into a defensive line that infantry garrisons can strengthen.

## Matchups

AoE2Insights shows Teutons at a 50% win rate in 1v1 random map. Their hardest opponents are Mongols, Shu, Vikings, Khitans, Japanese and Huns, and their best results come against Gurjaras, Slavs, Goths, Muisca, Khmer and Aztecs.

Speed and archers decide most of the bad matchups. Mongols and Huns run circles around slow Teuton armies with Mangudai, Tarkans and Cavalry Archers. Wall early, keep Skirmishers and Pikemen at home, and pick a moment to hit with Knights when their army is away, since chasing them only wastes time. Japanese and Vikings field fast infantry and good archers; use Knights against the archers and Teutonic Knights or Halberdiers against their infantry.

Teutons do well against slow, melee-heavy civilizations. Goths, Aztecs, Muisca and Gurjaras rely on infantry or camels that Teutonic Knights and armored Halberdiers beat head on.

## Common mistakes

- Chasing fast units with slow units. Teutonic Knights and Knights without Husbandry never catch Cavalry Archers; use walls, Skirmishers and Monks.
- Forgetting the cheap Farms. Put the saved wood into a faster Castle Age or an extra Town Center.
- Building foot archers into the late game. Without Thumb Ring, Bracer or Arbalester they fall behind quickly.
- Leaving Monks at home. With double healing range they belong next to the army, healing Knights between fights.
- Ignoring Ironclad. Rams with +4 melee armor survive a lot longer against Knights and infantry.

title: How to Play the Tupi
summary: Tupi swarm the map with Blackwood Archers that train in pairs, back them with Ibirapema Warriors and get part of every lost unit back. This guide covers the Champi and archer openings, the fast Castle Age into Blackwood Archers or Ibirapema Warriors, and the matchups to plan for.
body:
The Tupi are an archer and infantry civilization from The Last Chieftains. Like the other South American civilizations they have no Stable, use the Settlement as their drop site for every resource, start with a Champi Scout, and use the Champi line in place of Militia. Their bonuses are easy to use because they work in the background:

- They get 25 of every resource once the first Town Center is built.
- Up to five villagers can hide in each Settlement, much like Khmer houses.
- Fallen units, including villagers but not ships or siege, return 15% of their cost.
- Barracks and Archery Range technologies cost 50% less food, which covers Crossbowman, Arbalester, Champi upgrades, Squires and more.

Their team bonus makes towers, Kreposts, Donjons and Castles provide 10 population, so every Tupi tower doubles as two houses.

## The unique units

The Blackwood Archer comes from the Castle in pairs. For roughly the cost of one Crossbowman you get two archers that take half a population slot each, attack quickly and move faster than other foot archers. Each one is fragile with 20 hit points, but a Castle can produce them about as fast as three Archery Ranges make Crossbowmen. In the Imperial Age, Curare adds poison damage that ignores armor, so they keep up against high armor units. Spirit of the Law estimates they appear in about two thirds of Tupi games.

The Ibirapema Warrior is trained at the Barracks in the Castle Age. It is a sturdy infantry unit with 80 hit points that hits everything in a cone in front of it, so it shreds groups of infantry and light cavalry. It costs 60 gold, which makes it a support unit for most players, but Morley Games uses a fast Castle Age straight into Ibirapemas with good results.

## Openings

Two fast Castle Age builds cover most games and are both written up on this site. Tupi Fast Castle into Blackwood Archers collects stone during the Feudal Age, builds a Castle at home or forward on arrival and pumps out pairs of archers. Tupi Fast Castle into Ibirapema Warriors reaches the Castle Age at around 13:35 and needs no stone at all, only gold.

For Feudal play, a Champi Scout drush into archers or a Champi Runner opening are the usual choices. The cheaper Champi Runner upgrade and the 15% refund on lost units make early fights less costly. St4rk has also shown a tower rush, which uses the starting stone and the population that towers give.

The Settlement garrison is your safety net in every opening. Place Settlements next to wood, gold and berries, and pull villagers inside when raiders show up.

## Castle Age plan

With Blackwood Archers, research Fletching and Bodkin Arrow and keep the Castle producing. Mass them before you fight; trickling them in pairs gets them killed. Add Mangonels when the opponent answers with Elite Skirmishers, and a few Ibirapema Warriors or Pikemen against Knights. Take a second and third Town Center once the map is under control.

With an infantry plan, mix Champi Warriors and Ibirapemas, research Caciques for 25% faster Champi and Slinger attacks, and get Squires early. Slingers handle enemy infantry and Monks.

## Imperial Age

Bracer, Curare and Elite Blackwood Archer turn the archers into a late game army. Arbalesters get extra poison damage from Curare too, and Tupi Town Centers and Keeps become very dangerous once it is researched. Add Trebuchets and Siege Rams for sieges, Halberdiers against cavalry, and Elite Ibirapemas or Elite Champi Warriors as a frontline. The 15% refund keeps production running in long fights.

## Matchups

- Elite Skirmishers, Mangonels and Scorpions beat Blackwood Archers. Switch to Champi Warriors and Ibirapemas, or bring Mangonels of your own.
- Knight and Paladin civilizations threaten both Blackwood Archers and Champi units. Make Pikemen and Ibirapemas, and keep archers behind them.
- Infantry unique units such as Jaguar Warriors, Teutonic Knights and Samurai beat Ibirapemas in melee. Shoot them with archers instead.
- On water, Tupi are average and lack Shipwright, so try to win the land game.

## Common mistakes

- Sending Blackwood Archers into fights in small numbers.
- Forgetting to hide villagers in Settlements during raids.
- Skipping Curare. It is expensive but makes every archer and defensive building better.
- Leaving the starting stone unused. The extra 25 makes an early tower or a faster Castle easier.
- Making a Castle without a plan for Skirmishers. Have Mangonels or infantry ready.

title: How to Play the Turks
summary: The Turks mine gold faster, get Chemistry for free and field the toughest gunpowder units in the game, plus free Light Cavalry and Hussar upgrades. How to open, how to time the Imperial Age and how to avoid running out of gold.
body:
The Turks are the gunpowder civilization. Their gunpowder units have 25% more HP and train 25% faster, Chemistry is free, and their gold miners work 25% faster. They also get free Light Cavalry and Hussar upgrades and Scout Cavalry with +1 pierce armor. Their power grows with each age, and their main limit is gold: a Turk army is expensive and their trash units are poor.

## What the Turks are good at

The gold mining bonus is the engine. Gold miners work 25% faster, so every unit and technology that needs gold arrives sooner. That includes the Feudal and Castle Age age ups, which is why Turks can reach the Imperial Age quickly.

Gunpowder units have 25% more HP, and the team bonus makes them train 25% faster, which applies to you as well. Free Chemistry means you can train Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons the moment you reach the Imperial Age. The Janissary, the Turk unique unit, is a stronger Hand Cannoneer with more range that costs 60 food and 55 gold. Artillery gives Bombard Towers, Bombard Cannons and Cannon Galleons +2 range, and the Bombard Tower technology costs half.

The cavalry is strong. Light Cavalry and Hussar upgrades are free, and the Scout Cavalry line has +1 pierce armor, so Turkish scouts and Hussars handle archers better than most. Sipahi gives mounted archers +20 HP, which makes Turkish Heavy Cavalry Archers some of the best in the game. Knights, Camel Riders and Champions are all available.

The weaknesses are clear. The Turks have no Pikeman or Halberdier upgrade, no Elite Skirmisher and no Arbalester, so their trash units are Spearmen, Skirmishers and the Hussar. There is no Onager, Siege Onager or Paladin. The economy lacks Crop Rotation, Stone Shaft Mining and any bonus outside gold mining, and Monks lack Block Printing and Illumination.

## Openings that suit them

- Turks Scouts (civ-turks-scouts) is the most common ladder start; Scout Cavalry is the unit Turk players make most. The extra pierce armor makes the scouts much safer against archers than other civilizations' scouts.
- Turks Fast Imperial (civ-turks-fast-imperial) is the classic closed map plan. With free Chemistry and the gold bonus you reach the Imperial Age around 19 to 20 minutes and push with Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons.
- A fast castle into Light Cavalry and Scorpions or into Knights is a middle ground for players who want a faster Castle Age without going all in.

## Castle Age plans

The Turk Castle Age is about cavalry. Knights and Camel Riders handle the front line, and the free Light Cavalry upgrade gives you cheap raiders with extra pierce armor. Cavalry archers with Sipahi are strong if you can afford the gold. Crossbowmen work, but remember you will never get Arbalester.

Without Pikemen, Knights are your main answer to Knights, alongside Camel Riders and Monks. Without Elite Skirmishers, massed archers are best handled with Light Cavalry and Mangonels. Janissaries need a Castle and a lot of gold, so most players add them later.

Plan your Imperial Age. Two or three Town Centers in the Castle Age are normal, and you should take a second and third gold mine before the first one runs out.

## Imperial Age

The early Imperial Age is the Turks' strongest point. Hussars are free and are your cheapest good unit. The main army can be Heavy Cavalry Archers with Sipahi, Elite Janissaries or Hand Cannoneers, with Bombard Cannons and Artillery behind them. Bombard Towers with +2 range hold contested gold mines and chokepoints very well. Cavaliers, Heavy Camel Riders and Champions are good additions while gold lasts.

When the gold runs out the Turks fall off fast. Their trash army is Hussars, Spearmen and Skirmishers without the last upgrades. In team games, trade fixes that problem; in 1v1, try to end the game before the gold is gone.

## Matchups

On AoE2Insights the Turks' worst ladder matchups are Gurjaras, Khitans and Cumans. All three have strong cavalry or camels and fast economies, which punish the Turks' slow start and their lack of Halberdiers. Against them, use Camel Riders, Monks and Janissaries, and avoid long trash wars.

Archer civilizations are a fair matchup thanks to the Scout Cavalry armor, since Turkish scouts and Hussars take little damage from arrows. Gunpowder needs protection from Onagers and Mangonels; send Hussars or Light Cavalry at the siege.

The Turks' best matchups include the Portuguese, Muisca and Bohemians.

## Common mistakes

- Running out of gold. Take new mines early and protect them with Bombard Towers.
- Fast Imperial on an open map. Without walls, a Feudal or Castle Age rush catches you with almost no army.
- Making Spearmen late in the game. Without Pikeman they do little; use Camel Riders, Monks or Janissaries against Knights.
- Forgetting the free upgrades. Light Cavalry and Hussar cost you nothing, so they are often your best gold-free unit.
- Sitting back. The Turk economy is weak outside gold, so use the early Imperial power spike.

title: How to Play the Varangians
summary: The Varangians earn gold from sheep, hunt and fish, and their Bloodlines gives 30 extra hit points. Open with tanky Scout Cavalry or Knights, then build up to Cavaliers with trample damage and Varangian Guards that pay for themselves.
body:
## What the Varangians are good at

The Varangians came with The Viking Sagas as a cavalry and naval civilization, and their bonuses are easy to use. Shepherds, hunters and fishermen drop off 10% extra gold on top of their food, and Fishing Ships generate 5% extra gold. On a land map that adds up to roughly 150 to 190 gold by the time the sheep and hunt are gone, which pays for Loom, Bloodlines and part of the Castle Age without a single gold miner. On water maps the fish keep paying gold all game.

Bloodlines and Caravan are 50% stronger. Bloodlines normally gives mounted units 20 hit points, so for the Varangians it is 30: a Scout Cavalry with Bloodlines has 75 hit points in the Feudal Age and a Knight has 130. Varangian Guards, the regional heavy infantry from the Barracks, attack 25% faster and earn 50% more gold while fighting units, and Longships and Catapult Galleons fire 15% faster. The team bonus gives the Knight line 1 extra attack against infantry.

The unique unit is the Jarl, a Castle unit for 75 food and 55 gold that throws axes from short range. Its attack counts as melee damage, it has bonus damage against infantry and it can hit and pull back like a Mameluke, so it is good against infantry, archers and siege that have low melee armor. Vendel Legacy (Castle Age, 500 food and 300 gold) gives the Knight line 5 trample damage around each target, and Gothikon (Imperial Age) lets Varangian Guards throw axes at range 3 every so often.

The gaps: no Paladin, no Champion, no Arbalester, no Thumb Ring, no Cavalry Archer (the Mounted Crossbowman takes its place), no camels, no gunpowder, no Siege Onager and no Gold Shaft Mining. Defenses lack the Keep, Hoardings and Arrowslits, and the Monastery is weak, with no Heresy, Redemption or Sanctity.

The win condition is cavalry pressure backed by an economy that needs less gold mining early. Early ladder numbers showed low rated players doing better with them than high rated players, which fits a civilization whose strengths are tanky units and simple bonuses.

## Openings that suit them

Two Varangian builds are on this site. Varangians Bloodlines Scouts takes the free hunt gold into Bloodlines early in the Feudal Age, which most opponents cannot match; it works on maps with chickens and does not need deer pushing. Varangians Fast Castle Knights uses the same gold to reach the Castle Age quickly with 130 hit point Knights. On hybrid maps such as Four Lakes, fishing early is very strong because every Fishing Ship also brings gold.

## Castle Age plan

Knights are the core. Research Bloodlines first if you have not, then Husbandry and the Blacksmith armor. Vendel Legacy turns the Knights into a strong answer to clumped Archers, Skirmishers and Spearmen, since each hit also damages units around the target. Raid with the group, add Town Centers behind it, and use the Caravan bonus if you play team games with trade.

Varangian Guards become strong in the middle of the Castle Age. They beat most infantry and trade well in long fights, and the gold they earn while fighting softens their cost. Jarls are a good add-on against infantry-heavy armies and for picking off Archers, but they work best next to other units rather than on their own.

## Imperial Age

Cavaliers with Vendel Legacy, Hussars with 30 extra hit points, and Elite Varangian Guards with Gothikon make a full army. Halberdiers and Elite Skirmishers are available and fully upgradable, so your trash army is complete. Add Siege Rams and Trebuchets for buildings. Because Gold Shaft Mining is missing, plan to lean on Hussars and trash units earlier than a normal civilization, or use trade in team games where Caravan makes it better.

## Matchups

- Camel civilizations and Halberdier masses beat the Knight plan. Switch to Varangian Guards, Jarls and Skirmishers to clear the pikes, then bring the Knights back.
- Monk-heavy opponents convert Knights easily because you lack Heresy. Hussars and Light Cavalry kill Monks.
- Strong archer civilizations such as the Britons outrange your late army, and you have no Arbalester. Fight them with Knights, Hussars and Siege Rams, not with your own archers.
- Turks and other gunpowder civilizations hurt Varangian Guards with Hand Cannoneers; keep the Guards for fights against melee units.
- On water maps you have a full Dock plus Longships and faster Catapult Galleons, so take the water fight.

## Common mistakes

- Sending villagers to gold in the Dark Age out of habit. The hunt gold already covers Loom and Bloodlines in most games.
- Delaying Bloodlines. It is the strongest Varangian bonus in the Feudal Age, so research it as soon as you have a few scouts.
- Massing Archers or Mounted Crossbowmen in the late game without Thumb Ring or Arbalester.
- Sending Varangian Guards to attack buildings. They earn gold only from fighting units and lack the Militia line's bonus against buildings.
- Using Jarls alone against cavalry or camels, which beat them in melee.

title: How to Play the Vietnamese
summary: Vietnamese foot archers and Skirmishers have 20 percent more hit points, economy upgrades cost no wood and you see the enemy Town Center from the start. This guide covers the archer opening, the Castle and Imperial army and how to handle cavalry.
body:
The Vietnamese are an archer civilization with tough foot archers, a free scouting bonus and a cheap economy. They are one of the easier civilizations to learn because the plan rarely changes: make archers, keep them alive, and add the right support units as the game goes on.

## What the Vietnamese are good at

Foot archers and Skirmishers have 20 percent more hit points. An Archer with 36 hit points survives one more arrow than a normal one, which wins archer duels, and it holds up better against Mangonel shots and Scout Cavalry. This bonus covers the Archer line, the Rattan Archer and the Skirmisher line.

Economic technologies other than Coinage and Banking cost no wood and research twice as fast. Double-Bit Axe, Horse Collar, Wheelbarrow, Gold Mining and the rest cost food only, which saves several hundred wood across the Feudal and Castle Age. That wood goes into Archery Ranges, Farms and Town Centers. You also see where every enemy Town Center started at the beginning of the game, so your scout can spend its time on sheep and deer, and you know right away how far away the opponent is. Conscription is free in the Imperial Age.

The unique unit is the Rattan Archer, a fast foot archer with very high pierce armor that wins against other archers, towers and Scorpions. Your team bonus unlocks the Imperial Skirmisher, a stronger Elite Skirmisher, for you and your allies. Chatras gives Battle Elephants +100 hit points, and Paper Money in the Imperial Age makes your lumberjacks generate gold as they work, which helps when the mines run out. Fire Lancers are available at the Barracks as a wood and gold answer to cavalry.

## Weak spots in the tech tree

The Vietnamese have no Hussar and no Paladin, and their infantry and cavalry miss Blast Furnace, with infantry also missing Gambesons. There is no Hand Cannoneer, no Siege Ram, no Siege Onager and no Heavy Scorpion, so your siege is the Bombard Cannon and the Capped Ram. Gold Shaft Mining is missing, Architecture is missing, and the Monastery lacks Fervor, Redemption and Heresy. Your answer to most problems comes from the Archery Range or from Battle Elephants.

## Openings that suit them

- Archers, written up as "Vietnamese Archers (21 pop)". The free wood on economic technologies makes two Archery Ranges easy, and your archers win the first fights against other archers.
- Men-at-Arms into Archers. A few Men-at-Arms stop the enemy walls and pull Skirmishers away from your archers.
- Scouts, when you see that your opponent is going Skirmishers. Because you know where they are from the start, it is easy to spot their buildings early.
- Fast Castle on closed maps, using the saved wood for the Feudal buildings.

## Castle Age plan

Crossbowmen and Elite Skirmishers are the backbone. Get Bodkin Arrow and Thumb Ring early, and add a Siege Workshop for Mangonels when your opponent masses infantry or archers. Against Knights, add Pikemen or Fire Lancers in front, or a Castle and Battle Elephants with Chatras, which have so many hit points that they hold the line for your archers. Rattan Archers are expensive but strong against enemy archers and towers. Knights and Cavalry Archers are usable thanks to Bloodlines and Husbandry, but treat them as support.

A Castle also unlocks Chatras and later Paper Money, so build one in the middle of your base when you can. Your economy upgrades cost no wood, so research them as soon as you have the food.

## Imperial Age plan

The late army is Arbalesters or Elite Rattan Archers with Halberdiers or Elite Battle Elephants in front and Bombard Cannons behind. When gold runs low, Imperial Skirmishers and Halberdiers carry the trash war, and Paper Money keeps a trickle of gold coming in from your lumberjacks. Without Siege Onagers, use Bombard Cannons and Battle Elephants to break buildings, and Trebuchets for Castles.

## Matchups

- Cavalry heavy civilizations such as the Franks, Lithuanians or Persians are the main danger once they have Paladins. Use Halberdiers, Fire Lancers, Battle Elephants and Monks in front, and keep the archers behind.
- Other archer civilizations such as the Britons, Ethiopians or Maya meet your toughest units. Rattan Archers, Imperial Skirmishers and the extra hit points let you win these duels.
- Siege and infantry civilizations such as the Goths or Celts push into your archers; Mangonels and Bombard Cannons are your answer, along with Elite Skirmishers against their archers.
- Cavalry archer civilizations kite your foot army. Mass Elite Skirmishers and Imperial Skirmishers, and use Castles to hold ground.

## Common mistakes

- Spending the first minutes scouting for the enemy. You already know where they are; use the scout on sheep and deer.
- Forgetting to research economy upgrades early. They cost no wood and finish twice as fast, so there is no reason to wait.
- Making Light Cavalry as a late game raider. Without the Hussar it falls off; use Battle Elephants or archers instead.
- Fighting Paladins without a front line. Archers with extra hit points still lose to heavy cavalry that reaches them.
- Forgetting Paper Money in long games. It turns your woodcutters into a second source of gold.

title: How to Play the Vikings
summary: Vikings get Wheelbarrow and Hand Cart for free, tough infantry and cheap warships. The Viking Sagas rebuilt their army around the Varangian Guard, so this guide covers the updated plan on land and water, from the Fast Castle boom to the late game infantry and siege push.
body:
The Vikings are an infantry and naval civilization with one of the strongest economies from the Feudal Age to the early Imperial Age. The Viking Sagas changed them a lot in September 2026: they lost the Cavalry Archer, Gambesons and the Cannon Galleon, Chieftains no longer gives gold, and they gained the Varangian Guard, the Mounted Crossbowman and the Catapult Galleon. The Longboat is now the Longship, a regional unit shared with the other northern civilizations.

## What the Vikings are good at

- Wheelbarrow and Hand Cart are free, granted when you reach the Feudal and Castle Ages. That saves 475 food and 250 wood plus the research time, which is worth several villagers of production.
- Infantry have 20% more hit points from the Feudal Age on.
- Warships cost 10% less in the Feudal Age, 15% in the Castle Age and 20% in the Imperial Age, and Docks cost 15% less (the team bonus).

The Berserk is the Castle unique unit, an infantry unit that heals itself over time. Chieftains, the Castle Age unique technology, gives infantry +5 attack against cavalry and +4 against camels, which covers the missing Halberdier. Bogsveigar in the Imperial Age gives the Archer line and Longships +1 attack.

The new regional infantry, the Varangian Guard, comes from the Barracks in the Castle Age (65 food, 45 gold). It has 13 attack, decent armor and generates gold while it fights enemy units. With the Viking hit point bonus and Chieftains it is a strong all round unit that comes straight out of a Barracks, so a Viking Castle Age army no longer needs a Castle to have a good main unit.

Missing pieces: no Halberdier, Hussar, Paladin, Thumb Ring, Bloodlines, Husbandry, Siege Onager, Bombard Cannon or Hand Cannoneer. Cavalry is a Feudal raiding tool only. Monks lack Redemption, Sanctity and Theocracy, so siege is hard to answer without your own rams, Mangonels and infantry.

The win condition: use the free economy upgrades to get ahead in the Feudal and Castle Ages, then push with tough infantry, Varangian Guards and rams, or with archers and Longships on water.

## Openings that suit the Vikings

- Vikings Fast Castle Boom: the free Wheelbarrow makes the Feudal Age short and cheap, and the free Hand Cart arrives with the Castle Age. A good first build for new players.
- Vikings Men-at-Arms into Varangian Guards: the approach TheViper used after the update. Men-at-Arms with extra hit points pressure early, then a quick Castle Age brings Varangian Guards from the same Barracks.

Archers are still good on open maps; Viking archers lack Thumb Ring but the economy keeps two or three ranges producing. On water maps go Docks early, since your Galleys and Fire Galleys are cheaper than anyone's.

## Castle Age plan

On land, the main army is Varangian Guards or Long Swordsmen with Chieftains in front of Crossbowmen or Skirmishers. Add a Siege Workshop for Battering Rams; infantry and rams together break walls and Town Centers quickly. Boom with two extra Town Centers once your army holds the map, because your free Hand Cart makes every villager gather faster.

Berserks from a Castle are an option against other infantry and in long fights where their healing matters. Mounted Crossbowmen are available but without Bloodlines, Husbandry and Thumb Ring they are not worth a big investment.

On water, mass Galleys and Fire Galleys in the Feudal Age, then Longships in the Castle Age. They move fast and fire several arrows, and they are cheap for you.

## Imperial Age plan

Champions or Elite Varangian Guards, Elite Berserks, Arbalesters with Bogsveigar and Siege Rams make a solid late game. Use Heavy Scorpions or Onagers against archer masses and Trebuchets against Castles. Your Champions with Chieftains beat most cavalry, which fills the gap left by the missing Halberdier.

## Matchups and what gives the Vikings trouble

- Siege heavy civilizations. Bombard Cannons and Siege Onagers hurt infantry and you have weak answers without Redemption or Bombard Cannons of your own. Send infantry or rams at the siege early, or use Scorpions and Trebuchets.
- Mounted archer civilizations. Cavalry Archers and Mounted Crossbowmen kite infantry. Use Skirmishers and Arbalesters, and force fights near your buildings.
- Hand Cannoneers beat Varangian Guards and Berserks; answer them with archers, Mangonels and Skirmishers.
- Cataphracts and some unique cavalry such as the Boyar and Leitis beat Varangian Guards.
- Champion civilizations beat Varangian Guards, which count as shock infantry. Use Long Swordsmen and Champions of your own against them.

## Common mistakes with the Vikings

- Researching Wheelbarrow or Hand Cart by habit. They are free; spend that time on farms or Bow Saw.
- Making cavalry beyond a few Feudal scouts. Viking Stables have no upgrades to back them up.
- Floating resources while booming. The economy is strong, so add production buildings early.
- Sending infantry across open ground into archers without rams or Mangonels.
- Playing a slow game on land against siege civilizations instead of using the Castle Age lead.

title: How to Play the Wei
summary: Wei survive a weak start, then boom faster than almost anyone thanks to a free villager for every economy upgrade. This guide covers the Fast Castle boom, when to make Tiger Cavalry, Xianbei Raiders or Hei Guang Cavalry, and how to handle the civilizations that beat Wei most often.
body:
The Wei are the cavalry civilization of The Three Kingdoms expansion. They have a weak start, with no bonus in the Dark Age and a poor scout opening, and then one of the strongest villager booms in the game from the Feudal Age on. Their Castle Age has two good unique units, the Tiger Cavalry and the Xianbei Raider, so the usual plan is to survive the early game, boom hard and win with cavalry and mounted archers.

## What the Wei are good at

- You receive a free villager every time you finish an economic technology. In the Feudal Age that is up to six: Double-Bit Axe, Horse Collar, Gold Mining, Stone Mining, Wheelbarrow and Gillnets on water. Spirit of the Law counts 12 free villagers on a land map if you take every economy upgrade, and 14 on water.
- Hei Guang Cavalry and Xianbei Raiders get 20% more hit points in the Castle Age and 30% more in the Imperial Age.
- Traction Trebuchets and Lou Chuans cost 25% less.
- Your cavalry deals +2 damage to siege weapons, and so does your team's.
- Tuntian makes your infantry, archers and cavalry produce food while they exist, 1.8 food per minute each.
- Ming Guang Armor gives mounted units +4 melee armor.

The Hei Guang Cavalry is the Three Kingdoms version of the Knight. It has less health than a Knight and more armor, so it is strong against melee units and weak against Pikemen, Camel Riders and other units with bonus damage. The Tiger Cavalry is the anti-archer unit: it has extra pierce armor, bonus damage against archers, and gains hit points and attack for each enemy it kills, up to four kills. The Xianbei Raider replaces the Cavalry Archer. It costs 65 wood and 35 gold and fires a charged volley of five extra arrows every 30 seconds that is very strong against Spearmen and other infantry.

## Openings that suit them

The Wei Fast Castle Boom build on this site is the default. You play a normal 27 villager Dark Age, then research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar in Feudal, which pay you two villagers back, and click up. In the Castle Age you add Town Centers and every economy upgrade, each of which adds another villager.

On open maps you need to stay safe on the way. Wall the woodlines, and if you scout a fast Feudal rush, build an Archery Range for Skirmishers or a Barracks for Spearmen and keep the economy techs going; the free villagers replace losses. Scout and archer openings are possible, but Spirit of the Law rates the Wei scout opening as mediocre, so most players avoid a Feudal war.

## Castle Age plan

The free villagers make a three Town Center boom very strong. Research Wheelbarrow, Bow Saw, Heavy Plow, Gold Shaft Mining and Hand Cart as soon as you can; each of them gives a villager on top of its normal effect.

Pick your army from what the opponent makes.

- Against archers, Tiger Cavalry from the Castle. They are expensive but they shrug off arrows and get stronger with every kill.
- Against infantry and Spearmen, Xianbei Raiders. They are cheap on gold and their volley wrecks spear units, which is what most players build to stop cavalry.
- Against melee armies and siege, Hei Guang Cavalry with the Wei hit point bonus and the team bonus against siege.

Ladder data shows Xianbei Raiders are the most produced Wei unit, followed by Scout Cavalry and Hei Guang Cavalry, which matches this plan. Tuntian is worth it once you have a standing army of 25 or more units.

## Imperial Age plan

In the Imperial Age, Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry with Ming Guang Armor and the 30% hit point bonus can beat generic Paladins, and Xianbei Raiders get their full bonus. A typical late army is Hei Guang or Tiger Cavalry in front with a large group of Xianbei Raiders behind, plus Traction Trebuchets for buildings. Hussars and Halberdiers are available and help as gold free units.

Wei have no Arbalester, Plate Barding Armor, Hand Cannoneer or Bombard Cannon. Their foot archers stop at Crossbowman, so the Xianbei Raider does the job of the archer line.

## Matchups

Ladder statistics show the hardest matchups for the Wei are Goths, Hindustanis, Spanish, Cumans, Italians and Wu.

- Against cheap infantry floods (Goths), use Xianbei Raiders in large numbers with Tuntian, and keep Hei Guang Cavalry to clean up. Avoid fighting under Goth towers or Castles.
- Against Camel Riders (Hindustanis), switch from Hei Guang to Xianbei Raiders and Halberdiers. Tiger Cavalry are good against the Hindustani gunpowder but lose to camels.
- Against the Spanish, Tiger Cavalry with their high pierce armor take Conquistador shots well, while Halberdiers handle the Paladins.
- Against early aggression (Cumans), wall and defend with Spearmen and Skirmishers. The economy techs keep giving you villagers back while you hold.
- Against Genoese Crossbowmen (Italians), Tiger Cavalry win if they reach the crossbows before a big group forms. Bring Siege Rams against a large mass.

## Common mistakes

- Taking a Feudal fight you do not need. The Wei have no early bonuses, and their power comes once the economy techs pile up.
- Delaying economy upgrades. Each one is a free villager, so research them as soon as you can afford them.
- Using Hei Guang Cavalry like Knights against Pikemen. Their low hit points make them lose those fights badly.
- Making Tiger Cavalry against Spearmen. They are anti-archer specialists; Xianbei Raiders do that job far better.
- Forgetting the Wei siege options. Traction Trebuchets are cheap and give you a long range way to break Castles without Bombard Cannons.
