title: How to Play the Wu
summary: Military buildings that pay you food, regenerating infantry, the Jian Swordsman and a strong navy. How to use the Wu bonuses in each age, when to make Jian Swordsmen and Fire Archers, and what to do about the weak siege.
body:
The Wu are an infantry and navy civilization from The Three Kingdoms with a wide tech tree. Barracks, Archery Ranges, Stables, Siege Workshops, Castles and Docks each give 55 food when they finish. Infantry regenerate 10, 15 and 30 hit points per minute in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Ages. Jian Swordsmen and Hei Guang Cavalry gain +2 attack in the Imperial Age, and Careening and Dry Dock are free. Their team bonus, which also works for the Wu themselves, makes Houses build twice as fast.

## What the Wu are good at

The food bonus rewards building military. A Dark Age Barracks pays back 55 food, enough for most of a Militia, a two Stable scout opening gets back more than one Scout Cavalry, and every Dock you build for a water fight gives you food for the next Fishing Ships. Fast Houses mean one villager can build both starting Houses while the other two go straight to the sheep, and later you can wall with Houses without losing much villager time.

Regeneration makes infantry raids cheap. Men-at-Arms that retreat after a fight are back to full health a few minutes later, and in the Imperial Age 30 hit points a minute keeps a Champion or Halberdier line fresh between fights.

The Jian Swordsman, trained at the Barracks from the Castle Age, is the unit the Wu are known for. It fights behind a shield with 5 pierce armor and bonus damage against archers. Once it drops below 45 hit points it throws the shield away, moving and hitting faster but losing armor. Wu regeneration heals it back over that line, and the shield returns. A group of Jian Swordsmen walks through Crossbowman fire and kills the archers at the end of it.

The Fire Archer, the Castle unique unit, switches attack mode by target. Against buildings and ships it fires one long range shot that outranges Castles and towers. Against units it fires three short range arrows with a small blast. Use it mainly against buildings and ships. Red Cliffs Tactics adds burning damage for Fire Archers and Demolition Ships against ships and buildings.

The Wu replace the Knight line with the Hei Guang Cavalry, a heavily armored horseman with low hit points. In the Imperial Age they get Traction Trebuchets, which fire without packing up, the Lou Chuan tower ship, and Sun Jian, a cavalry hero who makes nearby units move faster.

The gaps: no gunpowder at all, no Thumb Ring, Parthian Tactics or Ring Archer Armor, no Capped Ram, no Siege Onager, no Siege Engineers, no Fortified Wall and no Heresy.

## Openings

- Wu Men-at-Arms into Archers (25 pop) uses the Dark Age Barracks food and Feudal regeneration for a Men-at-Arms opening that flows into an Archery Range.
- Wu Fast Castle into Jian Swordsmen (27+2) is the Castle Age power play that Hera has shown in several videos. It picks Feudal buildings that give food and hits archer civilizations with Jian Swordsmen from three Barracks.

Scout Cavalry openings also suit the Wu, since each Stable gives food back. On hybrid and water maps, the Dock food and the free Careening make an early Dock and a Fire Galley or Galley opening very strong, and Hera has a video on the Wu on hybrid maps.

## Castle Age plan

Your army depends on the opponent. Against archers, mass Jian Swordsmen with Blacksmith infantry armor and keep a few Pikemen with them. Against cavalry, Pikemen and Halberdiers with regeneration hold the line, and Hei Guang Cavalry deal with Skirmishers and siege. Long Swordsmen are good against enemy infantry and cost less gold. Fire Archers are your answer to towers, Castles and enemy ships; take them along when you push a base, since your Siege Workshop is weak.

Build every production building you need early. Each Barracks, Stable, Archery Range and Siege Workshop pays 55 food, so a three Barracks Jian push is cheaper than it looks.

## Imperial Age

Champions and Halberdiers with 30 hit points of regeneration a minute, Jian Swordsmen and Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry with their extra attack, and Traction Trebuchets for buildings make the core of the late army. Sitting Tiger adds projectiles to Traction Trebuchets and the Lou Chuan. Arbalesters work as support, but without Thumb Ring and the last archer armor they will not carry a fight against a real archer civilization. When gold runs out, Halberdiers, Hussars and Elite Skirmishers are all available.

Traction Trebuchets can be converted by Monks from a distance, so keep units near them and kill enemy Monks first.

## On water

Free Careening and Dry Dock mean every Wu ship gets the extra armor and speed without the research cost, and Docks give food. Red Cliffs Tactics makes Demolition Ships deadly against massed ships, and the Lou Chuan is an Imperial Age ship that destroys buildings and siege from long range. The Wu lack Shipwright, so their ships cost full wood.

## Matchups

- Strong cavalry civilizations such as the Franks, Lithuanians or Persians are hard for an infantry army. Keep Halberdiers in front, and avoid sending Jian Swordsmen against Knights.
- Gunpowder and Onager civilizations punish massed infantry. Spread out, raid with Hei Guang Cavalry or Hussars, and kill their siege before you fight.
- Strong infantry civilizations like the Japanese, Vikings or Goths beat Jian Swordsmen in melee. Use Long Swordsmen or Champions instead, and Fire Archers behind them.
- Archer civilizations such as the Britons, Ethiopians or Maya are where the Jian Swordsman rush shines.
- Cavalry Archer civilizations are slippery because your archers lack Thumb Ring. Use Skirmishers, Hei Guang Cavalry and Houses or walls to force fights.

## Common mistakes

- Using all three starting villagers on Houses. One is enough for the Wu.
- Picking a Market as a Feudal building when an Archery Range or Stable would give 55 food back.
- Sending Jian Swordsmen into cavalry or heavy infantry.
- Using Fire Archers as the main anti unit force. They are for buildings and ships.
- Relying on walls. Without Fortified Wall, a strong push breaks Wu walls easily.
